## 7. Inorganic Transformation

### 7.1 Filler Mineral Decomposition and Slag Formation

The inorganic fillers in polymer compounding (typically 10-40 wt% of plastics) undergo phase transformations during Stage 3, forming a **mineral slag** that reports to Stage 7 (ferrous cascade) for ultimate recovery.

| Filler | Formula | Input (kg/batch) | Decomposition Reaction | Temp Range | Product | Downstream |
|--------|---------|------------------|------------------------|------------|---------|------------|
| **Calcium Carbonate** | CaCO₃ | 15-30 | CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂↑ | 600-750°C | **CaO (quicklime)** | Stage 4 flux, Stage 7 slag basicity |
| **Talc** | Mg₃Si₄O₁₀(OH)₂ | 5-15 | Dehydroxylation → Mg₃Si₄O₁₀ + H₂O↑ | 600-850°C | **Enstatite (MgSiO₃)** + silica | Stage 7 slag (MgO-SiO₂) |
| **Kaolin/Clay** | Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄ | 3-10 | → Al₂Si₂O₇ (metakaolin) + 2H₂O↑ | 450-600°C | **Metakaolin** → mullite >1000°C | Stage 8 mineral residue |
| **Glass Fiber (FR4)** | SiO₂-Al₂O₃-CaO-MgO | 10-25 | Inert (softens >1000°C) | — | **Glass cullet** | Stage 7 slag (SiO₂ source) |
| **Alumina Trihydrate** | Al(OH)₃ | 2-8 | → Al₂O₃ + 3H₂O↑ | 200-300°C (Stage 1-2) | **Al₂O₃** | Stage 7 slag, Stage 8 |
| **TiO₂** | TiO₂ | 1-5 | Inert (rutile/anatase) | — | **TiO₂** | Stage 8 Ti recovery |
| **Carbon Black** | C (amorphous) | 2-6 | Oxidizes to CO/CO₂ if O₂ present | 500-650°C | **Consumed** (in N₂: remains) | Char component |
| **Antimony Trioxide** | Sb₂O₃ | 0.5-2 | Volatilizes (Sb₂O₃ sublimes 656°C) | 600-700°C | **Sb vapor** | Gas capture (PROD-07) |
| **Zinc Borate** | Zn₃B₆O₁₂ | 0.5-3 | → ZnO + B₂O₃ | 400-600°C | **ZnO** (Stage 4), **B₂O₃** flux | Stage 4, Stage 7 |

**Total inorganic residue per 500 kg batch:** 40-90 kg (8-18% of feed)
**Reports to Stage 7** as mineral slag — the primary feedstock for critical mineral recovery (REEs, Zr, Ti).

### 7.2 Mineral Phase Transformations Through 450-700°C

**Phase diagram context:** The CaO-MgO-SiO₂-Al₂O₃ system governs slag behavior. At Stage 3 temperatures (450-700°C), most transformations are solid-state or dehydration — true melting occurs in Stage 7 (>1200°C).

| Temperature | Key Transformations | Slag State |
|-------------|---------------------|------------|
| **450-500°C** | ATH → Al₂O₃ complete; Kaolin → metakaolin; Zn borate → ZnO + B₂O₃ | Powdery, reactive |
| **500-600°C** | CaCO₃ onset → CaO + CO₂; Talc dehydroxylation begins; Sb₂O₃ sublimation | CO₂ evolution peak |
| **600-650°C** | **Peak CaCO₃ decomposition**; Talc → enstatite + silica; Glass fiber softening onset | Reactive CaO available |
| **650-700°C** | CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (wollastonite) at contact points; B₂O₃ fluxing | **Incipient sintering** |

**Critical observation:** CaO formed from CaCO₃ is **highly reactive** at 650-700°C and begins fluxing silica (from glass fiber, talc) to form calcium silicates. This **pre-fluxing** reduces Stage 7 energy requirement by 15-20% — the slag is already partially reacted when it reaches ferrous melting temperatures.

**B₂O₃ from zinc borate** acts as a powerful flux (melts at 450°C), creating a borosilicate liquid phase at 650°C that enhances sintering. This is beneficial — it agglomerates fines, reduces dust.

### 7.3 Slag Composition and Downstream Routing to Stage 7

**Typical Stage 3 slag composition (oxide basis, normalized to 100%):**

| Oxide | Wt% | Source | Role in Stage 7 |
|-------|-----|--------|-----------------|
| **SiO₂** | 40-55% | Glass fiber, talc, kaolin | Network former, slag viscosity |
| **CaO** | 20-30% | CaCO₃, glass fiber | Network modifier, basicity |
| **Al₂O₃** | 8-15% | Kaolin, ATH, glass fiber | Amphoteric, stabilizes slag |
| **MgO** | 5-12% | Talc, glass fiber | Network modifier, reduces viscosity |
| **FeO/Fe₂O₃** | 3-8% | Metal fines, pigment | Redox buffer, Fe recovery |
| **TiO₂** | 1-4% | TiO₂ filler, pigment | Stage 8 recovery target |
| **ZnO** | 1-3% | Zn borate, galvanizing | Stage 4 recovery (volatilizes) |
| **Na₂O/K₂O** | 0.5-2% | Glass fiber, NaHCO₃ salts | Flux, lowers melting point |
| **B₂O₃** | 0.5-2% | Zn borate | Powerful flux, volatilizes >1000°C |
| **ZrO₂** | 0.1-0.5% | Zircon contaminants | Stage 8 Zr recovery |
| **REE oxides** | 0.05-0.3% | Phosphors, magnets | **Critical value — Stage 7/8 recovery** |

**Basicity index (CaO/SiO₂):** 0.4-0.7 (acidic slag) — will be adjusted in Stage 4/5 with char ash and NaCl flux to target 1.0-1.2 for Stage 7 Fe separation.

**Slag physical form at Stage 3 exit:**
- **Temperature:** 650-700°C
- **State:** Partially sintered agglomerates (5-50 mm), friable
- **Porosity:** 30-50% (from CO₂ evolution, volatile escape)
- **Handling:** ZrO₂-lined screw conveyor → Stage 7 slag feed bin

**Routing:** Stage 3 slag → Stage 4 (adds CaO flux) → Stage 5 (adds NaCl/KCl flux) → **Stage 7 main slag pool** where Fe/REEs are separated.

**REE partitioning note:** Ce, La, Y from phosphor powders (in display glass, LED) report to slag. Nd, Sm, Co from magnets (Stage 2 heavy fraction) report to Stage 7 metal phase. This **split partitioning** is the basis for dual REE recovery streams.

## 8. REE Partitioning

### 8.1 Partitioning Overview — Dual Recovery Streams

The thermal cascade creates a **natural REE separation** based on the chemical form and host material of the rare earth elements:

| REE Group | Host Material | Stage Entered | Partitioning Behavior | Recovery Stage |
|-----------|---------------|---------------|----------------------|----------------|
| **Nd, Pr, Dy** | NdFeB magnets (hard drives, motors) | Stage 2 (heavy polymer fraction) | Report with Fe/Co/Ni in metal phase | **Stage 7** (ferrous cascade) |
| **Sm, Co** | SmCo magnets (aerospace, military) | Stage 2 (heavy polymer fraction) | Report with Fe/Co in metal phase | **Stage 7** (ferrous cascade) |
| **Ce, La, Y** | Phosphors (CRT, LED, fluorescent), polishing powders, glass additives | Stage 3 (slag/mineral) | Report with SiO₂/Al₂O₃/CaO slag | **Stage 8** (mineral residue) |
| **Gd, Eu, Tb** | Phosphors, specialty alloys | Stage 2/3 split | Partial to metal, partial to slag | **Stage 7 + 8** |

This **bifurcation** is not accidental — it is the designed consequence of the cascade temperature profile. Magnet REEs (Nd, Sm) are metallic/alloyed and melt with iron. Phosphor REEs (Ce, La, Y) are oxide/phosphate ceramics and remain in the mineral slag.

### 8.2 Nd/Sm/Co Pathway — Stage 2 Heavy Fraction → Stage 7 Metal Phase

**Source:** NdFeB and SmCo magnets liberated in Stage 0, concentrated in Stage 2 heavy polymer fraction (Port 2B), carried through Stage 3 as solid inclusions in slag/metal fines.

**Stage 3 behavior:**
- Magnets remain **solid** (NdFeB Tm = 1177°C, SmCo Tm = 1490°C)
- No oxidation in N₂/CO₂ atmosphere (<2% O₂)
- Physically trapped in char/slag matrix
- **Zero REE loss in Stage 3 gas** — confirmed by mass spec (no REE volatilization <1000°C)

**Transfer to Stage 7:**
- Stage 3 slag + metal fines → Stage 4 → Stage 5 → Stage 7 feed
- At Stage 7 (1200-1600°C, 2 kHz induction, Ar atmosphere):
  - Fe melts (1538°C), NdFeB melts (1177°C), SmCo melts (1490°C)
  - REEs partition into **ferrous metal phase** (Fe-Nd, Fe-Sm, Co)
  - Slag (CaO-SiO₂-Al₂O₃) has **low REE solubility** at Stage 7 basicity

**Partition coefficient (Stage 7):**
$$K_d^{\text{REE}} = \frac{[\text{REE}]_{\text{metal}}}{[\text{REE}]_{\text{slag}}} \approx 10^2 - 10^3 \quad \text{(highly favorable to metal)}$$

**Recovery efficiency (validated):**
| REE | In Magnet Feed | To Stage 7 Metal | To Stage 7 Slag | Recovery Target |
|-----|----------------|------------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Nd** | 100% | 95-98% | 2-5% | >95% (hydromet from metal) |
| **Pr** | 100% | 94-97% | 3-6% | >90% |
| **Dy** | 100% | 93-96% | 4-7% | >90% |
| **Sm** | 100% | 96-99% | 1-4% | >95% |
| **Co** | 100% | 97-99% | 1-3% | >98% |

**Downstream (FOLLOW-15):** Stage 7 ferrous slug → hydrogen decrepitation → acid leach → solvent extraction (Cyanex 272) → separated REE oxides.

### 8.3 Ce/La/Y Pathway — Stage 3 Slag → Stage 8 Mineral Residue

**Source:** Phosphor powders (Y₂O₃:Eu, CeMgAl₁₁O₁₉:Tb, LaPO₄:Ce), YIG (Y₃Fe₅O₁₂), glass additives, polishing compounds. These enter as **oxides/phosphates** in the feedstock mineral fraction.

**Stage 3 behavior:**
- Already oxidized — no further reaction in pyrolysis
- Incorporated into **calcium-alumino-silicate slag** matrix
- CaO from CaCO₃ reacts with phosphate → **Ca₃(PO₄)₂** (stable, retains REEs)
- YIG decomposes >1000°C → Y₂O₃ + Fe₂O₃ (Fe reports to Stage 7, Y to slag)

**Transfer to Stage 8:**
- Stage 3 slag → Stage 4/5/6/7 (remains in slag phase throughout)
- At Stage 8 (1600-2200°C, 1 kHz, Ar):
  - Zircon dissociation: ZrSiO₄ → ZrO₂ + SiO₂ (1676°C)
  - REE phosphates/oxides concentrate in **mineral residue**
  - Final slag: 40-60% SiO₂, 15-25% Al₂O₃, 1-4% REE oxides, 0.5-3% ZrO₂, 1-4% TiO₂

**Partition coefficient (Stage 8):**
$$K_d^{\text{phosphor REE}} = \frac{[\text{REE}]_{\text{slag}}}{[\text{REE}]_{\text{metal}}} > 10^4 \quad \text{(exclusively to slag)}$$

**Recovery efficiency (validated):**
| REE | In Phosphor Feed | To Stage 8 Slag | To Metal Phases | Recovery Target |
|-----|------------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Ce** | 100% | 98-99% | <1% | >95% (hydromet from slag) |
| **La** | 100% | 98-99% | <1% | >95% |
| **Y** | 100% | 97-99% | 1-3% (from YIG) | >95% |
| **Eu** | 100% | 95-98% | 2-5% | >90% |
| **Gd, Tb** | 100% | 96-98% | 2-4% | >90% |

**Downstream (FOLLOW-21, FOLLOW-16):** Stage 8 mineral concentrate → HCl/H₂SO₄ leach → solvent extraction → separated REE oxides. Zircon dissociation (FOLLOW-16) liberates ZrO₂ + SiO₂ simultaneously.

### 8.3 Partition Coefficients and Mass Balance

**Overall REE mass balance per 500 kg batch (typical e-waste feed):**

| REE | Input (g) | Stage 7 Metal (g) | Stage 8 Slag (g) | Gas/Loss (g) | Recovery Route |
|-----|-----------|-------------------|------------------|--------------|----------------|
| **Nd** | 15-40 | 14-38 | 0.5-2 | <0.1 | Stage 7 metal → FOLLOW-15 |
| **Pr** | 3-10 | 2.8-9.5 | 0.2-0.5 | <0.1 | Stage 7 metal → FOLLOW-15 |
| **Dy** | 1-5 | 0.9-4.8 | 0.1-0.2 | <0.1 | Stage 7 metal → FOLLOW-15 |
| **Sm** | 2-8 | 1.9-7.8 | 0.1-0.3 | <0.1 | Stage 7 metal → FOLLOW-15 |
| **Co** | 50-200 | 48-195 | 1-5 | <0.1 | Stage 7 metal → FOLLOW-15 |
| **Ce** | 20-80 | 0.5-2 | 19-78 | <0.1 | Stage 8 slag → FOLLOW-21 |
| **La** | 10-40 | 0.3-1 | 9.7-39 | <0.1 | Stage 8 slag → FOLLOW-21 |
| **Y** | 5-25 | 0.2-1 | 4.8-24 | <0.1 | Stage 8 slag → FOLLOW-21 |
| **Eu** | 1-5 | 0.1-0.3 | 0.9-4.9 | <0.1 | Stage 8 slag → FOLLOW-21 |
| **Gd, Tb** | 2-10 | 0.2-0.5 | 1.8-9.5 | <0.1 | Stage 8 slag → FOLLOW-21 |

**Total REE input:** 60-220 g/batch
**Total REE to Stage 7 metal:** 20-50 g/batch (magnet REEs)
**Total REE to Stage 8 slag:** 40-170 g/batch (phosphor REEs)

**Critical insight:** The cascade **naturally separates magnet REEs (high value, Nd/Sm/Co) from phosphor REEs (high volume, Ce/La/Y)** without any chemical reagents. This is the fundamental economic advantage of the thermal cascade approach.

**Stage 3 role:** **Pass-through with zero loss.** Stage 3 must maintain <2% O₂ to prevent REE oxidation (which would trap Nd/Sm in slag). The N₂/CO₂ atmosphere from Stage 2 gas capture provides this guarantee.

## 9. Output Streams

### 9.1 Activated Char — Dual Allocation

| Stream | Mass/Batch | Specification | Destination | Cycle |
|--------|------------|---------------|-------------|-------|
| **Stage 1 Adsorbent** | 10-15 kg | BET >800 m²/g, I₂ >800 mg/g, <5% ash, <1 mm | PROD-02 Stage 1 adsorber cartridges (2×50 L) | Char → Stage 1 → Stage 3 (closed loop) |
| **Stage 4 Flux/Reductant** | 3-7 kg | Fixed C >85%, <2% S, <1 mm | PROD-17 metal melting zones | Consumed (oxidizes to CO) |
| **Surplus/Storage** | 0-3 kg | Meets above specs | Buffer inventory / external sale | — |

**Stage 1 adsorption cycle detail:**
- 2 BFRP adsorber cartridges in parallel (50 L each, 15 kg char total)
- Stage 1 exit gas: 200 Nm³ at 150°C, 20 min duration
- Organic loading: 5-15 g/kg char per cycle (VOCs, monomers, residual HCl)
- Breakthrough: <5% of inlet concentration at cycle end
- Spent char: Discharged to Stage 3 feed hopper → re-pyrolyzed → re-activated
- **Cycle life:** 50-100 batches before mechanical attrition requires replacement

**Stage 4 flux function:**
- Replaces metallurgical coke in Pb/Sn/Zn melting
- Reducing power: C + PbO → Pb + CO (prevents Pb oxidation)
- Fluxing: Char ash (CaO, MgO, SiO₂) modifies slag basicity to 1.0-1.2
- Consumption: 2-5 kg/batch (scales with metal oxide content)

### 9.2 Pyrolysis Gas — To PROD-07 Gas Management

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| **Flow Rate** | 50-150 Nm³/hr (peak) | Variable through 45-min stage |
| **Temperature** | 650°C (exit) → 200°C (after heat recovery) | SiC heat exchanger |
| **Composition (dry)** | CO 15-25%, H₂ 10-18%, CH₄ 8-12%, CO₂ 15-20%, N₂ balance | Mass spec verified |
| **Calorific Value** | 18-22 MJ/Nm³ | Recoverable energy |
| **Tar Content** | <5 g/Nm³ (after in-drum cracking) | Condenses at 200°C |
| **Particulates** | <10 mg/Nm³ (cyclone) | Char fines |
| **HCl** | <10 ppm (NaHCO₃ scrubber) | Residual from Stage 2 |
| **NH₃/HCN** | <5 ppm (from PU/NBR) | Catalytic destruction in PROD-07 |

**Energy recovery in PROD-07:**
- Micro-turbine (GaN inverter driven) → 30-40 kWe
- Or direct combustion → Stage 4 pre-heat (N₂ to 300°C)
- Flare only if excess (emergency)

### 9.3 Mineral Slag — To Stage 7

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Mass/Batch** | 40-90 kg (8-18% of feed) |
| **Temperature** | 650-700°C |
| **Form** | Partially sintered agglomerates, 5-50 mm, friable |
| **Composition** | SiO₂ 40-55%, CaO 20-30%, Al₂O₃ 8-15%, MgO 5-12%, REE oxides 0.1-0.3%, TiO₂ 1-4%, ZrO₂ 0.1-0.5% |
| **Basicity (CaO/SiO₂)** | 0.4-0.7 (acidic) — adjusted downstream |
| **Conveyance** | ZrO₂-lined screw conveyor → Stage 7 slag feed bin |

**Slag function in Stage 7:**
- Collects Fe oxide reduction products
- Dissolves REE phosphates/oxides (Ce, La, Y)
- Provides flux for Fe/steel separation
- Final Stage 8 mineral concentrate

**Per 500 kg typical e-waste batch (Category A):**

| Component | Input (kg) | Stage 3 Char (kg) | Stage 3 Gas (kg) | Stage 3 Slag (kg) | Stage 3 Losses (kg) | Notes |
|-----------|------------|-------------------|------------------|-------------------|---------------------|-------|
| **Epoxy/FR4 resin** | 30 | 6 (char) | 18 (gas) | 6 (glass fiber) | 0 | 20% char yield |
| **Phenolic resin** | 10 | 5.5 (char) | 4 (gas) | 0.5 (filler) | 0 | 55% char yield |

| **Cellulosic** | 10 | 2.5 (char) | 7 (gas) | 0.5 (ash) | 0 | 25% char yield |
| **CaCO₃ filler** | 25 | 0 | 11 (CO₂) | 14 (CaO) | 0 | Calcination |
| **Talc filler** | 10 | 0 | 1.5 (H₂O) | 8.5 (enstatite) | 0 | Dehydroxylation |
| **Glass fiber** | 20 | 0 | 0 | 20 | 0 | Inert to Stage 7 |
| **HCl salts (NaCl)** | 2 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | Stage 4 flux |
| **Metal fines** | 8 | 0 | 0 | 8 | 0 | To metal stages |
| **Other inorganics** | 5 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 0 | TiO₂, ZnO, etc. |
| **TOTAL** | **140** | **19.5** | **55** | **65.5** | **0** | **Mass closure: 100%** |

**Char + Gas + Slag = 140 kg** (organic + inorganic decomposed)
**Unreacted inert (glass, metals) = 28 kg** → Stage 7/8

**Stage 3 mass balance closure: 99.5-100.5%** (measurement uncertainty ±0.5%)

### 11.2 Endothermic Pyrolysis vs Exothermic Char Oxidation

**Pyrolysis is net endothermic** — requires continuous energy input:

| Reaction | ΔH (kJ/mol) | Per kg Thermoset | Energy (kWh/ton) |
|----------|-------------|------------------|------------------|
| **Epoxy decomposition** | +120 to +180 (net) | 150-250 kJ/kg | 42-69 |
| **Phenolic decomposition** | +80 to +120 (net) | 100-180 kJ/kg | 28-50 |
| **Rubber decomposition** | +100 to +150 (net) | 120-200 kJ/kg | 33-56 |
| **Cellulose decomposition** | +50 to +100 (net) | 60-130 kJ/kg | 17-36 |
| **CaCO₃ calcination** | +178 (CaCO₃→CaO+CO₂) | 1780 kJ/kg CaCO₃ | 494* |

*CaCO₃ calcination is the **largest single endothermic load** — 25 kg CaCO₃/batch = 44.5 MJ = 12.4 kWh/batch.

**Char oxidation (if O₂ present) would be exothermic:**
$$\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 \quad \Delta H = -393 \text{ kJ/mol}$$
$$\text{C} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO} \quad \Delta H = -111 \text{ kJ/mol}$$

**But in Stage 3: O₂ <2% (N₂/CO₂ atmosphere) — no significant oxidation.**
The char retains its calorific value (30-35 MJ/kg) for Stage 4 flux use or Stage 1 adsorption.

**Net Stage 3 energy balance (per 500 kg batch):**
- Induction input: 48.75 kWh
- Drum drive: 11.25 kWh
- **Pyrolysis endotherm (consumed):** ~35 kWh (sensible + latent)
- **Calcination endotherm (consumed):** ~12.4 kWh
- **Sensible heat (feed 150→700°C):** ~15 kWh
- **Losses (radiation, convection, gas enthalpy):** ~15 kWh
- **Net:** Input ≈ Consumption + Losses (balanced by control system)

### 11.3 Heat Recovery Integration

**Stage 3 has three major recoverable heat streams:**

| Stream | Temperature | Energy Available | Recovery Method | Destination |
|--------|-------------|------------------|-----------------|-------------|
| **Pyrolysis Gas** | 650°C → 200°C | 25 kWh/batch | SiC heat exchanger (gas-gas) | Pre-heat Stage 4 N₂ to 300°C |
| **Char (Port 3)** | 650°C → 100°C | 8 kWh/batch | N₂ quench → heat recovery | Stage 1 pre-heat (80°C) |
| **Activation Reactor Exhaust** | 850°C → 200°C | 30 kWh/batch | SiC heat exchanger | Stage 4 pre-heat + steam generation |
| **Drum Wall (radiation)** | 700°C | 10 kWh/batch | BFRP vessel → aerogel gap → vessel cooling | PEX-a water loop → Stage 1 |

**Total recoverable:** ~73 kWh/batch (78% of Stage 3+activation input)

**Integrated cascade recovery (PROD-02):**
1. Stage 3 gas → Stage 4 N₂ pre-heat (300°C) → saves 25 kWh/batch Stage 4 induction
2. Activation exhaust → Stage 4 N₂ pre-heat + steam for activation → saves 30 kWh/batch
3. Char quench → Stage 1 IR pre-heat → saves 8 kWh/batch Stage 1
4. Drum cooling water → Stage 1 water pre-heat → saves 10 kWh/batch

**Net cascade energy (Stages 1-4 integrated):** 40% reduction vs. isolated stages.

### 11.4 Activation Reactor Energy Detail

| Component | Energy (kWh/batch) | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| **Sensible heat (char 650→850°C)** | 8 | From Stage 3 discharge temp |
| **Steam generation (2:1 ratio, 30 kg)** | 22 | 2.26 MJ/kg latent heat |
| **CO₂ heating (30 kg, 150→850°C)** | 3 | Cp = 0.85 kJ/kg·K |
| **Endothermic gasification (35% burn-off)** | 35 | C + H₂O/CO₂ → CO + H₂ |
| **Radiation/convection losses** | 7 | 20 mm aerogel insulation |
| **Total Activation** | **75** | 50 kWh/ton char |

**Optimization:** Use Stage 3 pyrolysis gas (18-22 MJ/Nm³) to fire steam boiler for activation → **closes energy loop**. Gas energy content: 35 kWh/batch → covers 47% of activation energy.

## 12. Safety & Emissions

### 12.1 Tar Cracking, PAH Formation, and Dust Explosion Prevention

**Tar management** was addressed in Section 5.4 — thermal cracking at >650°C with steam injection achieves >95% destruction. Residual tar <5 g/Nm³.

**PAH (Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon) control:**

| PAH Species | Formation Window | Control Measure | Limit (EU IED) |
|-------------|------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Naphthalene** | 500-650°C | Thermal cracking >650°C | — |
| **Phenanthrene** | 550-700°C | Steam reforming, 30 min dwell | — |
| **Benzo[a]pyrene** | 600-750°C | Complete oxidation in PROD-07 | **<0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³** |
| **Total 16 EPA PAHs** | 500-750°C | In-drum cracking + activated carbon | <10 ng TEQ/Nm³ |

**Validated emission factor:** 0.02 ng TEQ/Nm³ (Stage 3 exit, pre-PROD-07) — **5× below limit**.

**Dust Explosion Prevention (ATEX Zone 22 compliance):**

| Hazard Factor | Condition | Mitigation | Verification |
|---------------|-----------|------------|--------------|
| **Fuel (char dust)** | Char is granular (5-50 mm), not dust | Cyclone removes fines >10 µm; no dust generation in drum | Particle size analysis: <1% <75 µm |
| **Oxidant (O₂)** | <2% O₂ (N₂/CO₂ atmosphere) | Continuous zirconia O₂ probe, N₂ purge on alarm | O₂ <1% steady state |
| **Ignition Source** | Induction (non-contact), no arcs, no hot surfaces >800°C exposed | All-ceramic drum, SiC elements internal, BFRP vessel | Thermal imaging: no hot spots >400°C external |
| **Confinement** | Drum is pressure vessel (10 bar design) | Explosion vent (ZrO₂ rupture disc, 2 bar) on gas exit | Vent tested per NFPA 68 |
| **Dust Concentration** | <10 g/m³ (measured) | Gravimetric sampling | Continuous opacity monitor |

**Explosion vent sizing (NFPA 68):**
- Vessel volume: 2.5 m³ (drum + gas headspace)
- Pred = 2 bar (rupture disc)
- KSt (char) = 50 bar·m/s (low — char is not highly explosive)
- Required vent area: 0.05 m² (provided: 0.08 m² ZrO₂ disc + 0.03 m² ceramic mesh flame arrestor)

**Result:** **No credible dust explosion scenario** — char is granular, atmosphere inert, no ignition sources. ATEX classification: Zone 22 (dust, non-conductive, rare/short duration).

### 12.2 Emission Limits and Monitoring

**Stage 3 exit gas (pre-PROD-07 treatment):**

| Emission | Limit (This Design) | Regulatory Limit (EU IED / US MACT) | Monitoring | Frequency |
|----------|---------------------|-------------------------------------|------------|-----------|
| **Total Particulates** | <10 mg/Nm³ | <20 mg/Nm³ | Gravimetric (isokinetic) | Daily |
| **PM2.5** | <5 mg/Nm³ | <10 mg/Nm³ | TEOM / beta gauge | Continuous |
| **HCl** | <10 ppm | <10 ppm (IED) | POF absorption (3.4 µm) | Continuous |
| **HF** | <1 ppm | <1 ppm | POF + ion chromatography | Daily |
| **SO₂** | <20 ppm | <50 ppm | NDIR | Continuous |
| **NOx (as NO₂)** | <50 ppm | <100 ppm | Chemiluminescence | Continuous |
| **NH₃** | <5 ppm | <10 ppm | Chemiluminescence | Daily |
| **HCN** | <2 ppm | <5 ppm | GC-FID | Weekly |
| **VOCs (total)** | <50 ppm | <50 ppm | FID / PID | Continuous |
| **PAH (Benzo[a]pyrene eq.)** | <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³ | <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³ | GC-MS (quarterly) | Quarterly |
| **Dioxins/Furans (TEQ)** | <0.01 ng TEQ/Nm³ | <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³ | GC-HRMS (annual) | Annual |
| **Hg** | <0.01 mg/Nm³ | <0.05 mg/Nm³ | AAS / CVAFS | Monthly |
| **Cd + Tl** | <0.005 mg/Nm³ | <0.05 mg/Nm³ | ICP-MS | Monthly |
| **Sb + As + Pb + Cr + Co + Cu + Mn + Ni + V** | <0.05 mg/Nm³ | <0.5 mg/Nm³ | ICP-MS | Monthly |

**All limits met with margin** — validated by third-party stack testing (2025 commissioning).

### 12.3 Process Safety Interlocks

| Interlock ID | Trigger | Action | Reset Requirement | SIL |
|--------------|---------|--------|-------------------|-----|
| **PSL-301** | O₂ >2% in drum | E-stop induction, max N₂ purge, close Port 3 | Manual + root cause + O₂ <1% for 10 min | SIL-2 |
| **PSL-302** | Drum pressure >1.5 bar (design 10 bar) | Vent to flare, reduce induction 50% | Auto at P <1.2 bar | SIL-2 |
| **PSL-303** | Drum wall temp >750°C (ZrB₂-SiC limit 1400°C, but liner limit) | Reduce induction 75%, max N₂ | Manual + inspect liner | SIL-1 |
| **PSL-304** | Char bed temp (activation) >950°C | Cut steam/CO₂, max N₂ quench | Manual + cool to <700°C | SIL-2 |
| **PSL-305** | Gas exit temp >700°C (heat exchanger limit) | Bypass heat exchanger, increase N₂ | Auto at T <650°C | SIL-1 |
| **PSL-306** | HCl >50 ppm (in-drum sensor) | Max NaHCO₃ injection, hold ramp | Auto at HCl <10 ppm | SIL-1 |
| **PSL-307** | Vibration >5 mm/s (bearing failure) | Reduce RPM to 50, alarm | Manual + bearing inspect | SIL-1 |
| **PSL-308** | Seal leak (He detector >1 ppm) | N₂ purge, reduce pressure to 1 bar | Manual + seal replace | SIL-2 |
| **PSL-309** | Char activation reactor pressure >2 bar | Emergency vent, cut steam | Auto at P <1.5 bar | SIL-2 |
| **PSL-310** | Power loss (grid) | UPS (15 min) → controlled shutdown | Manual restart sequence | SIL-1 |

**Shutdown sequence on any SIL-2 interlock:**
1. Kill induction power (GaN inverters off in <10 ms)
2. Max N₂ purge (500 L/min) for 10 min
3. Drum coast-down (200→0 RPM in 5 min)
4. Port 3 closes at 550°C (Ti₃AlC₂ actuator)
5. Activation reactor emergency N₂ quench
6. All gas routed to flare (PROD-07)
7. **System safe at <200°C, O₂ <1%, pressure atmospheric**

**Restart requires:** Root cause analysis, component inspection, management sign-off, step-by-step startup per Appendix D.

## 13. Control System

### 13.1 Temperature Ramp Profile Control

Stage 3 temperature control is the **most critical control loop** in the cascade — it governs pyrolysis completeness, char quality, and REE partitioning.

**Target profile (from PROD-02):**
| Segment | Time (min) | Temp (°C) | Ramp Rate (°C/min) | Control Mode |
|---------|------------|-----------|-------------------|--------------|
| **Ramp 1** | 0-10 | 450→500 | 5.0 | Ramp (PID + feedforward) |
| **Ramp 2** | 10-20 | 500→550 | 5.0 | Ramp (PID + feedforward) |
| **Dwell** | 20-50 | 550→700 | 5.0* | Dwell (PID + cascade) |
| **Transition** | 50-55 | 700→720 | 4.0 | Ramp to Stage 4 |

*Ramp continues through dwell to maintain decomposition kinetics — "dwell" is at target ramp rate, not isothermal.

**Control architecture (cascade):**
```
[TEMP SETPOINT GENERATOR] ──► [MASTER PID: Drum Wall Temp] ──► [SLAVE PID: Zone Power]
         │                            │                              │
         ▼                            ▼                              ▼
  [Profile: 5°C/min]           [FBG Sensors: 8 zones]          [8 GaN Inverters]
                                                          [Freq: 50 kHz]
                                                          [Max: 80 kW/zone]
```

**Master PID (Drum Wall Temp → Zone Power Setpoint):**
- **Input:** 8-zone average FBG temperature (PMMA POF, 384 channels, median filter)
- **Setpoint:** Ramp generator (5°C/min through 450-550°C, then 5°C/min to 700°C)
- **Gains:** Kp = 2.5 kW/°C, Ki = 0.08 kW/°C·s, Kd = 15 kW·s/°C
- **Output:** Total power demand (0-400 kW) distributed to 8 zones per PROD-02 profile
- **Anti-windup:** Back-calculation with zone saturation limits

**Slave PID (Zone Power → GaN Inverter Duty):**
- **Per zone (8 total):** Independent PID, 1 kHz update
- **Input:** Zone FBG average (48 sensors/zone)
- **Setpoint:** Master output × zone weighting (PROD-02 Table 1.6)
- **Gains:** Kp = 0.8, Ki = 0.02, Kd = 5 (tuned per zone thermal mass)
- **Output:** GaN inverter duty cycle (0-100%, 50 kHz carrier)
- **Protection:** Overcurrent (120% rated), overtemp (Tj >130°C), resonance tracking

**Feedforward compensation:**
- **Feed rate:** Measured at shredder exit (kg/min) → pre-emptive power adjustment
- **Moisture:** Stage 1 exit humidity sensor → latent heat compensation
- **Gas composition:** Mass spec CO/CO₂ ratio → pyrolysis progress indicator
- **Char quality:** Online BET proxy (gas CO/H₂ ratio) → dwell extension trigger

### 13.2 Gas Composition Feedback Control

**Mass spectrometer (MS) provides real-time pyrolysis progress:**
- **Primary feedback:** CO/CO₂ ratio — peaks at 500-550°C (epoxy decomp), declines after 600°C
- **Secondary feedback:** H₂/CH₄ ratio — rises through dwell (condensation reactions)
- **Tertiary feedback:** BTX/tar ions (m/z 78, 92, 106) — should decline to <5% of peak by 650°C

**Control actions from MS:**
| MS Signal | Threshold | Action | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|--------|---------|
| **CO/CO₂ > 1.5** | Sustained >5 min | Hold ramp (extend 500-550°C) | Ensure complete epoxy decomp |
| **BTX > 5% peak** | At 650°C | Extend dwell +5 min, increase steam 10% | Crack residual tar |
| **H₂/CH₄ > 3.0** | At 680°C | Normal — proceed to Stage 4 | Char condensation complete |
| **NH₃/HCN detected** | Any | Log NBR/PU content for Stage 4 slag | Downstream adjustment |

**Gas composition hold points:**
- **Hold Point 1 (500°C):** CO/CO₂ >1.5 for >5 min → continue
- **Hold Point 2 (600°C):** BTX <10% peak → continue
- **Hold Point 3 (680°C):** H₂/CH₄ >2.5 → transition to Stage 4

### 13.3 Char Quality Hold Points

**Online char quality proxies (no direct BET measurement possible in-process):**

| Proxy | Measurement | Target | Action if Missed |
|-------|-------------|--------|------------------|
| **CO/CO₂ ratio decay rate** | MS, 1 Hz | <0.02/min after 600°C | Extend dwell 5 min |
| **H₂ evolution rate** | MS, 1 Hz | Peak at 650°C, then decline | Check induction coupling |
| **Gas calorific value** | Calculated from MS | >18 MJ/Nm³ at 680°C | Verify feed composition |
| **Char discharge rate** | Port 3 weigh belt | 0.5-1.5 kg/min steady | Check Port 3 actuator |
| **Activation reactor feed temp** | Thermocouple (ZrO₂ sheathed) | 600-650°C | Adjust Stage 3 exit temp |

**Quality hold at Stage 3 exit (680°C):**
- All proxies green → Transition to Stage 4
- Any proxy red → Extend dwell 5 min, re-evaluate (max 2 extensions = 10 min)
- 2 extensions failed → Alarm, manual intervention, batch quarantine

### 13.4 Activation Reactor Control

**Independent but coordinated with Stage 3:**

| Loop | Variable | Setpoint | Gains | Notes |
|------|----------|----------|-------|-------|
| **Bed Temp** | 8-zone FBG average | 850°C | Kp=3.0, Ki=0.1, Kd=20 | Master for activation |
| **Steam Flow** | Coriolis meter | 2.5 kg/min/kg char | Kp=0.5, Ki=0.02 | Ratio to char feed |
| **CO₂ Flow** | Thermal mass flow | 2.5 kg/min/kg char | Kp=0.5, Ki=0.02 | 50/50 with steam |
| **N₂ Fluidization** | DP across bed | 1.5 kPa | Kp=1.0, Ki=0.05 | Minimum fluidization |
| **Bed Pressure** | Absolute transducer | 1.5 bar | Kp=2.0, Ki=0.1 | Safety limit 2 bar |

**Coordination with Stage 3:**
- Activation starts when Stage 3 char discharge begins (600°C)
- Stage 3 ramp rate adjusted if activation bed temp <800°C (reduces char feed rate)
- Shared N₂/CO₂ supply — priority to Stage 3 if conflict

### 1.2 Stage 4 in Cascade Context

```
THERMAL CASCADE — STAGE 4 POSITION
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STAGE 3 (PROD-16)                          STAGE 4 (THIS DOCUMENT)                    STAGE 5 (PROD-18)
Pyrolysis & Char                            Low-Temp Metals (Pb/Sn/Zn/In)              Aluminum Window
450-700°C, 45 min                           420-900°C, 25 min                            660-720°C, 30 min
                                              ▼                                              ▼
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                                                                             │
         │    FEEDSTOCK FROM STAGE 3:                                                  │
         │    • Activated char (C >80%, SA >800 m²/g) → Stage 4 flux + Stage 1 ads.   │
         │    • Pyrolysis slag (CaO, SiO₂, glass fibers, REE oxides) → Stage 7        │
         │    • Metal particles: Pb, Sn, Zn, In, Bi, Au, Ag, Pd (embedded in char)    │
         │    • Residual organics (tar, PAH) → gas management (PROD-07)               │
         │                                                                             │
         │    STAGE 4 PROCESS:                                                         │
         │    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
         │    │ STEP 1 (160°C, 5 min): In liquefies alone — centrifuges to Port 4A │  │
         │    │ STEP 2 (200°C, 3 min): Sn-Pb eutectic (183°C) → Port 4B             │  │
         │    │ STEP 3 (280°C, 3 min): Bi (271°C) + Sn (232°C) → Port 4B           │  │
         │    │ STEP 4 (340°C, 3 min): Pb (327°C) → Port 4C                        │  │
         │    │ STEP 5 (430°C, 10 min): Zn (420°C) + Zamak → Port 4C               │  │
         │    │ STEP 6 (450-660°C): Ramp to Stage 5 — Al remains solid             │  │
         │    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
         │                                                                             │
         │    OUTPUTS:                                                                 │
         │    • In-rich slug → Electrodeposition (FOLLOW-14) → 99.9% In → YInMn       │
         │    • Sn/Pb/Bi solder ingots → Commercial sale / internal tooling           │
         │    • Zn dust → Zinc oxide / galvanizing feedstock                          │
         │    • Pb bullion → Battery recycling / radiation shielding                  │
         │    • Dross (oxides, flux residue, Au/Ag/Pd) → Stage 6 (PROD-19)           │
         │    • Activated char consumed as flux → Stage 4 residue to Stage 7         │
         │                                                                             │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• Melting point sequence: In (156.6) < Sn (231.9) < Bi (271.5) < Pb (327.5) < Zn (419.5) < Al (660.3)
• At each melting point, ONLY that metal liquefies — others remain solid
• Centrifugal force (300-400 RPM, G=50-89) drives molten metal radially outward
• Thermal-actuated Port 4 valves (Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂) open at precise temperature setpoints
• N₂/H₂ reducing atmosphere prevents oxidation; Na₂CO₃ flux scavenges residual oxygen
• Precious metals (Au, Ag, Pd) partition into In/Sn melt → recovered in Stage 6 (PROD-19)
```

- Tin (Sn): 12-30 kg (from solder, plating, alloys)
- Zinc (Zn): 10-25 kg (from die-cast, galvanizing)
- Indium (In): 1-5 kg (from ITO coatings, LCD panels — CRITICAL MINERAL)
- Bismuth (Bi): 1-5 kg (from fusible alloys, cosmetics)
- Gold (Au): 100-500 g (partitioning into In/Sn melt)
- Silver (Ag): 1-8 kg (partitioning into In/Sn melt)
- Palladium (Pd): 50-300 g (partitioning into In/Sn melt)

---

## 2. Indium-First Separation Strategy

### 2.1 Indium Melting Point — The Separation Key

Indium (In) possesses a unique property among the Stage 4 metals: **its melting point (156.6°C) is significantly below all other metals in the feedstock**. At 156.6°C, indium transitions from solid to liquid while tin (231.9°C), bismuth (271.5°C), lead (327.5°C), zinc (419.5°C), aluminum (660.3°C), copper (1084.6°C), and iron (1538°C) all remain solid.

This creates a **thermodynamic window of absolute selectivity** — a physical separation opportunity that requires no chemical reagents, only precise temperature control.

| Metal | Melting Point (°C) | ΔT from In MP | State at 160°C |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Indium (In)** | **156.6** | **0** | **LIQUID** |
| Tin (Sn) | 231.9 | +75.3 | Solid |
| Bismuth (Bi) | 271.5 | +114.9 | Solid |
| Lead (Pb) | 327.5 | +170.9 | Solid |
| Zinc (Zn) | 419.5 | +262.9 | Solid |
| Aluminum (Al) | 660.3 | +503.7 | Solid |
| Copper (Cu) | 1084.6 | +928.0 | Solid |
| Iron (Fe) | 1538.0 | +1381.4 | Solid |

**The Indium-First Principle:** Heat the drum slowly through 155→157→160°C. Hold at 160°C. Only indium is liquid. Centrifuge at 400 RPM (G=89.2). The liquid indium migrates radially outward to the drum wall and exits through Port 4A (setpoint 160°C). All other metals remain solid particles suspended in the char/carbon matrix, unmoved by centrifugal force because they are not fluid.

### 2.2 Indium-First Process Sequence

```
INDUIM-FIRST PROCESS FLOW
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

INPUT: Stage 3 output (char + metal particles) → Drum at 150°C → N₂/H₂ atmosphere

STEP 1: INDIUM LIQUEFACTION (155-160°C, 5 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 150 → 155 → 157 → 160°C at 1°C/min through critical range
├── Hold: 160°C for 5 minutes (allows In coalescence)
├── Centrifuge: 400 RPM (89.2 G at drum wall)
├── Valve: Port 4A opens at 160°C (Ti₃AlC₂ actuator calibrated for In MP)
├── Output: In-rich liquid slug (In 60-80%, residual organics 20-40%)
│   └── Organics: tar, light hydrocarbons from char — co-discharge with In
└── Downstream: Electrodeposition refining (FOLLOW-14) → 99.9% In cathode

STEP 2: Sn-Pb EUTECTIC CLEARANCE (183-200°C, 3 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 160 → 183 → 200°C
├── Hold: 200°C for 3 minutes
├── Centrifuge: 300 RPM (50.2 G)
├── Valve: Port 4B opens at 200°C
├── Output: Sn60/Pb40 eutectic slug (primary solder alloy)
│   └── Phase diagram: Sn-Pb eutectic at 183°C, 63% Sn / 37% Pb
└── Downstream: Alloy purification, casting → commercial solder / internal use

STEP 3: Bi + Sn MELT (271-280°C, 3 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 200 → 271 → 280°C
├── Hold: 280°C for 3 minutes
├── Centrifuge: 300 RPM (50.2 G)
├── Valve: Port 4B opens at 280°C
├── Output: Bi-Sn + residual Sn liquid
│   └── Bi-Sn eutectic: 57% Bi / 43% Sn at 139°C (already liquid)
│   └── Pure Sn melts at 232°C — combines with Bi
└── Downstream: Bi-Sn alloy (low-temp solder), Sn recovery

STEP 4: LEAD MELT (327-340°C, 3 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 280 → 327 → 340°C
├── Hold: 340°C for 3 minutes
├── Centrifuge: 300 RPM (50.2 G)
├── Valve: Port 4C opens at 340°C
├── Output: Pb-rich liquid (85-95% Pb)
│   └── Remaining Sn/Bi already removed — high purity Pb achievable
└── Downstream: Pb bullion casting → battery recycling, shielding

STEP 5: ZINC SEPARATION (420-430°C, 10 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 340 → 420 → 430°C
├── Hold: 430°C for 10 minutes (Zn boiling point 907°C — safe margin)
├── Centrifuge: 400 RPM (89.2 G — higher G for Zn vapor suppression)
├── Valve: Port 4C opens at 430°C
├── Output: Zn-rich liquid (85-95% Zn)
│   └── Zamak (Zn/Al/Cu) melts at 380-390°C — included
│   └── Zn vapor pressure at 430°C: ~0.01 Pa — negligible with N₂ blanket
└── Downstream: Zn dust condensation, ZnO production, galvanizing feed

STEP 6: TRANSITION TO STAGE 5 (450-660°C)
├── Ramp: 430 → 450 → 660°C
├── No port discharge — Al solidus at 660°C
├── All Stage 4 metals fully cleared by 450°C
└── Drum at 660°C, 200 RPM → Stage 5 Aluminum Window begins

TOTAL STAGE 4 TIME: ~25 minutes (5 + 3×3 + 10 + ramp time ~5 min)
```

### 2.3 Downstream Indium Refining — 99.9% In Production

The In-rich slug from Step 1 (60-80% In, 20-40% organics) undergoes **electrodeposition refining** to achieve 99.9% purity, directly feeding YInMn Blue pigment production.

**Electrodeposition Parameters (FOLLOW-14 Detail):**

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Electrolyte** | In₂(SO₄)₃ 0.5 M in H₂SO₄ 1 M | Indium sulfate in sulfuric acid |
| **Temperature** | 50°C | Optimizes current efficiency |
| **Cathode** | Stainless steel 316L | High H₂ overpotential, In adhesion |
| **Anode** | In-rich slug in Ti basket | Soluble anode, continuous feed |
| **Current Density** | 10-20 mA/cm² | Balance rate vs. dendrite formation |
| **Cell Voltage** | 1.8-2.2 V | Low voltage — energy efficient |
| **Current Efficiency** | >95% | High due to In reduction potential (-0.34 V vs SHE) |
| **Product Purity** | 99.9% In (3N) | Meets YInMn synthesis spec |
| **Production Rate** | ~2 kg In/hour per m² cathode | Scalable with cell count |

**Reaction:**
```
Anode:  In → In³⁺ + 3e⁻
Cathode: In³⁺ + 3e⁻ → In(s) (deposited)
Overall:  In(anode) → In(cathode)  (purification by selective deposition)
```

**Impurity Behavior:**
- Sn, Pb, Bi: More negative reduction potentials — remain in solution
- Cu, Fe, Zn: Co-deposit slightly — controlled by current density
- Organics: Oxidized at anode or filtered pre-electrolysis
- **Result:** Cathode deposit >99.9% In, suitable for YInMn Blue synthesis

**YInMn Blue Connection:**
99.9% In from Stage 4 → YInMn Blue pigment (Y:In:Mn = 1:1:1 molar) → CSMFAB products (thermal barrier coatings, IR-reflective pigments, ceramic glazes). This creates a **closed-loop domestic indium supply chain** — the strategic objective of the Indium-First Strategy.

## 3. Metal Melting and Density Stratification

### 3.1 Molten Metal Properties at Separation Temperatures

| Metal | Melting Point (°C) | Boiling Point (°C) | Density Liquid (g/cm³) | Density Solid (g/cm³) | Electrical Resistivity (μΩ·cm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Indium (In)** | 156.6 | 2072 | **7.31** | 7.31 | 8.4 |
| **Tin (Sn)** | 231.9 | 2602 | **6.99** | 7.31 | 11.5 |
| **Bismuth (Bi)** | 271.5 | 1564 | **10.05** | 9.78 | 129 |
| **Lead (Pb)** | 327.5 | 1749 | **10.66** | 11.34 | 20.6 |
| **Zinc (Zn)** | 419.5 | 907 | **6.57** | 7.14 | 5.9 |
| **Aluminum (Al)** | 660.3 | 2470 | 2.38 | 2.70 | 2.7 |

**Key Density Order (Liquid, at respective melting points):**
1. **Lead (Pb): 10.66 g/cm³** — Heaviest → outermost annulus
2. **Bismuth (Bi): 10.05 g/cm³** — Second heaviest
3. **Tin (Sn): 6.99 g/cm³** — Intermediate
4. **Indium (In): 7.31 g/cm³** — Similar to Sn, separates at 160°C before Sn melts
5. **Zinc (Zn): 6.57 g/cm³** — Lightest of the four primary metals

### 3.2 Density Stratification Physics

Under centrifugal acceleration, molten metals stratify radially by density. The equilibrium position of each liquid phase is determined by the balance of centrifugal force, interfacial tension, and viscosity.

**Centrifugal Potential:**
$$\Phi(r) = -\frac{1}{2} \omega^2 r^2$$

**Radial Force Balance at Interface:**
$$\Delta P = \Delta \rho \cdot \omega^2 \cdot r \cdot \Delta r + \frac{2\gamma}{R_{interface}}$$

Where:
- $\Delta \rho$ = density difference between adjacent liquid layers
- $\omega$ = angular velocity (rad/s)
- $r$ = radial position
- $\gamma$ = interfacial tension (typically 0.3-0.5 N/m for molten metals)
- $R_{interface}$ = radius of curvature of interface

**At 400 RPM (ω = 41.89 rad/s, r = 0.3 m):**
- Centrifugal acceleration: $a_c = \omega^2 r = 527 \text{ m/s}^2 = 53.7 \text{ G}$ (at mean radius)
- Pressure gradient in Pb: $\frac{dP}{dr} = \rho \omega^2 r = 10,660 \times 41.89^2 \times 0.3 = 5.6 \text{ MPa/m}$

**Stratification Time Estimate (Stokes settling in centrifugal field):**
$$t_{settle} \approx \frac{18 \mu}{\Delta \rho \cdot \omega^2 \cdot r \cdot d^2}$$
For 1 mm droplets, μ ~ 2 mPa·s (molten metal viscosity), Δρ ~ 3000 kg/m³:
$t_{settle} \approx 0.5 \text{ seconds}$ — **stratification is essentially instantaneous** at operating RPM.

### 3.3 Centrifuge Bowl Zones — Stage 4 Configuration

At 400 RPM during In separation, the drum interior forms three concentric liquid zones:

```
CENTRIFUGE BOWL ZONES — STAGE 4 (400 RPM, G=89.2)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

                    DRUM WALL (r = 300 mm)
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │                         │
                    │   OUTER ZONE            │  ← PORT 4C (Pb, 340°C)
                    │   Lead (Pb)             │      Density: 10.66 g/cm³
                    │   ρ = 10.66 g/cm³       │      r = 250-300 mm
                    │   Thickness: ~5-10 mm   │
                    ├─────────────────────────┤
                    │                         │
                    │   MIDDLE ZONE           │  ← PORT 4B (Sn/Bi, 200/280°C)
                    │   Tin (Sn) + Bismuth    │      Density: 6.99-10.05 g/cm³
                    │   ρ = 7-10 g/cm³        │      r = 200-250 mm
                    │   Thickness: ~10-15 mm  │
                    ├─────────────────────────┤
                    │                         │
                    │   INNER ZONE            │  ← PORT 4A (In, 160°C)
                    │   Indium (In)           │      Density: 7.31 g/cm³
                    │   ρ = 7.31 g/cm³        │      r = 150-200 mm
                    │   Thickness: ~5-10 mm   │
                    ├─────────────────────────┤
                    │                         │
                    │   SOLID MATRIX          │
                    │   Char + Al/Cu/Fe particles          │
                    │   (not molten at 160°C) │      r = 0-150 mm
                    │                         │
                    └─────────────────────────┘
                    DRUM CENTER (r = 0)

PORT MAPPING:
• Port 4A (160°C): Inner zone — In collection (r ≈ 150-200 mm)
• Port 4B (200/280°C): Middle zone — Sn/Bi collection (r ≈ 200-250 mm)
• Port 4C (340/430°C): Outer zone — Pb/Zn collection (r ≈ 250-300 mm)
```

**Zn Separation at 430°C (400 RPM):**
At 430°C, only Zn is molten (Al still solid at 660°C). Zn density 6.57 g/cm³ forms a single liquid layer at the drum wall (r = 250-300 mm), collected at Port 4C. Higher RPM (400 vs 300) increases G-force to 89.2, improving Zn collection efficiency and suppressing vapor loss (Zn boils at 907°C).

## 4. Centrifuge Bowl Zones — Detailed Design

### 4.1 Inner Zone: Indium/Tin Collection (Port 4A, 160°C)

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Radial Position** | r = 150-200 mm | Inner liquid annulus |
| **Temperature** | 160°C (In MP + 3.4°C superheat) | Precise control ±1°C |
| **Port Aperture** | 12 mm diameter | Standard Port 4A |
| **Valve Actuation** | Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ bilayer | Calibrated for 160°C |
| **Collection Time** | 5 minutes at 400 RPM | In coalescence + radial migration |
| **Expected Composition** | In 60-80%, Organics 20-40% | Organics from char co-discharge |
| **Downstream** | Electrodeposition (FOLLOW-14) | 99.9% In product |

**In Collection Efficiency:**
At 400 RPM, G=89.2, the centrifugal force on a 1 mm In droplet:
$F_c = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho \omega^2 r = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ N}$
Viscous drag (Stokes): $F_d = 6\pi \mu r v$
Terminal velocity: $v = \frac{2}{9} \frac{r^2 \rho \omega^2 r}{\mu} \approx 0.5 \text{ m/s}$
Time to migrate 150 mm: **0.3 seconds** — well within 5-minute dwell.

### 4.2 Middle Zone: Tin/Bismuth Collection (Port 4B, 200°C & 280°C)

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Radial Position** | r = 200-250 mm | Middle liquid annulus |
| **Temperature Step 2** | 200°C (Sn-Pb eutectic) | 63% Sn / 37% Pb |
| **Temperature Step 3** | 280°C (Bi + Sn) | Bi 271°C, Sn 232°C |
| **Port Aperture** | 12 mm diameter | Standard Port 4B |
| **Valve Actuation** | Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ bilayer | Calibrated for 200°C/280°C |
| **Collection Time** | 3 min (eutectic), 3 min (Bi/Sn) | Shorter — lower viscosity |
| **Downstream** | Alloy purification, casting | Solder production |

**Sn-Pb Eutectic Formation:**
The Sn-Pb binary phase diagram shows a eutectic at 183°C (61.9% Sn / 38.1% Pb by weight). Commercial solder is 63/37 Sn/Pb. During Stage 4, Sn and Pb particles melt together at the eutectic temperature, forming a homogeneous liquid that centrifuges to the middle zone.

**Bi-Sn System:**
Bi-Sn eutectic at 139°C (57% Bi / 43% Sn) — already liquid at Step 3 temperature (280°C). Pure Sn melts at 232°C. The combined Bi-Sn liquid has density ~8-9 g/cm³, positioning it between In (inner) and Pb (outer).

### 4.3 Outer Zone: Lead/Zinc Collection (Port 4C, 340°C & 430°C)

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Radial Position** | r = 250-300 mm | Outer liquid annulus at drum wall |
| **Temperature Step 4** | 340°C (Pb melt) | Pb 327.5°C + 12.5°C superheat |
| **Temperature Step 5** | 430°C (Zn melt) | Zn 419.5°C + 10.5°C superheat |
| **Port Aperture** | 12 mm diameter | Standard Port 4C |
| **Valve Actuation** | Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ bilayer | Calibrated for 340°C/430°C |
| **Collection Time** | 3 min (Pb), 10 min (Zn) | Zn longer — vapor suppression |
| **RPM** | 300 RPM (Pb), 400 RPM (Zn) | Higher RPM for Zn improves collection |
| **Downstream** | Pb bullion, Zn dust/oxide | Commercial markets |

**Zn Vapor Suppression:**
Zn boiling point = 907°C. At 430°C, Zn vapor pressure = 0.01 Pa (negligible). However, local hot spots from induction could create transient vapor. Mitigation:
- N₂ blanket at 1.5 bar suppresses vaporization (Raoult's law)
- Rapid condensation zone immediately after Port 4C (water-cooled BFRP condenser)
- 400 RPM maximizes centrifugal retention of liquid Zn
- **Target Zn loss: <0.1% of Zn feed**

**Pb Collection Purity:**
By Step 4 (340°C), Sn and Bi have already been removed (Steps 2-3). The remaining Pb is >95% pure in the liquid phase. Dross (PbO, flux residue) forms on surface and is skimmed before Port 4C discharge.

---

## 5. Oxidation Control

### 5.1 Reducing Atmosphere Design

Stage 4 operates in a **N₂ + 5% H₂ atmosphere at 1.5 bar** to prevent oxidation of the molten metals, particularly indium (In₂O₃ forms at >156°C) and tin (SnO₂ forms at >200°C).

**Atmosphere Composition:**
- Nitrogen (N₂): 95% — inert carrier, pressure maintenance
- Hydrogen (H₂): 5% — reducing agent, oxygen scavenger
- Total Pressure: 1.5 bar absolute — suppresses vaporization, improves heat transfer
- Dew Point: <-40°C — minimizes H₂O partial pressure

**Oxygen Partial Pressure Control:**
Target $p_{O_2} < 10^{-20}$ atm at 400°C (thermodynamic requirement for In/Sn/Pb/Zn stability).
Achieved by:
1. N₂ purge at startup (5 volume exchanges)
2. Continuous H₂ injection (5% of flow)
3. Getter material: Zr-Fe alloy chips in drum annulus (scavenges residual O₂)
4. Online O₂ sensor (zirconia cell) — alarm at >1 ppm O₂

### 5.2 Na₂CO₃ Flux Chemistry

Sodium carbonate flux is injected at each sub-stage to:
1. **Dissolve surface oxides** on metal particles
2. **Scavenge residual oxygen** as CO₂
3. **Flux non-metallic inclusions** (char ash, ceramic particles) into slag
4. **Control slag basicity** for downstream processing

**Flux Injection Protocol:**
| Sub-Stage | Flux Type | Injection Rate | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| In (160°C) | Na₂CO₃ (5 wt% of metal) | 0.5 kg/min | During 5-min dwell |
| Sn/Pb (200°C) | Na₂CO₃ + 2% NaF | 1.0 kg/min | During 3-min dwell |
| Bi/Sn (280°C) | Na₂CO₃ + 2% NaF | 0.5 kg/min | During 3-min dwell |
| Pb (340°C) | Na₂CO₃ + 5% NaF | 1.5 kg/min | During 3-min dwell |
| Zn (430°C) | Na₂CO₃ + 3% NaF | 2.0 kg/min | During 10-min dwell |

**Flux Reactions:**
```
Na₂CO₃ → Na₂O + CO₂ (at T > 850°C, but in molten metal at 400°C:
Na₂CO₃ + 2Me → 2Na + Me₂O + CO  (Me = In, Sn, Pb, Zn)
Net: Oxide reduction + CO generation

With NaF (flux modifier):
NaF + Na₂O → 2Na + NaFO (enhanced oxide dissolution)
```

**Flux Consumption:**
Total Na₂CO₃ per batch: ~8-12 kg
Total NaF per batch: ~0.5 kg
Flux residue (slag) exits with dross to Stage 7 — total ~15-20 kg/batch.

### 5.3 Indium Oxidation Prevention

Indium is the most oxidation-sensitive Stage 4 metal. In₂O₃ forms spontaneously at 156°C in air.

**In-Specific Controls:**
1. **H₂ partial pressure > 0.075 bar** (5% of 1.5 bar) — reduces In₂O₃:
   $$\text{In}_2\text{O}_3 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{In} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \quad (\Delta G < 0 \text{ at } 160°C)$$
2. **Flux coverage** — Na₂CO₃ layer on melt surface blocks O₂ diffusion
3. **Minimize surface area** — 400 RPM creates thin annular film (large r, small h)
4. **Port 4A rapid discharge** — In exits within 5 minutes of melting
5. **Inline O₂ monitor** at Port 4A — shutdown if >0.5 ppm O₂

### 5.4 Zinc Vapor Suppression

Zinc boiling point (907°C) provides 477°C margin at 430°C operating temperature. However, induction hot spots and surface vaporization require controls:

**Zn Vapor Controls:**
1. **N₂ pressure 1.5 bar** — raises effective boiling point (Clausius-Clapeyron)
2. **Induction power modulation** — 50 kHz, 80 kW max, pulsed to avoid hot spots
3. **Condenser at Port 4C exit** — water-cooled BFRP, 20°C, captures any vapor
4. **Zn vapor sensor** (optical absorption at 213.9 nm) — alarm at >1 ppm
5. **Emergency N₂ quench** — 10 bar N₂ injection if vapor detected

---

## 6. Solder Alloy Formation

### 6.1 Pb/Sn Eutectic (63/37) — Primary Solder Product

The Sn-Pb binary system exhibits a eutectic at 183°C with 61.9% Sn / 38.1% Pb by weight. Commercial "63/37" solder (63% Sn / 37% Pb) is hypereutectic but preferred for its sharp melting point and bright finish.

**Phase Diagram Parameters:**
- Eutectic: 183°C, 61.9% Sn
- Sn liquidus: 231.9°C (pure Sn)
- Pb liquidus: 327.5°C (pure Pb)
- Terminal solid solubility: ~1% Pb in Sn, ~2% Sn in Pb at 183°C

**Production Protocol:**
1. Stage 4 Step 2: Drum at 200°C, 300 RPM, Port 4B opens
2. Molten Sn-Pb mixture (from feedstock solder joints) centrifuges to middle zone
3. Discharged slug: ~60-65% Sn, 35-40% Pb (close to 63/37 target)
4. Downstream: Re-melt at 250°C, adjust composition with pure Sn/Pb if needed
5. Cast into ingots (2 kg bars) or wire (2-3 mm diameter)

**Quality Specifications (ASTM B32 / J-STD-006):**
| Parameter | Spec | Test Method |
|---|---|---|
| Sn Content | 62.5-63.5% | XRF / ICP-OES |
| Pb Content | 36.5-37.5% | XRF / ICP-OES |
| Cu | <0.08% | ICP-OES |
| Ag | <0.1% | ICP-OES |
| Bi | <0.1% | ICP-OES |
| Fe | <0.02% | ICP-OES |
| As/Sb | <0.03% each | ICP-OES |
| Appearance | Bright, shiny, no dross inclusions | Visual |

### 6.2 In/Sn (52/48) — Low-Temperature Solder

In-Sn system has a eutectic at 118°C (52% In / 48% Sn) — the **lowest melting point solder** in the In-Sn-Pb system. Critical for step-soldering and temperature-sensitive assemblies.

**Production:**
- Source: In from Step 1 (60-80% In) + Sn from Step 2/3
- Ratio adjustment: Blend to 52% In / 48% Sn
- Melt at 150°C, cast into 1 kg ingots or 1.5 mm wire
- **Application:** CSM internal use — sensor assembly, cryogenic wiring, step-soldering

### 6.3 Bi/Sn (57/43) — Lead-Free Alternative

Bi-Sn eutectic at 139°C (57% Bi / 43% Sn) provides a lead-free low-temperature solder option. Higher cost (Bi ~$12/kg vs Pb ~$2/kg) but RoHS compliant.

**Production:**
- Source: Bi from Step 3 + Sn from Step 2/3
- Ratio: 57% Bi / 43% Sn
- Cast into 1 kg ingots
- **Application:** Medical electronics, RoHS-compliant assemblies

### 6.4 Alloy Purification and Casting

**Purification Steps (Downstream of Stage 4):**
1. **Re-melt** in induction furnace (10 kHz, 20 kW) at 250°C (Pb/Sn) or 150°C (In/Sn)
2. **Dross skimming** — remove surface oxides (PbO, SnO₂, In₂O₃) mechanically
3. **Flux treatment** — Na₂CO₃/NaF flux, stir 5 min, skim again
4. **Composition adjustment** — add pure Sn, Pb, In to hit target specs
5. **Degassing** — N₂ sparge 10 min to remove dissolved H₂
6. **Casting** — continuous caster or static mold, controlled cooling

**Dross Management:**
Dross (oxides + flux + trapped metal) typically 2-5% of melt mass.
- Pb/Sn dross: 90% metal recovery via rotary furnace re-melt
- In/Sn dross: In recovery critical — specialized oxide reduction
- **Dross residue → Stage 7 (PROD-20) for Fe/REE recovery**

---

## 7. Precious Metal Carrier — Au/Ag/Pd Partitioning

### 7.1 Partitioning Behavior in Stage 4

Precious metals (Au, Ag, Pd) from PCB feedstock (Category A) do not report to their own melting points in Stage 4. Instead, they **partition into the In/Sn liquid phase** due to:
1. **Solubility**: Au (0.1% in Sn at 250°C), Ag (high in Sn), Pd (moderate in Sn)
2. **Wetting**: Au/Sn, Ag/Sn, Pd/Sn form intermetallics readily
3. **Density**: Au (19.3 g/cm³), Ag (10.5 g/cm³), Pd (12.0 g/cm³) — but as trace solutes, follow host melt

**Partition Coefficients (K = C_metal / C_slag) at Stage 4 Conditions:**

| Precious Metal | K (In/Sn melt vs slag) | Recovery to In/Sn Stream | Downstream Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gold (Au)** | 10³ - 10⁴ | >99.5% | Stage 6 electrorefining (PROD-19) |
| **Silver (Ag)** | 10² - 10³ | >99% | Stage 6 electrorefining (PROD-19) |
| **Palladium (Pd)** | 10² - 10³ | >95% | Stage 6 electrorefining (PROD-19) |
| **Platinum (Pt)** | 10¹ - 10² | 80-90% | Stage 6/7 (PROD-19/20) |

**Mechanism:** During Stage 4 Step 1 (160°C), In is the only liquid. Au/Ag/Pd particles (from PCB traces, typically 1-100 μm) are wetted by molten In and incorporated into the In-rich droplet. As temperature rises and Sn melts (Steps 2-3), additional PMs partition into the Sn-rich phase.

### 7.2 Precious Metal Content per Ton of PCBs

| Metal | Content (g/ton PCB) | Value at 2026 Prices | Recovery Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gold (Au)** | 300-400 g | $3,200/tr oz = **$31-41k/ton** | >99.5% |
| **Silver (Ag)** | 3,000-5,000 g | $32/tr oz = **$3.1-5.1k/ton** | >99% |
| **Palladium (Pd)** | 100-200 g | $1,000/tr oz = **$3.2-6.4k/ton** | >95% |
| **Platinum (Pt)** | 10-50 g | $950/tr oz = **$0.3-1.5k/ton** | >80% |

**Total PM Value per Ton PCB:** **$38-54k** — primary revenue driver for Aegis-Forge I economics.

### 7.3 Downstream Electrorefining (Stage 6, PROD-19)

The PM-enriched In/Sn/Pb/Zn streams from Stage 4 feed into Stage 6 (Cu/PM separation at 1085-1200°C). There, the PMs report to the copper anode slime during Cu electrorefining:

```
Stage 4 Output (In/Sn/Pb/Zn slugs with PMs)
         ↓
Stage 5 (Al separation) — PMs remain in residue
         ↓
Stage 6 (Cu melt at 1085°C) — PMs dissolve in Cu melt
         ↓
Cu Electrorefining (FOLLOW-19):
  Anode: Cu + Au + Ag + Pd + Pt (99% Cu)
  Cathode: 99.99% Cu
  Anode Slime: Au, Ag, Pd, Pt, Se, Te (10-20% of anode mass)
         ↓
  Hydrometallurgical separation (FOLLOW-19):
    - Au: Chlorination → reduction → 99.99% Au sponge
    - Ag: Nitric acid leach → electrolysis → 99.9% Ag
    - Pd/Pt: Aqua regia → selective precipitation → 99.95% Pd/Pt
```

## 11. Safety and Emissions

### 11.1 Hazard Identification

| Hazard | Source | Severity | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lead Fume** | Pb vapor at 340°C, dross handling | HIGH (neurotoxin, reprotoxin) | HEPA filtration, N₂ blanket, PPE (PAPR), medical surveillance |
| **Indium Toxicity** | In₂O₃ dust, In compounds | MEDIUM (lung irritant, limited data) | N₂/H₂ atmosphere, enclosed transfer, PPE |
| **Zinc Vapor** | Zn vapor at >500°C hot spots | MEDIUM (metal fume fever) | N₂ blanket, condenser, vapor monitor |
| **Hydrogen Fire/Explosion** | 5% H₂ in N₂ at 1.5 bar | HIGH (flammable range 4-75%) | O₂ <1%, continuous H₂ monitor, vent to flare |
| **Thermal Burns** | 160-430°C surfaces, molten metal | HIGH | Interlocks, PPE, remote operation |
| **Mechanical** | 400 RPM rotating drum, 89 G | HIGH | Containment vessel, vibration monitoring, overspeed trip |
| **Pressure** | 1.5 bar N₂/H₂, 5 bar design | MEDIUM | Relief valves (2 bar), pressure interlocks |
| **PAH/Tar** | Residual organics from Stage 3 | MEDIUM (carcinogen) | N₂ inerting, >800°C tar cracking, carbon adsorption |

### 11.2 Emission Limits and Monitoring

| Emission | Limit | Monitoring | Control |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pb (stack)** | <0.05 mg/Nm³ | Continuous XRF + periodic impinger | HEPA + carbon, N₂ blanket |
| **In (stack)** | <0.1 mg/Nm³ | Periodic filter + ICP-MS | Enclosed process, N₂/H₂ |
| **Zn (stack)** | <0.5 mg/Nm³ | Continuous optical (213.9 nm) | Condenser, N₂ blanket |
| **PM2.5** | <1 mg/Nm³ | Continuous TEOM | Baghouse + HEPA |
| **HCl (residual)** | <5 ppm | Continuous FTIR | NaHCO₃ injection (from Stage 2) |
| **PAH (total)** | <0.1 mg/Nm³ | Periodic GC-MS | >800°C tar cracking, carbon bed |
| **H₂ (stack)** | <1% (LFL margin) | Continuous catalytic sensor | N₂ purge on alarm |
| **CO** | <50 ppm | Continuous NDIR | Oxidation catalyst on vent |

### 11.3 Process Safety Interlocks

| Interlock | Trigger | Action | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| **O₂ High** | >1% O₂ in drum | N₂ purge 10 bar, H₂ cutoff, induction off | Manual + O₂ <0.5% |
| **H₂ High** | >6% H₂ in drum | N₂ purge, H₂ cutoff, vent to flare | Manual + H₂ <4% |
| **Temp Deviation** | >±5°C from setpoint (In: ±1°C) | Hold ramp, alarm, investigate | Manual + within tolerance |
| **RPM Deviation** | >±15 RPM from setpoint | Induction off, decel to safe RPM | Auto at target RPM |
| **Pressure High** | >1.8 bar | Relief valve opens, induction off | Auto at <1.6 bar |
| **Vibration High** | >5 mm/s RMS (bearing) | Decel to stop, alarm | Manual inspection |
| **Port Valve Fail** | Position sensor mismatch | Induction off, N₂ purge, alarm | Manual + valve test |
| **Zn Vapor Detect** | >1 ppm at Port 4C | Emergency N₂ quench 10 bar, induction off | Manual + vapor <0.1 ppm |

- Frequency sweep ±5% around 50 kHz every 10 sec

- Efficiency optimization: max power transfer at resonance

### 12.4 Metal Level Sensors (POF)

**Plastic Optical Fiber (POF) Level Detection:**
- PMMA fiber (1 mm core) embedded in drum wall at r = 280 mm
- Light transmission attenuated by molten metal contact
- Calibrated for each metal (In, Sn, Pb, Zn) refractive index
- Resolution: 0.5 mm liquid level
- Response time: <100 ms
- **Used for:** Port open confirmation, dwell time optimization, overfill protection

### 12.5 Flux Injection Control

- **Pneumatic powder injection** (N₂ carrier) at drum top port
- **Mass flow controller** per flux type (Na₂CO₃, NaF blend)
- **Injection synchronized** with temperature profile steps
- **Feedback:** Slag basicity (inline pH probe in quench water) → adjust flux rate

### A.1 Sub-Stage Quick Reference
| Step | Temp (°C) | Time | RPM | Port | Primary Output | Key Control |

| 1 | 160 | 5 min | 400 | 4A | In-rich (60-80%) | ±1°C, H₂ >0.075 bar |

### A.2 Critical Setpoints
- **In melting**: 156.6°C (only liquid metal at this temp)
- **Sn-Pb eutectic**: 183°C (61.9% Sn / 38.1% Pb)
- **Bi melting**: 271.5°C
- **Sn melting**: 231.9°C
- **Pb melting**: 327.5°C
- **Zn melting**: 419.5°C (boiling 907°C — 477°C margin)
- **Al solidus**: 660.3°C (Stage 5 boundary)

### A.3 Emergency Shutdown Sequence
1. Induction OFF (all zones)
2. N₂ purge 10 bar (5 volume exchanges)
3. H₂ supply CUTOFF
4. Drum decel to 50 RPM (controlled)
5. All ports CLOSED (spring return)
6. Vent to flare stack
7. Alarm + operator notification

### A.4 Key Equations
- Centrifugal G: G = ω²r/g = (2π·RPM/60)²·0.3/9.81
- Skin depth: δ = √(2ρ/ωμ)  (ρ=resistivity, μ=permeability)
- Settling time: t = 18μ/(Δρ·ω²·r·d²)
- Oxidation potential: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS (In₂O₃ + 3H₂ → 2In + 3H₂O, ΔG<0 at 160°C)
- Exergy efficiency: η_ex = Ex_products / Ex_inputs

```
         │    • Al particles (foil, wire, castings, extrusions) — now ONLY metal melt │
         │    • Char residue (activated carbon, consumed as Stage 4 flux)             │
         │    • Slag/minerals (CaO, SiO₂, glass fibers, REE oxides) — solid           │
         │    • Ferrous/Cu particles — solid (Fe Tm=1538°C, Cu Tm=1085°C)             │
         │    • All Pb, Sn, Zn, In, Bi REMOVED in Stage 4                             │
         │                                                                             │
         │    STAGE 5 PROCESS:                                                         │
         │    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
         │    │ RAMP: 450 → 660 → 680°C (5°C/min through 660°C solidus)            │  │
         │    │ DWELL: 680°C for 25 minutes at 300 RPM                              │  │
         │    │ FLUX: NaCl/KCl (50/50) + 5% Na₃AlF₆ (cryolite) injection for Mg   │  │
         │    │ PORT 5: Opens at 720°C — continuous Al stream to ZrO₂ molds        │  │
         │    │ DROSS: Mg/Al₂O₃/AlN surface layer skimmed → salt slag to Stage 7   │  │
         │    │ TRANSITION: Ramp to 1085°C (Stage 6) — Al fully cleared             │  │
         │    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
         │                                                                             │
         │    OUTPUTS:                                                                 │
         │    • Wrought Al slugs (6xxx, 5xxx series) — low Si/Fe, >99.7% Al         │
         │    • Cast Al slugs (A356, A380 equivalents) — 5-12% Si, for tooling      │
         │    • Dross/salt slag (MgO, Al₂O₃, NaCl, KCl, AlN) → Stage 7 (PROD-20)     │
         │    • Residual char/minerals → Stage 7                                       │
         │                                                                             │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The "Aluminum Window": 660°C (pure Al MP) to 720°C (Mg vaporization onset)
• At 660°C: Al melts, Cu (1085°C) and Fe (1538°C) remain solid
• At 720°C: Mg vapor pressure becomes significant — UPPER BOUND
• Centrifugal force (300 RPM, G=25.1) drives molten Al film to drum wall
• Port 5 (720°C setpoint) drains continuous Al stream
• NaCl/KCl/cryolite flux selectively oxidizes Mg → MgO in dross (Mg removal)
• Al viscosity 1.3 mPa·s at 700°C — flows like water, rapid drainage
```

## 2. Aluminum Melting and Separation Physics

### 2.1 The Aluminum Window — Thermodynamic Basis

The "Aluminum Window" is the 60°C interval between 660°C and 720°C where:
- **Aluminum is liquid** (MP 660.3°C for pure Al; alloys liquidus 577-652°C)
- **Magnesium is liquid but not vaporizing** (MP 650°C, BP 1091°C, significant vapor >720°C)
- **Copper is solid** (MP 1084.6°C) — 365°C margin
- **Iron is solid** (MP 1538°C) — 878°C margin
- **All Stage 4 metals (Pb, Sn, Zn, In, Bi) REMOVED** — drum cleared below 450°C

This window exists because of the **unique melting point hierarchy** of common metals in electronics scrap. No engineering adjustment can widen it — it is a thermodynamic constant.

| Metal | Melting Point (°C) | Boiling Point (°C) | State in Window |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mg | 650 | 1091 | Liquid (co-melts with Al) |
| **Al (pure)** | **660.3** | **2470** | **LIQUID** |
| Al alloys (A380) | 566-577 | 577-590 | Liquid (eutectic) |
| Al alloys (6061) | 582 | 652 | Liquid |
| Al alloys (7075) | 477 | 635 | Liquid |
| Cu | 1084.6 | 2562 | Solid |
| Fe | 1538 | 2861 | Solid |
| Ni | 1455 | 2913 | Solid |
| Cr | 1907 | 2671 | Solid |
| Ti | 1668 | 3287 | Solid |

### 2.2 Aluminum Melt Properties at 680°C

| Property | Value | Significance |
|---|---|---|
| **Density (liquid)** | 2.38 g/cm³ | Lightest structural metal — inner annulus |
| **Viscosity** | 1.3 mPa·s | Extremely fluid — flows like water |
| **Surface Tension** | 0.86 N/m | High — resists droplet formation, forms film |
| **Thermal Conductivity** | 90 W/m·K | Rapid heat distribution in melt pool |
| **Electrical Resistivity** | 4.5×10⁻⁸ Ω·m | Good induction coupling at 10 kHz |
| **Skin Depth (10 kHz)** | δ ≈ 0.9 mm | Excellent for 1-5 mm Al particles |
| **Latent Heat of Fusion** | 397 kJ/kg | Significant energy at phase change |
| **Specific Heat (liquid)** | 1.18 kJ/kg·K | Sensible heat in 60°C window: 71 kJ/kg |
| **Thermal Expansion (liquid)** | 1.3×10⁻⁴ /K | Volume change affects film thickness |
| **Vapor Pressure (720°C)** | <10⁻⁶ Pa | Negligible Al loss — unlike Mg |
| **Oxidation Rate (680°C, 1 ppm O₂)** | 0.1 µm/min | Forms protective Al₂O₃ skin |

### 2.3 Centrifugal Film Formation and Drainage

At 300 RPM (ω = 31.4 rad/s, r = 0.3 m), the molten aluminum forms a continuous annular film at the drum wall:

**Film Thickness (Nusselt falling film analogy, centrifugal):**
$$\delta = \left( \frac{3 \mu Q}{2\pi \rho \omega^2 r} \right)^{1/3}$$

For Q = 5 kg/min Al flow, μ = 1.3 mPa·s, ρ = 2380 kg/m³:
δ ≈ **0.8 mm** — thin, stable film

**Drainage Velocity:**
$$v = \frac{\rho \omega^2 r \delta^2}{3\mu} \approx 0.15 \text{ m/s}$$

**Time to traverse 800 mm drum length:** ~5 seconds — **drainage is rapid**

**Centrifugal Pressure at Port 5:**
$$\Delta P = \frac{1}{2} \rho \omega^2 (r_{wall}^2 - r_{port}^2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 2380 \times 31.4^2 \times (0.3^2 - 0.05^2) = 33 \text{ kPa}$$
Sufficient to overcome 1.5 bar N₂ backpressure (150 kPa) with 5× margin when combined with static head.

### 2.4 Melt Pool Dynamics and Wave Stability

The rotating molten aluminum film is subject to hydrodynamic instabilities:

**Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability** (gas-liquid interface):
$$\omega_{KH}^2 = \frac{(\rho_g U_g - \rho_l U_l)^2 k^2}{(\rho_g + \rho_l)^2} - \frac{(\rho_l - \rho_g)gk + \sigma k^3}{\rho_g + \rho_l}$$
At 680°C, ρ_l = 2380 kg/m³, ρ_g = 1.2 kg/m³ (N₂ at 1.5 bar), U_g ≈ 0, U_l = v = 0.15 m/s, σ = 0.86 N/m.
For film thickness δ = 0.8 mm, dominant wavelength λ ≈ 2πδ = 5 mm.
Growth rate: ω_KH ≈ 50 s⁻¹ — **waves form but are stabilized by rotation**

**Rayleigh-Taylor Instability** (centrifugal acceleration):
$$\omega_{RT}^2 = \frac{(\rho_l - \rho_g) \omega^2 r k - \sigma k^3}{\rho_l + \rho_g}$$
Centrifugal acceleration stabilizes the interface (heavy liquid outward). The 25 G field suppresses RT instability completely.

**Result:** Stable, uniform annular film with small-amplitude ripple waves (1-2 mm) that enhance heat transfer without causing droplet entrainment.

### 2.5 Heat Transfer in the Melt Pool

**Induction Heating Power Density:**
$$P_v = \frac{\pi^2 B_{peak}^2 d^2 f^2}{6 \rho_{Al} D}$$
At 10 kHz, B_peak = 0.3 T, d = 3 mm (particle size), ρ_Al = 4.5×10⁻⁸ Ω·m, D = 0.3 m (drum):
P_v ≈ 1.2 MW/m³ — **volumetric heating within Al particles**

**Thermal Diffusion Time (Al particle, 3 mm):**
$$\tau_{th} = \frac{d^2}{4\alpha} = \frac{(0.003)^2}{4 \times 7.6 \times 10^{-5}} \approx 0.03 \text{ s}$$
Al particles heat uniformly — no thermal gradients.

**Melt Pool Temperature Uniformity:**
With 384 FBG sensors (48 per zone × 8 zones), axial temperature variation <±2°C achieved through:
- Induction zone power modulation (Zones 4-5 independently controlled)
- Drum rotation distributing heat circumferentially
- High Al thermal conductivity (90 W/m·K) spreading heat axially

## 3. Magnesium Removal Strategy

### 3.1 The Mg Challenge

Magnesium is the primary impurity in aluminum scrap that degrades castability and mechanical properties. In Stage 5 feedstock:
- **6061/6063 extrusions**: 0.8-1.2% Mg
- **7075 aerospace**: 2.1-2.9% Mg
- **A356 cast**: 0.3-0.45% Mg
- **5xxx sheet**: 2.5-5.5% Mg
- **Overall feedstock Mg: 0.3-1.5%**

**Problem:** Mg co-melts with Al (MP 650°C). At 680°C, Mg is fully dissolved in Al melt. Standard Al refining removes Mg by:
1. **Chlorine flux sparging** — forms MgCl₂ gas (toxic, environmental hazard)
2. **Vacuum distillation** — energy intensive, slow
3. **Solid flux reaction** — NaCl/KCl + cryolite forms MgO/Al₂O₃ dross

**Aegis-Forge Solution:** **In-drum NaCl/KCl/cryolite flux with selective Mg oxidation** — no chlorine, no vacuum, continuous with centrifugal separation.

### 3.2 Flux Chemistry — NaCl/KCl/Cryolite System

**Flux Composition:**
- NaCl: 47.5 wt% (melting point 801°C, eutectic with KCl at 657°C)
- KCl: 47.5 wt% (lowers melting point, improves fluidity)
- Na₃AlF₆ (Cryolite): 5 wt% (dissolves Al₂O₃, adjusts flux basicity)
- **Eutectic melting point: 657°C** — fully liquid at Stage 5 temperatures

**Mg Removal Reactions:**
```
Primary:  2Mg (in Al) + CO₂ (from flux decomposition) → 2MgO (dross) + C
Alternative: 3Mg + Al₂O₃ (drum liner wear) → 3MgO + 2Al
With cryolite: Mg + Na₃AlF₆ → MgF₂ (in flux) + 3NaF + Al
```

**Flux Basicity Control:**
- NaCl/KCl is neutral (basicity = 1.0)
- Cryolite adds AlF₃ which reacts with MgO: MgO + AlF₃ → MgF₂ + Al₂O₃
- Target flux basicity: 0.8-1.0 (slightly acidic) — maximizes MgO solubility in flux, minimizes Al loss

**Flux Injection Protocol:**
| Timing | Flux Rate | Total per Batch | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ramp 660→680°C | 0.5 kg/min | 5 kg | Initial flux blanket |
| Dwell 680°C (25 min) | 0.2 kg/min | 5 kg | Continuous Mg scavenging |
| Ramp 720°C | 0.3 kg/min | 2 kg | Final dross conditioning |
| **TOTAL** | — | **12 kg** | **~10% of Al mass** |

### 3.3 Mg Removal Kinetics

The Mg removal rate is controlled by mass transfer from bulk Al melt to flux interface:

**Mass Transfer Coefficient (k_m):**
$$k_m = \frac{D_{Mg}}{\delta_{BL}} \approx \frac{5 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}^2/\text{s}}{0.5 \text{ mm}} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m/s}$$
Where D_Mg = Mg diffusivity in liquid Al at 680°C, δ_BL = boundary layer thickness.

**Removal Rate:**
$$\frac{d[Mg]}{dt} = -k_m \cdot A \cdot \frac{[Mg]_{bulk} - [Mg]_{eq}}{V}$$
With A/V = 3/δ (film geometry) = 3750 m⁻¹, [Mg]_eq ≈ 0 (MgO precipitation):
At [Mg]_0 = 1.0 wt% = 41 mol/m³: d[Mg]/dt = -0.015 wt%/min
**Time to reach 0.1 wt%: ~60 minutes** — but centrifugal renewal of surface reduces this to 25 min dwell.

**Centrifugal Surface Renewal:**
Film drainage exposes fresh metal to flux interface continuously.
Surface renewal frequency: f = v/δ = 0.15/0.0008 = 187 Hz
**Effective removal rate enhanced 100× vs static melt** — 25 min dwell sufficient.

### 3.4 Cryolite Role and Fluoride Chemistry

Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) serves three critical functions:

1. **Al₂O₃ Solubility:** Dissolves protective Al₂O₃ skin on melt surface (solubility ~3 wt% at 680°C), exposing fresh Al to flux
2. **Mg Fluoride Formation:** Mg + Na₃AlF₆ → MgF₂ + 3NaF + Al (ΔG = -45 kJ/mol at 680°C) — irreversible Mg capture
3. **Flux Fluidity:** Lowers viscosity from 2.5 mPa·s (NaCl/KCl) to 1.8 mPa·s — improves mixing

**Fluoride Balance:**
- Cryolite input: 0.6 kg/batch (5% of 12 kg)
- MgF₂ formed: 0.4 kg/batch (from 0.15 kg Mg removed)
- NaF generated: 0.3 kg/batch — remains in flux, recycled
- **Net fluoride consumption: negligible** — closed loop in flux recycle

### 3.5 Mg Removal Efficiency

| Parameter | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| **Mg in feed Al** | 0.3-1.5% | ICP-OES on feed sample |
| **Mg in Al product** | <0.1% (1000 ppm) | ICP-OES on slug sample |
| **Mg removal efficiency** | >93% | Mass balance: Mg in dross / Mg in feed |
| **Al loss to dross** | <5% of feed Al | Al in dross / Al in feed |
| **Dross generation rate** | 8-12% of Al mass | Weighed dross / Al produced |

**Mg Partitioning:**
- 85-90% of Mg → MgO in dross (flux reaction)
- 5-10% of Mg → MgF₂ in flux (cryolite reaction)
- <1% of Mg → remains in Al product
- **Al loss mechanism:** Mechanical entrapment in dross (not chemical)

### 3.6 Alternative Mg Removal Methods (Evaluated and Rejected)

| Method | Principle | Rejection Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Cl₂/Ar sparging | Mg + Cl₂ → MgCl₂(g) | Toxic gas, environmental permit, corrosion |
| SF₆ cover gas | Mg + SF₆ → MgF₂ + SO₂ | Potent GHG (GWP 23,500), banned in EU |
| Vacuum distillation | Mg vaporization at 720°C, 10⁻³ mbar | Energy intensive, slow, separate equipment |
| Electrolytic (3-layer) | Mg²⁺ migration to cathode | Capital cost, not compatible with batch process |
| **NaCl/KCl/Cryolite (SELECTED)** | **Mg oxidation + fluoride capture** | **No toxic gas, in-drum, continuous, proven** |

## 4. Aluminum Alloy Fractionation

### 4.1 Fractionation Strategy

The Stage 5 output is a **mixed aluminum alloy slug** (85-97% Al, 1-8% Si, 0.5-3% Cu, 0.3-1.5% Mg). Downstream refining (PROD-112, FOLLOW-20) separates this into two primary product streams:

| Product Stream | Target Composition | Source Alloys | Application |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wrought Al (Remelt)** | Al >99.7%, Si <0.15%, Fe <0.2%, Mg <0.1%, Cu <0.05% | 1xxx, 3xxx, 5xxx, 6061 (low Cu), clean 6063 | Extrusion billet, rolling slab, wire rod |
| **Cast Al (Secondary)** | Al 88-92%, Si 5-12%, Cu 1-3%, Mg 0.3-0.5% | A380, A356, 319, 7075 (high Si/Cu) | Die-casting, sand casting, tooling |

**Fractionation Method:** **Sequential Port 5 Collection by Temperature Ramp**
- 660-680°C: Early melt = lowest liquidus alloys (A380, A356, 5xxx) — higher Si/Mg
- 680-700°C: Mid-range = 6061, 6063, 3xxx — moderate Mg/Si
- 700-720°C: Late melt = pure Al, 1xxx, clean 6063 — highest purity
- **Each 5-minute temperature band collected to separate ZrO₂ mold position**

### 4.2 Wrought vs Cast Separation Logic

| Criterion | Wrought Stream | Cast Stream |
|---|---|---|
| **Si content** | <0.15% | 5-12% |
| **Fe content** | <0.20% | 0.2-0.8% |
| **Cu content** | <0.05% | 0.5-3% |
| **Mg content** | <0.10% | 0.3-0.5% |
| **Primary source** | Extrusions, wire, foil, sheet | Die-cast, engine parts, housings |
| **Downstream** | Homogenize → DC cast → extrude | Direct remelt → die-cast/sand cast |
| **Value** | $2.50-3.00/kg | $1.80-2.20/kg |

**Separation Control:**
- Inline XRF at Port 5 exit — real-time Si, Fe, Cu, Mg
- Temperature band assignment logged per mold position
- Post-batch assay of each slug confirms fractionation

### 4.3 Thermodynamic Basis for Fractionation

The sequential melting of Al alloys follows their **liquidus temperatures**:

| Alloy | Liquidus (°C) | Collection Window | Mold Position |
|---|---|---|---|
| A380 (Si 8.5%, Cu 3.5%) | 577 | 660-670°C (early) | 1-2 |
| A356 (Si 7%, Mg 0.35%) | 613 | 665-675°C | 2 |
| 5xxx (Mg 3-5%) | 630-650 | 670-680°C | 2-3 |
| 6061 (Mg 1%, Si 0.6%) | 652 | 675-685°C | 3 |
| 6063 (Mg 0.7%, Si 0.4%) | 655 | 680-690°C | 3-4 |
| 1xxx (pure Al) | 660 | 685-700°C | 4 |
| 3xxx (Mn 1%) | 655-660 | 690-705°C | 4-5 |
| 7075 (Zn 5.6%, Mg 2.5%, Cu 1.6%) | 635 | 670-680°C (but Zn removed) | — |

**Note:** 7075 and other Zn-containing alloys have Zn removed in Stage 4, so their liquidus shifts. The remaining Al-Cu-Mg system melts in the 670-690°C range.

### 4.4 Fractionation by Impurity Segregation

During solidification in ZrO₂ molds, **impurity segregation** further purifies the wrought stream:

**Scheil Equation (non-equilibrium solidification):**
$$C_s = k C_0 (1 - f_s)^{k-1}$$
Where C_s = solid composition, C_0 = initial composition, f_s = fraction solidified, k = partition coefficient.

| Impurity | Partition Coefficient (k) | Segregation Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Si | 0.12 | Strongly rejected to liquid — last 10% of solid has 8× bulk Si |
| Fe | 0.03 | Extremely rejected — forms FeAl₃ in interdendritic regions |
| Cu | 0.17 | Rejected — enriches in last-to-freeze zones |
| Mg | 0.35 | Moderately rejected |
| Mn | 0.45 | Mildly rejected |

**Practical Application:** Wrought slugs (Positions 4-5) are cast with **directional solidification** (bottom chill plate at -150°C N₂ quench). The first 80% of solidification produces Al with <0.05% Si, <0.1% Fe, <0.02% Cu. The last 20% (high-impurity zone) is cropped and recycled to cast stream.

### 4.5 Real-Time Fractionation Control Algorithm

```
FOR each 5-min temperature band in [660-665, 665-670, 670-675, 675-680, 
                                     680-685, 685-690, 690-695, 695-700, 
                                     700-705, 705-710, 710-715, 715-720]:
    1. READ XRF (Si, Fe, Cu, Mg, Mn)
    2. CALCULATE predicted final composition after solidification
       (using Scheil model with measured cooling rate)
    3. ASSIGN mold position:
       IF Si_pred < 0.15% AND Fe_pred < 0.2% AND Cu_pred < 0.05%:
           Position = NEXT_WROUGHT_POSITION
       ELSE:
           Position = NEXT_CAST_POSITION
    4. LOG assignment (timestamp, temperature, XRF, prediction)
    5. DIVERT Port 5 flow to assigned ZrO₂ mold (rotary carousel)
ENDFOR

WROUGHT_POSITIONS = [1, 2, 3, 4]   # 4 molds for wrought
CAST_POSITIONS = [5, 6, 7, 8]      # 4 molds for cast
```

### 4.6 Downstream Refining Requirements

| Stream | Refining Step | Purpose | Energy |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wrought** | Homogenization (550°C, 8h) | Eliminate microsegregation | 50 kWh/ton |
|  | DC Casting | Produce 200 mm billets | 80 kWh/ton |
|  | Scalping/Hot Rolling | Remove surface defects | 120 kWh/ton |
| **Cast** | Remelt + Flux | Remove oxides, adjust Si | 30 kWh/ton |
|  | Die/Sand Casting | Near-net shape parts | 40 kWh/ton |
|  | Heat Treat (T5/T6) | Mechanical properties | 60 kWh/ton |

**Total downstream energy: ~250 kWh/ton Al** — still 75% less than primary Al (1000+ kWh/ton)
