## 13. Control System

### 13.1 Control Architecture — Stage 8 Specific

**Cascade PID Structure (from PROD-10, extended for Stage 8):**
```
STAGE 8 CONTROL HIERARCHY
══════════════════════════

SUPERVISORY (1 Hz)
├── Batch State Machine: CHARGE → DISSOCIATION → FLASH_SINTER → RESIDUAL_SEP → COOLDOWN
├── Recipe Management: Temp profile, RPM, gas, power, pO₂, precursor additions
├── Quality Gate: XRD dissociation, 3Y-TZP density, SiO₂ SSA
├── Precursor Management: Y₂O₃, B₂O₃, C inventory, addition scheduling
└── Phoenix Registry: Slug UUID, grade, downstream route (FOLLOW-16,21,32)

ZONE 8 PID (1 kHz) — PROD-10 Zone 8
├── Master: Drum wall temp (FBG median, 48 sensors) → Power setpoint
├── Slave 1: Resonance tracking (GaN inverter) → Frequency/phase (1 kHz ZVS)
├── Slave 2: POF level (slag height) → Feed rate
├── Slave 3: Gas analyzer (Ar, He, O₂, SiO) → MFC setpoints, condenser flow
├── Slave 4: Pyrometer (surface) → Temp cross-check
├── Slave 5: ZrO₂ probe (pO₂) → Ar/He ratio, getter status
├── Slave 6: Flash sinter cell (V, I, T) → Field profile, duration
├── Slave 7: Port 8A mold FBG (6 per mold) → N₂ quench flow
└── Slave 8: Port 8B condenser temp → Coolant flow

DISSOCIATION MONITOR (10 Hz)
├── READ MS_SiO₂ → p_SiO₂
├── TARGET p_SiO₂ = 10⁻³ atm
├── IF p_SiO₂ > 10⁻²: INCREASE Ar sweep, DECREASE power
├── IF p_SiO₂ < 10⁻⁴: DECREASE Ar sweep (SiO₂ re-deposition risk)
├── CALCULATE X_diss = 1 - (p_SiO₂_measured / p_SiO₂_initial)^(1/3)
├── IF X_diss < 0.95 at t=25 min: EXTEND dwell, ALERT

FLASH SINTER CONTROL (100 Hz)
├── READ V_cell, I_cell, T_pyrometer
├── TARGET: T=1800°C, E=300 V/cm, t=300s
├── RAMP: E = 100 + 200×(t/60) V/cm for t<60s
├── FLASH DETECTION: dI/dt > threshold → thermal runaway start
├── HOLD: E = 300 V/cm, PID on T_pyrometer
├── IF T > 1850°C: REDUCE E, ALERT
├── COOL: E = 0, N₂ quench profile

DUAL-PORT CAROUSEL CONTROL (10 Hz)
├── Port 8A (3Y-TZP): 2 molds × 10 kg, flash sinter sync
├── Port 8A (final): Al₂O₃/TiO₂/REE concentrate
├── Port 8B (SiO₂): Continuous condenser, no mold
├── Cool: N₂ quench profile per material
├── Demold/Stamp/LIBS/Registry: per PROD-08

SAFETY INTERLOCKS (Hardwired, <10 ms)
├── pO₂ > 10⁻¹⁰ atm → Emergency Ar flood, power cut
├── SiO > 10 ppm in off-gas → Condenser check, power cut
├── Temp > 2250°C → Power cut, Ar flood
├── Pressure > 1.3 bar → Vent, power cut
├── Vibration > 3 G → Power cut (lower RPM = lower G tolerance)
├── FBG comm loss > 100 ms → Power cut
├── Flash cell V > 200V or I > 600A → Power cut
├── Carousel position error > 1° → E-stop
└── O₂ area < 19.5% → Evacuation alarm, Ar purge
```

### 13.2 Key Control Algorithms

**Zircon Dissociation Control:**
```
X_diss_target = 0.95
p_SiO₂_setpoint = 10⁻³ atm
MEASURED_X_diss = 1 - (MS_SiO₂ / MS_SiO₂_initial)^(1/3)
ERROR_diss = X_diss_target - MEASURED_X_diss
IF ERROR_diss > 0.05 at t>20 min:
    EXTEND dwell by ERROR_diss × 600 s
    INCREASE power by 10%
    LOG to batch record
```

**Flash Sinter Detection:**
```
FLASH_DETECTED = (dI_cell/dt > 50 A/s) AND (T_pyrometer > 1750°C)
IF FLASH_DETECTED:
    LOG flash_time
    SWITCH to hold_mode (E=300 V/cm constant)
    TARGET_T = 1800°C
    PID_GAINS: Kp=0.5, Ki=0.01, Kd=0.1 (pre-tuned)
```

**REE/Al/Ti Separation Verification:**
```
IF Zone 8-4 active:
    READ XRF_residual → C_Al, C_Ti, C_REE, C_Zr
    IF C_Zr > 5% in residual: ZrO₂ carryover → ALERT, adjust Zone 8-3 duration
    IF C_REE < 5% in concentrate: REE loss → ALERT, check Zone 8-2 dissociation
```

```
├── **MAX Phase Self-Production**: Ti₃AlC₂ → MXene for EMI, energy storage
├── **Carbon Negative Potential**: Char → C for carbothermal → CO for Stage 7
└── **Zero Critical Mineral Imports**: Zr, Y, Ti, Al, Si, REE all domestic

SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS:
├── REE Price -30%:     Margin $4,800/batch (REE = 70% of external revenue)
├── Electricity +50%:   Margin $6,250/batch (energy = minor)
├── Y₂O₃ Price +100%:   Margin $6,260/batch (Y₂O₃ = minor)
├── ZrSiO₄ Feed -50%:   Margin $5,500/batch (3Y-TZP reduced)
└── **Most sensitive to: REE prices, ZrSiO₄ feed availability, drum lifetime**

CASCADE ECONOMIC INTEGRATION:
Stage 8 is the **keystone** of the Aegis-Forge economic model:
- Produces the drum material (ZrB₂-SiC) that enables the Forge to exist
- Produces the insulation (aerogel from SiO₂) that enables thermal efficiency
- Produces the REE oxides that enable magnet manufacturing (FOLLOW-33)
- Produces the MAX Phase (Ti₃AlC₂) for EMI shielding (Carrington hardening)
- **Without Stage 8, the Forge cannot build itself. With Stage 8, the Forge replicates.**
```

# PROD-22: Phoenix Protocol Integration
## 1. Phoenix Protocol Overview

### 1.1 Mission Statement

The Phoenix Protocol is the operational doctrine that transforms the Aegis-Forge I from a waste-processing machine into a **perpetual material engine**. Its mandate: **100% end-of-life (EOL) product return, zero-waste loop, and critical mineral sovereignty** for the Carrington Storm Motors (CSM) portfolio. Every Aegis product — from Embark wall panels to Faraday alarms to Phantom robots — is designed from inception to re-enter the Forge at end of service. The Protocol closes the loop between product retirement and seed material generation.

### 1.2 Strategic Imperatives

| Imperative | Description | KPI Target |
|------------|-------------|------------|
| **Take-Back Compliance** | 5-year warranty with recovery incentive drives return rate | >95% of CSM products by mass |
| **Material Sovereignty** | Eliminate external supply chain for Zr, REE, In, Co, Nb, W | 85% in-house/recycled by Year 5 |
| **Carbon Negativity** | MgO carbonation + avoided primary production sequesters CO₂ | -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL processed |
| **Economic Autonomy** | EOL revenue funds Phase 2-3 machine construction | $3.25M per 10,000 panels retired |
| **Traceability** | UUID chain from mine → Forge → product → return → Forge | Blockchain-anchored digital twin |

### 1.3 Protocol Architecture

The Phoenix Protocol operates as a **three-layer recursive system**:

```
Layer 1 — Collection & Disassembly (Depot Network)
    ↓ Feedstock Classification (Category A-D per PROD-13)
Layer 2 — Forge Re-Entry (Stage-by-Stage Material Routing)
    ↓ Product Regeneration (Hydromet, SPS, SHS, Solvolysis)
Layer 3 — Product Re-Manufacture (Assembly Line Integration)
    ↓ Product Deployment → End of Service → Layer 1
```

Each layer validates the next. Layer 1 output (classified feedstock) must meet Layer 2 re-entry specifications. Layer 2 output (regenerated seed materials) must meet Layer 3 production tolerances. Layer 3 products must be designed for Layer 1 disassembly. The recursion is the guarantee.

### 1.4 Design-for-Disassembly (DfD) Principles

Every Aegis product embeds DfD from CAD conception:

| DfD Principle | Implementation | Verification |
|---------------|----------------|--------------|
| **Modular Joints** | PEEK CF40 threaded inserts, ZrO₂ alignment pins | Torque-to-yield spec, ultrasonic inspect |
| **Material Segregation** | No overmolding, no adhesives between material classes | Visual + LIBS at disassembly |
| **Fastener Standardization** | Single PEEK CF40 M8×1.25 for all structural joints | Gauge check at depot |
| **Fluid Drain Ports** | Ti₃AlC₂ ball valves on all fluid circuits | Pressure decay test |
| **Component Labeling** | Laser-etched UUID + material code on every part >50g | LIBS reads code at disassembly |
| **Hazard Isolation** | Batteries, capacitors in dedicated cassettes (tool-free remove) | Depot scan verifies removal |

**DfD Compliance Metric:** Disassembly time ≤ 15 min/product (automated), ≤ 45 min (manual fallback).

### 1.5 Protocol Governance

**Phoenix Protocol Steering Committee (PPSC):**
- Chair: CSM VP Materials & Circularity
- Members: Forge Operations Director, Depot Network Lead, Hydromet Chief Engineer, Digital Twin Architect, Sustainability Officer, Legal/Compliance
- Meets: Monthly (operational), Quarterly (strategic)
- Authority: Approve blend ratio changes, new re-entry paths, depot expansions, protocol amendments

**Protocol Amendment Process:**
1. Change Request (CR) submitted via Git (PROD-38 Config Mgmt)
2. Impact Assessment: Mass balance, energy, safety, economics, schedule
3. PPSC Review: Technical feasibility + business case
4. Approval: Unanimous for safety, majority for ops/econ
5. Implementation: Staged rollout (1 Forge → 3 Forges → Fleet)
6. Validation: 100 batches at new spec before fleet deployment

**Version Control:** Protocol v1.0 (this document) → v1.x (operational tweaks) → v2.0 (major architecture change). All versions archived in Git with tagged releases.

## 2. Return Logistics Network

### 2.1 Collection Hub Topology

| Hub Tier | Count (Year 3) | Coverage Radius | Throughput | Function |

| **Secondary** | 12 | 500 km | 100 ton/yr | Pre-sort, discharge, crate, ship to Primary |
| **Tertiary** | 50+ | 100 km | 20 ton/yr | Consumer drop-off, installer return, warranty claim intake |

**Hub Equipment (Primary):**
- Automated disassembly cell (6-axis + vision, 15 min/product)
- Thermal solvolysis reactor (350°C, 2h, 500L Elium® recovery)
- Ultrasonic cleaning station (PEEK/ZrO₂ hardware)
- LIBS + XRF inline analyzer (composition verification)
- BFRP crate washer (closed-loop water, 99% recycle)

### 2.2 Transport Specification — DUNNAGE-FREE

All EOL material moves in **BFRP/Elium® crates** (CSMFAB-P001 spec):
- Crate dimensions: 1200×800×600 mm (Euro-pallet compatible)
- Mass: 18 kg empty, 500 kg loaded
- Stackable 4-high, forklift pockets, RFID + QR + Data Matrix
- Hermetic seal option (Ar backfill) for reactive fractions
- Crate life: 500 cycles → crushed → BFRP recycling (thermal solvolysis)

**No wood, cardboard, foam, or plastic dunnage.** Ever. The crate IS the packaging.

### 2.3 Collection Triggers

| Trigger | Mechanism | Incentive | SLA |
|---------|-----------|-----------|-----|
| **Warranty Return** | 5-yr CSM warranty requires return for full refund | 100% deposit refund + $50/panel | <30 days from claim |
| **Upgrade Swap** | Embark module replacement program | Trade-in credit toward Gen-II | <14 days scheduled |
| **Decommissioning** | Infrastructure EOL (poles, pipeline, rail) | Scrap value + carbon credit | Contract-defined |
| **Voluntary Return** | Consumer/owner drop-off at Tertiary hub | $25/panel store credit | Immediate |

### 2.4 Reverse Logistics Optimization

**Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) Solution:**
- **Algorithm**: Clarke-Wright savings + 2-opt local search
- **Objective**: Minimize Σ(distance × carbon intensity) subject to hub capacity
- **Fleet**: Electric Class 8 (500 km range) for Secondary→Primary; Diesel hybrid for Tertiary→Secondary
- **Load Consolidation**: Minimum 80% crate fill before dispatch
- **Backhaul**: Return empty crates + deliver virgin feedstock (BFRP crates, Ar cylinders)

**Network KPIs:**
- Average haul distance: 320 km (Primary←Secondary), 65 km (Secondary←Tertiary)
- Crate turnaround: 14 days (return → clean → redeploy)
- Carbon intensity: 0.08 kg CO₂e/ton-km (electric) vs. 0.22 (diesel)

## 4. Preprocessing at Depot

### 4.1 Disassembly Sequence (Automated Cell)

```
Step 1: Electronic/Optical Extraction (2 min)
    - Vision-guided 6-axis removes PCBs, displays, sensors, LoRa modules
    - Output: Electronics fraction → Stage 0 (AMLS) or refurbishment queue

Step 2: Hardware Removal (3 min)
    - PEEK CF40 fasteners, ZrO₂ ceramic bearings, Ti₃AlC₂ EMI shields
    - Ultrasonic clean (40 kHz, 60°C, 10 min) → inspect → re-use queue

Step 3: BFRP Structural Solvolysis (120 min batch)
    - Elium® resin depolymerization: 350°C, 2h, N₂ atmosphere, 15 bar
    - Monomer recovery: MMA >99%, glycol >98% → distillation → Elium® reformulation
    - Basalt fiber recovery: 95% yield, 15-20 μm diameter retained
    - Output: Clean fiber bundles → BFRP pultrusion (FOLLOW-05)

Step 4: Ceramic Core Processing (15 min)
    - ZrB₂-SiC panel cores: Jaw crush → ball mill (3-5 μm) → hydromet (H₂SO₄ leach)
    - ZrO₂/Si₃N₄ buffers: Separate stream → re-precipitation (3Y-TZP) or direct SPS
    - Output: Zr/Y hydroxide gel → calcination → 3Y-TZP powder (Stage 8 loop)

Step 5: Critical Mineral Glaze Recovery (30 min)
    - YInMn Blue (exterior): H₂SO₄ leach → ionic liquid [P₈₈₈₈][Cl] extraction
    - CoAl₂O₄ Cobalt Blue (interior): HCl dissolution → electroplating
    - Output: In 99.9% (YInMn), Y 98% (YSZ), Co 98% (electroplated)

Step 6: Fluid & Battery Drain (5 min)
    - MRF-140CG: Centrifugal separation → quality cert → re-fill
    - LiFePO₄: Full discharge → hydromet (LFP precursor recovery)
```

### 4.2 Depot Throughput & Economics

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Disassembly time** | 15 min/product (automated) |
| **Solvolysis batch** | 500 kg Elium®/batch, 4 batches/day |
| **Depot throughput (Primary)** | 2,000 products/day = 500 ton/yr |
| **Labor** | 4 operators + 1 supervisor/shift |
| **Energy** | 180 kWh/product (solvolysis dominant) |
| **Revenue per product** | $185 avg (In, Y, Co, Zr, fiber, monomer) |
| **Cost per product** | $42 (energy, labor, consumables) |
| **Net margin** | $143/product = $286K/day/Primary hub |

### 5.2 Blend Ratios — Virgin + Recycled Feed

The Forge operates on a **dynamic blend** to maintain slag chemistry and thermal stability:

| Feedstock Type | Blend Ratio (Mass) | Adjustment Logic |
|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Virgin e-waste (Cat A-C) | 50-70% | Baseline cascade feed |
| EOL Aegis products (Cat D1) | 20-30% | High-purity known composition |
| Structural BFRP (Cat D2) | 5-10% | Carbon + fiber supplement |
| Ceramic cores (Cat D3) | 3-8% | Zr/REE boost for Stage 8 |
| Mineral fractions (Cat D4) | 2-5% | Critical mineral spike |
| Electronics (Cat D5) | 5-10% | Cu/PM supplement for Stage 6 |
| Energy storage (Cat D6) | 1-3% | Li/Fe/P to Stage 3/7 |

**Blend Control:** Inline LIBS at shredder exit (PROD-11) measures elemental composition in real-time. MFC adjusts virgin feed rate to maintain target blend ±2%.

### 5.3 Re-Entry Quality Gates

Each re-entry stream passes through a **Quality Gate** before Forge admission:

| Gate | Location | Tests | Pass Criteria | Fail Action |
|------|----------|-------|---------------|-------------|
| **Gate 0** | Depot exit | Radiation, SoC, LIBS fingerprint | All pass | Quarantine, re-sort |
| **Gate 1** | Forge receiving | Weigh, dimension, moisture, LIBS | ±2% mass, <5% H₂O | Reject to depot |
| **Gate 2** | Pre-Stage 0 | PCB count, battery count, size | 0 batteries, <150mm | Manual remove |
| **Gate 3** | Pre-Stage 3 | Char carbon content, volatile matter | C >80%, VM <10% | Adjust blend |
| **Gate 4** | Pre-Stage 4 | In content, oxidation state | In >500 ppm, In⁰ >90% | Pre-reduce |
| **Gate 5** | Pre-Stage 5 | Al purity, Fe contamination | Al >99.5%, Fe <0.1% | Eddy current sort |
| **Gate 6** | Pre-Stage 6 | Cu purity, PM content | Cu >99.5%, PM <500 ppm | Adjust flux |
| **Gate 7** | Pre-Stage 7 | Fe grade, REE magnet presence | Fe >95%, magnet ID'd | Mag separate |
| **Gate 8** | Pre-Stage 8 | ZrO₂ content, REE oxide grade | ZrO₂ >60%, REE >20% | Re-crush/leach |

### 6.3 Reconciliation Protocol

**Daily Reconciliation (End of Shift):**

4. Automated script compares: Σ(Input) + Σ(Return) = Σ(Outputs) ± 2%

**Monthly Audit:**
- Third-party assay of 5% random slugs (umbilical samples)
- Mass balance closure report to CSM Board

## 7. Drum Material Circularity

### 7.1 ZrB₂-SiC Drum Life Cycle

```
NEW DRUM (Gen 1)
    │
    ├─→ 500 batches (90-min cycle each = 750 hr operation)
    │     └─→ FBG monitoring: wall thickness, thermal gradient, seal integrity
    │
    ├─→ End-of-Life Criteria:
    │     • Wall thinning >15% (ultrasonic)
    │     • Seal leak rate >10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s
    │     • FBG drift >±5°C uncorrectable
    │     • Crack detection (acoustic emission >threshold)
    │
    └─→ RETIREMENT → Phoenix Depot
          │
          ├─→ Crush → Ball Mill (3-5 μm)
          │
          ├─→ Hydrometallurgical Zr Recovery:
          │     H₂SO₄ leach (95°C, 4h) → Zr⁴⁺ in solution
          │     NH₄OH co-precipitation (with Y³⁺ from REE stream)
          │     → Zr-Y hydroxide gel → 120°C dry → 1200°C calcine (4h)
          │     → 3Y-TZP ZrO₂ powder (97% TD target)
          │
          ├─→ Carbothermal ZrB₂ Synthesis:
          │     ZrO₂ + B₂O₃ + 5C → ZrB₂ + 5CO (1800°C, 2h, Ar)
          │     OR SHS: Zr + 2B → ZrB₂ (1h, self-propagating)
          │
          └─→ Flash Sinter → NEW DRUM (Gen 2)
                (Same ZrB₂-SiC spec as PROD-04)
```

### 7.2 Drum Generation Mass Balance

| Generation | ZrB₂ Source | SiC Source | Yield | Cumulative Drums |
|------------|-------------|------------|-------|------------------|
| **Gen 1** | Commercial (external) | Commercial | 100% | 1 |
| **Gen 2-5** | Stage 8 ZrO₂ + Stage 3 B₂O₃/C | Stage 3 char | 99% | 5 |
| **Gen 6-15** | Stage 8 ZrO₂ (recycled) + Stage 3 B₂O₃/C | Stage 3 char + recycled drum crush | 98% | 15 |
| **Gen 16-31** | 100% recycled ZrB₂ + Stage 3 B₂O₃/C | 100% recycled SiC | 97% | 31 |

**Key Result:** 1 initial drum → 31 drum generations → 15,500 batches → 775,000 kg processed over facility lifetime. The Forge makes its own body from the waste it processes.

### 7.3 Quality Gates for Recycled Drum Material

| Parameter | Spec (Gen 1) | Spec (Gen 2+) | Test Method |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|-------------|
| **Density** | >5.9 g/cm³ | >5.85 g/cm³ | Archimedes |
| **B/Zr ratio** | 2.00±0.02 | 2.00±0.03 | ICP-OES |
| **Oxygen** | <0.5 wt% | <0.7 wt% | LECO |
| **Grain size** | 2-5 μm | 2-6 μm | SEM |
| **Flexural strength** | >450 MPa | >420 MPa | 4-pt bend |
| **Thermal shock** | 5 cycles 2200→25°C | 3 cycles | Quench test |

### 7.4 Drum Recycling Process Flow (Detailed)

```
RETIRED DRUM (500 batches)
         │
         ▼
Phoenix Depot Receiving
         │
         ▼
Non-Destructive Evaluation:
  • Ultrasonic wall thickness map (200 points)
  • FBG thermal history replay
  • Acoustic emission scan (crack map)
  • Helium leak test (all ports, seals)
         │
         ▼
Segregation Decision:
  ├─→ PRIME (wall >85%, no cracks) → Direct re-SPS (Gen +1)
  ├─→ STANDARD (wall 70-85%, minor cracks) → Crush → Hydromet (Gen +1)
  └─→ SCRAP (wall <70%, major cracks) → Crush → Hydromet (Gen +1, lower yield)
         │
         ▼ (for STANDARD/SCRAP)
Crushing Circuit:
  • Jaw crusher (50 mm) → Cone crusher (5 mm) → Ball mill (3-5 μm)
  • Argon atmosphere, -40°C dew point (prevent oxidation)
  • Throughput: 500 kg/hr per line
         │
         ▼
Hydrometallurgical Zr Recovery:
  • Reactor: BFRP/Elium®, 2000L, H₂SO₄ 2M, 95°C, 4h, stir 200 RPM
  • Leach efficiency: 96% Zr, 94% Y, 92% Si (reports to silica stream)
  • Solid residue: SiC (unleached) → filter → dry → SiC recycle stream
  • Filtrate: Zr⁴⁺, Y³⁺, Fe³⁺, Al³⁺, Ti⁴⁺ in solution
         │
         ▼
Selective Precipitation:
  1. pH 2.5 (NH₄OH): Fe³⁺, Al³⁺ → hydroxide (waste → Stage 7 slag)
  2. pH 5.5: Ti⁴⁺ → TiO₂·xH₂O (filter → Stage 8 TiO₂ stream)
  3. pH 8.0: Zr⁴⁺ + Y³⁺ → Zr-Y hydroxide gel (co-precipitate)
  4. pH 10.5: Residual REE → REE hydroxide (FOLLOW-15)
         │
         ▼
Gel Processing:
  • Filter press (BFRP plates, PEEK CF40 cloth) → 35% solids
  • Wash: 3× DI water (counter-current) → Cl⁻ <50 ppm, SO₄²⁻ <100 ppm
  • Dry: 120°C, 4h, N₂ atmosphere → free-flowing powder
  • Calcination: 1200°C, 4h, air → 3Y-TZP crystalline (97% theoretical)
         │
         ▼
Carbothermal ZrB₂ Synthesis (FOLLOW-32):
  • Mix: 3Y-TZP + B₂O₃ + 5C (molar 1:1:5) + 2% B₄C sintering aid
  • Press: 100 MPa → green density 55% TD
  • Furnace: Induction, 1800°C, 2h, Ar, graphite susceptor
  • Conversion: 98.5% → ZrB₂ + 5CO (gas captured → PROD-07)
  • Mill: 3-5 μm, narrow distribution (D90/D10 <2.5)
         │
         ▼
Flash Sintering (PROD-04 / FOLLOW-01):
  • 3Y-TZP + ZrB₂ composite → 1800°C, 300 V/cm, 5 min
  • 97% TD, 0.5 μm grain, ZrB₂ percolation network
  • Result: NEW DRUM (Gen N+1)
```

### 7.5 Drum Recycling Energy & Emissions

| Process Step | Energy (kWh/kg ZrB₂) | CO₂e (kg/kg) | Notes |
|--------------|---------------------|--------------|-------|
| Crushing & milling | 8 | 0.5 | Argon atmosphere |
| H₂SO₄ leach (95°C, 4h) | 12 | 0.8 | Steam heat recovery 60% |
| Precipitation & wash | 3 | 0.2 | Counter-current water |
| Calcination (1200°C, 4h) | 25 | 1.5 | NG-fired, 85% efficiency |
| Carbothermal (1800°C, 2h) | 45 | 2.8 | Induction, Ar, CO capture |
| Flash sinter (1800°C, 5 min) | 18 | 1.1 | 300 V/cm, 5 min |
| **TOTAL** | **111 kWh/kg** | **6.9 kg CO₂e/kg** | **vs. 280 kWh/kg virgin** |

**Carbon Advantage:** Recycled drum ZrB₂ = 6.9 kg CO₂e/kg vs. virgin 45 kg CO₂e/kg → **85% reduction**. At 500 kg/drum × 31 generations = 15,500 kg ZrB₂ saved per initial drum = **590 tCO₂e avoided per drum lineage**.

## 8. EMI Shielding Circularity (Ti₃AlC₂ MAX Phase)

### 8.1 MAX Phase Life Cycle

```
NEW Ti₃AlC₂ SHIELD (Gen 1)
    │
    ├─→ Product service life (10-20 yr typical)
    │
    ├─→ RETURN → Phoenix Depot
    │
    ├─→ Crush → Chloride-Thermal Extraction:
    │     Ti₃AlC₂ + 6Cl₂ → 3TiCl₄ + AlCl₃ + 2C (800°C, Cl₂)
    │     TiCl₄ purified → TiO₂ (hydrolysis) → Ti powder (Mg reduction)
    │     AlCl₃ → Al metal (electrolysis)
    │
    ├─→ Re-synthesis:
    │     3TiO₂ + Al₂O₃ + 14C → Ti₃AlC₂ + 11CO (1500°C, 4h, Ar)
    │     OR direct: 3Ti + Al + 2C → Ti₃AlC₂ (SHS, 1h)
    │
    └─→ NEW Ti₃AlC₂ SHIELD (Gen 2)
          (Same spec as PROD-09 actuators, PROD-36 EMI)
```

```
  • No composition change
         │

Re-certify:

  • Flexural strength >300 MPa
         │

RETURN TO SERVICE (Gen N, Life +50%)
```

# PROD-23: Control System Architecture
# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-23 Control System Architecture
## Williams / Keymaker / El Segundo Synthesis

---

### The Lock That Forges the Key

The Aegis-Forge I control system exists because **a 2200°C induction furnace cannot tolerate a single copper wire crossing its pressure boundary during a Carrington storm.** This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not negotiable — it is physics. A 5000 nT/s geomagnetic field induces >100 A/km in conductors. Inside the forge, that coupling destroys GaN gate drivers (6 V threshold), corrupts safety logic, and melts the ZrB₂-SiC drum.

The **empirical gap** (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between continuous-time control theory and discrete-time implementation under electromagnetic hostility. PROD-10 and PROD-03 establish the theoretical baseline: 8-zone Class E inverters, 100 kHz → 1 kHz, ZVS maintained by varactor tuning. But fabrication reality demands: (1) FBG sensors at 125 Hz each, 384 channels, reconstructed via 1 kHz thermal model because PMMA degrades >800°C; (2) PLL lock acquisition <50 ms while varactor updates 100× slower than GaN switching; (3) SIL-3 SIFs with 2oo3 voting on sensors that share cable trays, power supplies, and interrogators — physical independence ≠ functional independence.

The **fabrication fidelity gap** (Keymaker: Empirical Lock) is precisely this divergence: continuous phase control vs. 100× slower varactor actuation; point measurement at cold flange → inference of hot drum inner surface; common-cause failure modes that defeat 2oo3 voting.

---

### The Mathematical Key That Turns the Lock

The single computational primitive that generates the solution is the **discrete-time thermal-admittance model executed at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU:**

```
T_inner[k+1] = T_inner[k] + (Δt/ρcV) × (P_ind[k] - hA(T_inner[k] - T_flange[k]) - εσA(T_inner⁴[k] - T_surr⁴))
```

This one equation, discretized with Δt = 1 ms on ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr, <100 μs compute), is the **atomic computation** (Keymaker: Mathematical Key). Everything derives from it:
- Thermal PID setpoint → power command via inverse model + PID
- Resonance tracker → frequency/varactor via pre-computed LUT (PROD-10)
- Cascade feedforward → downstream stage setpoints with transport delay
- SIF trip logic → predicted T_inner 50 ms ahead → pre-emptive trip
- Digital twin sync → full state trajectory at 10 Hz for PROD-37

TSN latency spike (2.3 ms) → local OCXO on each node. Varactor saturation (28 V) → 8-bit cap bank + slag-level feedforward.

## Aegis-Forge I: Control System Architecture — Distributed Control, Safety Interlocks & Carrington Immunity
### Hierarchical FPGA/RTU/PLC/SCADA, SIL-3 SIS, TSN Network, GIC-Hardened OT
**Document Number:** CSMFAB000000000123 (PROD-23)
**Series:** Aegis-Forge Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator (TCIMS)
**Date:** November 2026
**Classification:** CSMFAB Internal — Engineering Specification

## 1. Control Architecture Overview

### 1.1 Design Philosophy

The Aegis-Forge I control system is a **four-level hierarchical distributed architecture** designed to operate in the most hostile electromagnetic environment on Earth: inside a 500 kW induction furnace at 2200°C, during a Carrington-class geomagnetic storm. Every design decision flows from three irreducible constraints:

1. **All-Dielectric Sensing & Actuation:** No copper wires cross the pressure boundary. All 480+ field devices communicate via PMMA POF optical fiber. This eliminates antenna effects for GIC/EMP.
2. **Deterministic Real-Time Control:** 1 kHz zone-level PID loops with resonance tracking require <1 ms jitter. Achieved via TSN (IEEE 802.1Qbv) time-aware scheduling on a dual-ring 1 Gbps optical network.
3. **SIL-3 Safety Integrity:** 24 safety instrumented functions with 2oo3 voting, <50 ms response, certified to IEC 61508/ISA-84.

### 1.2 Hierarchy Summary

| Level | Name | Hardware | Cycle Time | Scope | Key Functions |
|-------|------|----------|------------|-------|---------------|
| **L0** | **Cell (FPGA)** | Artix-7 FPGA (BFRP board) | 10 μs (100 kHz) | Single inverter leg | GaN gate drive, desat protection, ZVS tracking, current sense |
| **L1** | **Zone RTU** | ARM Cortex-A53 (8×, BFRP) | 1 ms (1 kHz) | One inductive zone | Thermal PID, resonance tracker, FBG acquisition, MFC control |
| **L2** | **Stage PLC** | IEC 61131-3 PLC (8×, rugged) | 10 ms (100 Hz) | One thermal stage | Cascade control, interlock logic, recipe management, carousel |
| **L3** | **Plant SCADA** | Linux workstation (dual, air-gapped) | 100 ms (10 Hz) | Full Forge | Historian, alarm mgmt, batch tracking, MES, digital twin |

### 3.3 Thermal PID Parameters (Per Zone)

| Zone | Stages | K<sub>p</sub> | K<sub>i</sub> (s⁻¹) | K<sub>d</sub> (s) | Anti-Windup | Feedforward |
|------|--------|---------------|---------------------|-------------------|-------------|-------------|
| Z1-2 | 1-2 | 0.8 | 0.02 | 0.5 | ±10% | Radiative + convective |
| Z3 | 3 | 1.0 | 0.03 | 0.8 | ±10% | + Latent heat (pyrolysis) |
| Z4-5 | 4-5 | 1.2 | 0.05 | 1.0 | ±10% | + Latent heat (melting) |
| Z6 | 6 | 1.5 | 0.08 | 1.2 | ±10% | + Latent heat (Cu) |
| Z7 | 7 | 1.8 | 0.10 | 1.5 | ±10% | + Latent heat (Fe) + hysteresis |
| Z8 | 8 | 2.0 | 0.15 | 2.0 | ±10% | + Radiative (T⁴ dominant) |

**Gain Scheduling:** Parameters interpolate based on T_setpoint (300-2200°C). At T < 400°C, K<sub>d</sub> = 0 (noise suppression).

### 3.4 Resonance Tracker (PLL) Design

The Class E inverter maintains ZVS by aligning the switch voltage zero-crossing with the gate turn-on instant. A software PLL runs at 100 Hz:

```
Phase Error:  φ_err = t(V_DS=0) - t(gate_on)

PLL Output:   ΔV_varactor = K_p_PLL × φ_err + K_i_PLL × ∫φ_err dt
              ΔCap_Bank   = round(ΔV_varactor / V_per_step)  (coarse)

Gains:        K_p_PLL = 0.05 V/ns,  K_i_PLL = 500 V/s
Lock Range:   ±5% of nominal frequency
Acquisition:  <50 ms from cold start
```

**FPGA Interface:** The RTU sends varactor bias (16-bit DAC) and cap bank select (6-bit GPIO) to the Cell FPGA via PMMA POF. The FPGA updates the hardware within 10 μs.

### 3.5 FBG Acquisition & Processing

```
FBG Interrogator (per Zone RTU):
├── VCSEL: 650-850 nm sweep, 1 kHz triangle wave
├── WDM: 8-channel thin-film filter (20 nm spacing)
├── TDM: 1×6 PMMA splitter per wavelength
├── Detection: Balanced InGaAs PIN, 2 MHz BW
├── Processing: Peak detection (centroid), λ → T conversion
│   T = (λ_measured - λ_ref) / 0.15 nm/°C  (PMMA FBG sensitivity)
├── Output: 48 temperatures @ 125 Hz each (6 per TDM channel)
└── Health: SNR >20 dB, peak width <0.5 nm, no missing channels
```

**Fault Handling:** If >10 sensors in a zone report invalid data → RTU limits zone power to 50%, raises SCADA alarm, logs event.

### 4.2 Stage Control Functions

Each Stage PLC manages the complete thermal stage operation:

| Function | Description | Cycle |
|----------|-------------|-------|
| **Cascade Temperature Control** | Receives T_setpoint from SCADA, sends zone power commands to RTUs | 10 ms |
| **Interlock Logic** | Evaluates 24 SIL-3 + 12 SIL-2 + 36 SIL-1 conditions per stage | 1 ms (SIS) |
| **Recipe Management** | Loads Stage recipe (temp profile, durations, gas flows) from SCADA | On batch start |
| **Carousel Control** | Indexes 16-position slug mold carousel, triggers quench/demold | Event-driven |
| **Flux Injection** | Controls Na₂CO₃/NaCl/KCl/cryolite feed rates per stage recipe | 10 ms |
| **Gas Atmosphere** | Manages Ar/He/H₂/N₂/CO/CO₂ MFCs to maintain pO₂ < 10⁻¹⁵ atm | 10 ms |
| **Composition Feedback** | Receives XRF/LIBS/mass spec data, adjusts setpoints | 100 ms |
| **Digital Twin Sync** | Publishes stage state to Kafka (OPC-UA) for PROD-37 | 100 ms |

### 4.3 Cascade Control Strategy

The 8 stages form a **cascade control hierarchy** with feedforward between stages:

```
Stage 0 (AMLS) ──► Stage 1 (Drying) ──► Stage 2 (Polymer) ──► Stage 3 (Pyrolysis)
     │                │                   │                    │
     ▼                ▼                   ▼                    ▼
Feed composition → Moisture → Polymer type → Char yield → Gas composition
     │                │                   │                    │
     └────────────────┴───────────────────┴────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                    STAGE 4 (Low-Temp Metals)
                              │
                              ▼
                    STAGE 5 (Aluminum Window)
                              │
                              ▼
                    STAGE 6 (Copper & PM)
                              │
                              ▼
                    STAGE 7 (Ferrous Cascade)
                              │
                              ▼
                    STAGE 8 (Mineral/Zircon)
```

**Feedforward Parameters (Passed Downstream):**
- Stage 0→1: Liberation index (LI), particle size distribution
- Stage 1→2: Residual moisture, organics composition
- Stage 2→3: Polymer melt viscosity, HCl generation rate
- Stage 3→4: Char yield, fixed carbon, inorganic composition
- Stage 4→5: In/Pb/Sn/Zn removed, PM captured, residue analysis
- Stage 5→6: Al removed, Mg content, dross composition
- Stage 6→7: Cu removed, PM grade, Fe/REE in residue
- Stage 7→8: Slag composition (B=1.2, MgO/Al₂O₃=1.5), FeO, REE oxides

### 4.4 Interlock Logic (Per Stage)

Each stage implements a **Safety Instrumented Function (SIF)** table:

| SIF Tag | Description | SIL | Sensors (2oo3) | Actuators | Response |
|---------|-------------|-----|----------------|-----------|----------|
| SIF-XX-01 | Drum over-temp (any FBG > T_lim) | 3 | 3× FBG/zone | All zone inverters OFF | <50 ms |
| SIF-XX-02 | Vessel over-pressure (>5 bar) | 3 | 3× Pressure | Emergency vent, inverters OFF | <50 ms |
| SIF-XX-03 | Atmosphere breach (pO₂ > 10⁻⁶ atm) | 3 | 3× ZrO₂ pO₂ | N₂ purge, inverters OFF | <50 ms |
| SIF-XX-04 | Cooling water loss (flow < 10 L/min) | 3 | 3× Flow | Graceful power ramp to 20% | <100 ms |
| SIF-XX-05 | FBG comms loss (>10 sensors/zone) | 2 | RTU heartbeat | Zone power limited to 50% | <500 ms |
| SIF-XX-06 | Drum rotation loss (<10 RPM) | 2 | 2× Encoder | Inverters OFF, drum coast | <100 ms |
| SIF-XX-07 | Ground fault (NGR > 5 A) | 3 | NGR monitor | All inverters OFF, isolate | <50 ms |
| SIF-XX-08 | GIC event (grid dV/dt > threshold) | 2 | Grid monitor | Ride-through mode | <10 ms |
| SIF-XX-09 | Port valve fail (position mismatch) | 2 | Valve FBG | Block stage advance | <500 ms |
| SIF-XX-10 | Carousel jam (index timeout) | 2 | Position sensor | Hold stage, alarm | <1 s |

**Voting Logic:** 2oo3 (two-out-of-three) for SIL-3. Sensors are physically separated (different angular positions on drum).

## 7. Carrington GIC Immunity — EMP-Hardened OT

### 7.1 Threat Model

| Phenomenon | Parameter | Standard |
|------------|-----------|----------|
| **GIC (Geomagnetic)** | dB/dt = 5000 nT/s, 100 A/km induced | IEEE Std 1656 |
| **E1 HEMP** | 50 kV/m, 1 ns rise, 100 MHz bandwidth | IEC 61000-2-9 |
| **E2 HEMP** | 1-10 kV/m, 1 μs-1 ms, similar to lightning | IEC 61000-4-25 |
| **E3 HEMP** | Slow (1-100 s), quasi-DC, like GIC | IEC 61000-4-34 |
| **Surface Charging** | >10 kV (space environment) | MIL-STD-1857 |

### 7.2 Hardening Architecture

| Layer | Mitigation | Implementation |
|-------|------------|----------------|
| **Physical** | Faraday cage RTUs | BFRP housing + conductive YInMn glaze (σ = 10⁴ S/m) |
| **Power** | Floating secondary | Isolation transformers (Δ-Y), no earth reference |
| **Power** | NGR limiting | 5 A high-resistance grounding |
| **Power** | Surge protection | GDT (3 kA) + MOV at transformer primary |
| **Signal** | All-dielectric comms | PMMA POF — zero conductive path |
| **Signal** | Optical isolation | No copper crossing pressure boundary |
| **Signal** | Common-mode choke | Nanocrystalline on any residual copper |
| **Network** | TSN dual-ring | No single point of failure, deterministic |
| **Cyber** | Air-gap + data diode | Unidirectional to IT, no external IP |
| **Firmware** | Signed boot | Secure boot on all FPGA/RTU/PLC |

### 7.3 GIC Ride-Through Mode

When grid dV/dt > threshold (detected by dedicated monitor):

1. **Detection** (1 ms): Grid monitor FPGA triggers interrupt
2. **Transition** (5 ms): Inverters switch to "ride-through" — maintain DC link from bus capacitors
3. **Isolation** (10 ms): Physical contactors open (vacuum, BFRP housed) — Forge islanded
4. **Sustain** (indefinite): LiFePO₄ backup (100 Wh) powers control system; drum coast-down
5. **Reconnect** (auto): When grid stable >30 s, pre-charge → contactor close → resume

**Validation:** Tested at up to 100 A/m simulated field (Helmholtz coil facility). No protection trips, no data loss.

## 8. Network Architecture — TSN Deterministic Ethernet

### 8.1 TSN Configuration (IEEE 802.1Qbv)

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Topology** | Dual-ring (counter-rotating), 8 RTUs + 8 PLCs + 2 SCADA |
| **Speed** | 1 Gbps (1000BASE-T1 automotive, PMMA POF media) |
| **Scheduling** | Time-Aware Shaper (TAS), 1 ms cycle, 8 time slices |
| **Time Slices** | Slice 0: SIS (SIL-3), Slice 1: RTU control, Slice 2: PLC, Slice 3: SCADA, Slice 4-7: Best effort |
| **Latency** | <100 μs (SIS), <500 μs (RTU), <1 ms (PLC), <5 ms (SCADA) |
| **Jitter** | <10 μs (SIS), <50 μs (RTU), <100 μs (PLC) |
| **Redundancy** | FRER (Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability) |
| **VLANs** | VLAN 10: SIS, VLAN 20: RTU, VLAN 30: PLC, VLAN 40: SCADA, VLAN 99: Mgmt |
| **Sync** | IEEE 802.1AS (PTP), <1 μs accuracy |

### 8.2 Time-Aware Schedule (1 ms Cycle)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         TSN 1 ms CYCLE (GCL - Gate Control List)            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  0.000 ms  │►│ SIS (SIL-3)          │ Gate Open: VLAN 10                   │
│            │   │ 2oo3 voting frames │ Duration: 200 μs                     │
│            │   │ Priority: 7        │                                      │
│  0.200 ms  │►│ RTU Control        │ Gate Open: VLAN 20                   │
│            │   │ PID commands, FBG  │ Duration: 300 μs                     │
│            │   │ Priority: 6        │                                      │
│  0.500 ms  │►│ PLC Data           │ Gate Open: VLAN 30                   │
│            │   │ Cascade setpoints  │ Duration: 200 μs                     │
│            │   │ Priority: 5        │                                      │
│  0.700 ms  │►│ SCADA / Mgmt       │ Gate Open: VLAN 40/99                │
│            │   │ OPC-UA, Historian  │ Duration: 200 μs                     │
│            │   │ Priority: 3-4      │                                      │
│  0.900 ms  │►│ Guard Band         │ Gate Closed (all)                    │
│            │   │ Sync margin        │ Duration: 100 μs                     │
│  1.000 ms  │   CYCLE REPEATS                                                │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 8.3 Network Health Monitoring

| Metric | Threshold | Action |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| **Frame loss (SIS)** | >0 frames/hr | Immediate alarm, path switch |
| **Latency (RTU)** | >500 μs | Degrade to 500 Hz control |
| **PTP offset** | >1 μs | Alarm, switch to holdover OCXO |
| **FRER mismatch** | >0.1% | Path degradation alert |
| **Link utilization** | >80% | Traffic shaping, alarm |

## 10. Cyber-Physical Security — Air-Gapped OT

### 10.1 Security Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         CYBER-PHYSICAL SECURITY ZONES                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  IT NETWORK (Enterprise)                                                    │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ ERP, Email, Web, Historian (read-only), Engineer Workstations      │   │
│  └────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                   │                                         │
│                                   ▼ UNIDIRECTIONAL DATA DIODE               │
│                                   (TX-only fiber, RX physically cut)       │
│                                   │                                         │
│  OT NETWORK (Forge) — AIR-GAPPED                                            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ SCADA, PLCs, RTUs, SIS, FPGAs, FBG Interrogators                   │   │
│  │ NO external IP, NO wireless, NO USB ports, NO Bluetooth            │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
│  DMZ (Data Historian Replica)                                               │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ InfluxDB replica (read-only), MQTT broker (IT→OT blocked)          │   │
│  │ Updated via data diode (1-way: OT → IT)                             │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 10.2 Defense in Depth

| Layer | Controls |
|-------|----------|
| **Perimeter** | Physical air-gap, data diode, no internet connectivity |
| **Network** | TSN VLAN segmentation, MACsec encryption, port security |
| **Host** | Immutable OS (NixOS), signed firmware, no package manager runtime |
| **Application** | Role-based access (Operator/Engineer/Safety/Admin), MFA (hardware token) |
| **Data** | Encryption at rest (AES-256), blockchain-anchored audit log |
| **Monitoring** | ML anomaly detection (FOLLOW-29), behavioral baselines, zero-trust |

### 10.3 Anomaly Detection (FOLLOW-29 Integration)

- **Model:** LSTM autoencoder trained on 6 months normal operation
- **Inputs:** All 480+ sensor streams, network traffic, PLC scan times
- **Output:** Anomaly score (0-1), alert if >0.95 for >10 s
- **Response:** Auto-isolate affected VLAN, alert SOC, log full context
- **False Positive Rate:** <0.1% (validated on 10,000 batches)

| Priority | Color | Response | Examples |

| **Critical (SIL)** | Red flashing | Immediate, auto-action | SIF trip, over-temp, over-pressure |
| **High** | Red | <1 min acknowledgment | Zone deviation >10°C, FBG loss |
| **Medium** | Yellow | <10 min acknowledgment | Efficiency <95%, flow deviation |
| **Low** | Blue | <1 hr acknowledgment | Maintenance due, log full |
| **Info** | Gray | Logged only | Recipe change, batch complete |

### 11.3 Training Simulator

- **Platform:** Digital twin (PROD-37) in "shadow mode" — same models, simulated sensors
- **Scenarios:** Normal startup, feedstock variations, SIF trips, GIC event, cyber intrusion
- **Certification:** Operators must complete 40 hrs sim + 20 hrs supervised before solo
- **Recertification:** Annual (8 hrs sim + 1 emergency drill)

### The Lock That Forges the Key

The Aegis-Forge I control system exists because **a 2200°C induction furnace cannot tolerate a single copper wire crossing its pressure boundary during a Carrington storm.** This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not negotiable — it is physics. A 5000 nT/s geomagnetic field induces >100 A/km in conductors. Inside the forge, that coupling destroys GaN gate drivers (6 V threshold), corrupts safety logic, and melts the ZrB₂-SiC drum.

The **empirical gap** (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between continuous-time control theory and discrete-time implementation under electromagnetic hostility. PROD-10 and PROD-03 establish the theoretical baseline: 8-zone Class E inverters, 100 kHz → 1 kHz, ZVS maintained by varactor tuning. But fabrication reality demands: (1) FBG sensors at 125 Hz each, 384 channels, reconstructed via 1 kHz thermal model because PMMA degrades >800°C; (2) PLL lock acquisition <50 ms while varactor updates 100× slower than GaN switching; (3) SIL-3 SIFs with 2oo3 voting on sensors that share cable trays, power supplies, and interrogators — physical independence ≠ functional independence.

The **fabrication fidelity gap** (Keymaker: Empirical Lock) is precisely this divergence: continuous phase control vs. 100× slower varactor actuation; point measurement at cold flange → inference of hot drum inner surface; common-cause failure modes that defeat 2oo3 voting.

The single computational primitive that generates the solution is the **discrete-time thermal-admittance model executed at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU:**

```
T_inner[k+1] = T_inner[k] + (Δt/ρcV) × (P_ind[k] - hA(T_inner[k] - T_flange[k]) - εσA(T_inner⁴[k] - T_surr⁴))
```

This one equation, discretized with Δt = 1 ms on ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr, <100 μs compute), is the **atomic computation** (Keymaker: Mathematical Key). Everything derives from it:

# PROD-24: Thermal Modeling and Simulation
# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-24 Thermal Modeling & Simulation
## Williams / Keymaker / El Segundo Synthesis

---

### The Lock That Forges the Key

The Aegis-Forge I thermal model exists because **induction heating power is a nonlinear function of the very temperature it creates, and the material properties governing both are themselves strong functions of temperature.** This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not a modeling preference — it is physics. At Stage 7, Fe ferromagnetic permeability drops from 200 to 1 at 770°C, collapsing induction power by 60%. At Stage 8, the 2000°C radial gradient in the 35 mm ZrB₂-SiC drum wall combines thermal stress (220 MPa) with centrifugal stress (185 MPa at 500 RPM) to exceed the 350 MPa allowable — but only when computed together with temperature-dependent $E(T)$, $\alpha(T)$. At Stage 4, gas convection cooling of In droplets ($h_{conv}$) determines whether centrifugal separation succeeds — and $h_{conv}$ is an output of the CFD, not an input.

The **empirical gap** (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between single-physics simulations and integrated cascade test data. PROD-10 inverter tests showed Zone 7 power collapsing from 350 kW at 1100°C to 140 kW at 1300°C — a 60% drop invisible to constant-$\mu_r$ models. PROD-04 first-article drum FA-01 showed 385 MPa von Mises at Liner B — 35 MPa over allowable — missed by linear superposition of thermal + centrifugal. PROD-17 batch 1 achieved 97.2% In recovery vs. 99.5% predicted — the gap traced to $h_{conv}$ being 2× higher than assumed.

The **fabrication fidelity gap** (Keymaker: Empirical Lock) is precisely this divergence: fixed-property EM models vs. temperature-dependent ferromagnetic coupling; superposition of linear analyses vs. nonlinear combined loading; assumed convection coefficients vs. CFD-resolved gas flow in a rotating drum. Every lock is a coupling that was assumed negligible but measured significant.

---

### The Mathematical Key That Turns the Lock

The single computational primitive that generates the solution is the **discrete-time thermal-admittance operator evaluated at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU — the same primitive that drives the control system (PROD-23):**

$$
\mathcal{T}[T_{inner}, T_{flange}, P_{ind}, h, \epsilon] : \quad T_{inner}[k+1] = T_{inner}[k] + \frac{\Delta t}{\rho c V} \left( P_{ind}[k] - h A (T_{inner}[k] - T_{flange}[k]) - \epsilon \sigma A (T_{inner}^4[k] - T_{surr}^4) \right)
$$

This one equation, discretized with $\Delta t = 1$ ms on ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr, <100 $\mu$s), is the **atomic computation** (Keymaker: Mathematical Key). Everything derives from it:
- **Full FEA:** The operator is the *reduced-order model* of the 3D FEA. FEA *computes* $\rho c V(T)$, $h A(T)$, $\epsilon \sigma A(T)$; the operator *executes* them at control speed.
- **EM-Thermal Coupling:** $P_{ind}[k]$ is computed by EM solver using $\rho(T_{inner}[k])$, $\mu_r(T_{inner}[k])$. Fixed-point iteration $\mathcal{T} \circ \mathcal{E}$ *is* the coupling.
- **Cascade CFD:** $h$ is not constant — it is $\mathcal{C}[\omega, T, P, X]$. The operator *queries* CFD at 10 Hz.
- **Stage Models:** Each stage is $\mathcal{T}$ with stage-specific $P_{ind}(t)$, $h(t)$, $\epsilon(t)$, moving boundary $m_{charge}(t)$.
- **Transient Cycling:** Operator integrates over 300 min. Fatigue damage from $T(t)$ history.
- **V&V:** Code verification validates *discretization* of $\mathcal{T}$. Solution verification validates *convergence* of $\mathcal{T} \circ \mathcal{E} \circ \mathcal{C}$.
- **UQ:** Sobol indices measure sensitivity of $\mathcal{T}$ outputs to 20 inputs.
- **ROM:** POD-Galerkin ROM *is* projection of $\mathcal{T}$ onto 12 modes.
- **Scaling:** Dimensionless groups (Fo, Re, Pe, Nu, $\delta/d$, G) are non-dimensional $\mathcal{T}$.

**Theory→History validation** (Keymaker: Turn): The operator predicts CSMFAB0108 test data within measurement uncertainty — FA-01 drum stress 385 MPa predicted vs. 325 MPa measured; Zone 7 power 142 kW predicted vs. 140 kW measured; vessel outer surface 150°C predicted vs. 148°C measured.

**History→Theory correction** (Keymaker: Turn): Curie transition width narrowed from 25°C to 8°C (sigmoid $\mu_r(T)$). $\alpha(T)$ piecewise correction (5.8→6.5×10⁻⁶/K at 1000°C) captured Liner B stress exactly. Aerogel $k(T)$ updated from guarded hot plate data. CFD-coupled $h_{conv}$ closed In recovery gap. Dual-basis ROM (thermal + structural modes) reduced stress error from 4.2 MPa to 1.1 MPa.

The mathematical key **absorbs history** — each anomaly tightens a correlation or adds a coupling to $\mathcal{T}$, but the operator structure remains invariant.

The thermal model observes its own fabrication through **four nested metrology loops** (El Segundo: Mirror):

1. **Microsecond (FEA EM Solver):** Field residual $\|\nabla \times (\nu \nabla \times A) + \sigma \partial A/\partial t - J_s\|_2 < 10^{-6}$; energy balance (Poynting theorem) error < 1%; ZVS indicator $\phi_{err} < 5$ ns. The solver *verifies Maxwell's equations at every frequency step*.

3. **Aerogel Performance Audit:** Vessel outer surface trend from FBG strain (thermal expansion proxy). Compute effective $\lambda_{aerogel}$ from $q = \lambda A \Delta T/L$. If $\lambda > 0.012$ W/m·K → replacement. Non-monotonic degradation requires context. The operator *witnesses the insulation aging*.

4. **ROM Calibration Review:** PROD-37 reports ROM error statistics monthly. Model engineer reviews error by stage, Sobol indices. New parameter in top-5? Retraining batch selection — excluding anomalies is judgment. The operator *witnesses the model learning*.

**Automation computes; humans validate at boundaries of consequence.** HMI presents exactly the comparison plots needed — FEA vs. thermocouples, power vs. reference, temperature trend vs. degradation limit, ROM error heatmap.

### Multi-Physics Framework, 50+ Material Properties, V&V Plan, ROM for Digital Twin
**Document Number:** CSMFAB000000000124 (PROD-24)

## 1. Multi-Physics Framework Overview

### 1.1 Design Philosophy

The Aegis-Forge I thermal model is a **four-way coupled multi-physics framework** that resolves the simultaneous electromagnetic, thermal, structural, and fluid dynamics phenomena governing the 8-stage thermal cascade. This is not a collection of separate analyses — it is a single computational primitive that captures the irreducible coupling between induction heating and material transformation.

**Irreducible Couplings (The Lock):**
- **EM → Thermal:** Induction power $P_{ind} = \frac{\pi^2 B^2 d^2 f^2 V}{6\rho}$ (non-mag) or $\frac{\pi B^2 f V}{\mu}$ (ferromagnetic) depends on temperature-dependent $\rho(T)$ and $\mu_r(T)$
- **Thermal → EM:** $\rho(T)$ increases 3-5× from RT to melting; $\mu_r$ drops from 200→1 at 770°C Curie transition
- **Thermal → Structural:** 2000°C radial gradient → 400 MPa thermal stress in 35 mm ZrB₂-SiC drum wall
- **Structural → Fluid:** Drum rotation (0-500 RPM) + centrifugal stratification → phase separation physics
- **Fluid → Thermal:** Gas convection coefficients $h(T, v, P)$ depend on flow regime in rotating drum

**The Single Computational Primitive (The Key):**
```
T_inner[k+1] = T_inner[k] + (Δt/ρcV) × (P_ind[k] - hA(T_inner[k] - T_flange[k]) - εσA(T_inner⁴[k] - T_surr⁴))
```
Discretized at Δt = 1 ms on Zone RTU (PROD-23). This is the atomic computation — all FEA, CFD, and ROM derive from it.

### 1.2 Physics Domains & Coupling Strategy

| Domain | Governing Equations | Solver | Coupling Variables | Update Rate |
|--------|---------------------|--------|-------------------|-------------|
| **EM (Induction)** | Maxwell's equations (quasi-static) + Circuit | ANSYS Maxwell 3D / Custom FEA | $P_{ind}(x,y,z,t)$, $B(x,y,z,t)$ | 100 Hz (RTU) |
| **Thermal (Transient)** | $\rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t} = \nabla \cdot (k \nabla T) + Q_{gen}$ | ANSYS Transient Thermal / Custom | $T(x,y,z,t)$, $h_{eff}(t)$ | 1 kHz (RTU) |
| **Structural (Thermo-Mechanical)** | $\nabla \cdot \sigma + f = 0$, $\sigma = C : (\epsilon - \alpha \Delta T)$ | ANSYS Mechanical | $\sigma(x,y,z,t)$, $\epsilon(x,y,z,t)$ | 100 Hz (PLC) |
| **Fluid (Gas-Solid CFD)** | Navier-Stokes + Lagrangian particle tracking | ANSYS Fluent / OpenFOAM | $v(x,y,z,t)$, $h_{conv}(t)$, RTD | 10 Hz (SCADA) |

**Coupling Strategy:**
- **Weak coupling (EM ↔ Thermal):** Staggered iteration with Aitken relaxation (ω = 0.7). Converged when $|T^{n+1} - T^n| < 0.1°C$ per zone
- **One-way coupling (Thermal → Structural):** Thermal load mapped to structural mesh at 100 Hz
- **Weak coupling (Structural → Fluid):** Drum deformation updates CFD wall boundary at 10 Hz
- **One-way coupling (Fluid → Thermal):** Convection coefficients $h_{conv}$ mapped to thermal mesh at 10 Hz

### 1.3 Time Scale Separation

| Process | Time Constant | Model Fidelity | Application |
|---------|---------------|----------------|-------------|
| EM wave propagation | 10 ns | Quasi-static (1 kHz RTU) | Inverter resonance |
| Thermal diffusion (drum wall) | 1-10 s | 1D transient (1 kHz RTU) | PID control |
| Thermal diffusion (charge) | 10-300 s | 2D axisymmetric (100 Hz PLC) | Stage cascade |
| Structural response | 10 ms | Linear elastic (100 Hz PLC) | Stress limits |
| Gas convection | 1-10 s | RANS (10 Hz SCADA) | Atmosphere control |
| Particle settling | 10-100 s | Lagrangian (10 Hz SCADA) | Separation efficiency |
| Batch cycle | 3.5-5 hr | Reduced-order (10 Hz SCADA) | Digital twin |

## 3. Electromagnetic-Thermal FEA (Induction Zones)

### 3.1 EM Model Formulation

**Governing Equations (Quasi-Static Maxwell):**
$$\nabla \times (\nu \nabla \times A) + \sigma \frac{\partial A}{\partial t} = J_s$$
$$\nu = 1/\mu = 1/(\mu_0 \mu_r(T))$$

Where $A$ = magnetic vector potential, $\nu$ = reluctivity, $\sigma$ = electrical conductivity, $J_s$ = source current density.

**Boundary Conditions:**
- Outer boundary: Magnetic insulation ($\mathbf{n} \times A = 0$)
- Coil terminals: Current excitation $I(t) = I_{rms}\sqrt{2}\sin(2\pi f t)$
- Symmetry: 1/8 model (45° sector) with periodic BCs

**Mesh Strategy:**
- Air gap (15 mm): 1.5 mm max element, 3 layers normal to B-field
- Drum wall (35 mm): 2 mm elements, 10 layers through thickness
- Coil windings: 3 mm elements, explicit turn resolution
- Far field: 10 mm growing to 50 mm
- **Total DOF:** ~1.2M per zone (8 zones = 9.6M, parallelized)

### 3.2 Coil-Drum Mutual Inductance Matrix

The 8-zone coil bank is modeled as a coupled inductor system:

$$\mathbf{V} = (j\omega\mathbf{L} + \mathbf{R})\mathbf{I} + \mathbf{M}\frac{d\mathbf{I}}{dt}$$

Where $\mathbf{L}$ = self-inductance matrix (8×8), $\mathbf{M}$ = mutual inductance matrix.

| Zone Pair | Mutual Inductance (μH) | Coupling Coefficient |
|-----------|------------------------|---------------------|
| Adjacent (Z4-Z5) | 2.1 | 0.18 |
| Next-adjacent (Z4-Z6) | 0.6 | 0.05 |
| Separated (Z1-Z8) | 0.08 | 0.007 |

**Key finding:** Cross-zone coupling <5% for adjacent zones, <1% for non-adjacent. Decoupled PID control (PROD-23) is valid. Resonance tracking per zone (PROD-10) compensates for mutual loading.

### 3.3 Eddy Current Distribution & Skin Depth Validation

**Analytical Skin Depth (PROD-10):**
$$\delta = \sqrt{\frac{2\rho}{\omega\mu}}$$

**FEA Validation at Stage 6 (Cu, 5 kHz, 1085°C):**
| Location | Analytical δ | FEA δ (effective) | Error |
|----------|--------------|-------------------|-------|
| Drum inner surface | 1.0 mm | 1.05 mm | +5% |
| Drum mid-wall | 1.0 mm | 0.95 mm | -5% |
| Charge surface (Cu) | 1.0 mm | 1.1 mm | +10% |

**Temperature-Dependent Coupling:**
At Stage 7 (Fe, 2 kHz, 1200°C): $\mu_r$ drops from 200 → 1 at 770°C. FEA shows power density drops 40% at Curie transition — captured by RTU resonance tracker (PROD-23 Section 3.4).

### 3.4 EM-Thermal Coupling Iteration

**Coupling Loop (per RTU cycle, 1 ms):**
1. Thermal model provides $T(x,y,z)$ at drum wall
2. Update $\rho(T)$, $\mu_r(T)$ in EM model
3. Solve EM → $P_{ind}(x,y,z)$
4. Map $P_{ind}$ to thermal model as $Q_{gen}$
5. Solve thermal → new $T(x,y,z)$
6. Check convergence: $\max|T^{n+1} - T^n| < 0.1°C$

**Aitken Relaxation:**
$$\omega^{n+1} = -\omega^n \frac{(T^{n+1}-T^n)^T(T^n-T^{n-1})}{|T^{n+1}-T^n|^2}$$
Clamped to [0.3, 1.0]. Typical convergence: 3-5 iterations per RTU cycle.

### 3.5 Induction Power Validation (vs. PROD-10 Measurements)

| Zone | Stage | FEA Power (kW) | PROD-10 Measured (kW) | Error |
|------|-------|----------------|------------------------|-------|
| Z1 | 1 | 48 | 50 | -4% |
| Z3 | 3 | 78 | 80 | -2.5% |
| Z5 | 5 | 152 | 150 | +1.3% |
| Z7 | 7 | 342 | 350 | -2.3% |
| Z8 | 8 | 495 | 500 | -1% |

**Validation metric:** All zones within ±5% — meets ASME V&V 40 validation threshold.

## 4. Drum Thermal-Structural FEA

### 4.1 Thermal Model — 2000°C Radial Gradient

**Geometry:** 1/8 sector (45°), 800 mm length, 35 mm wall, 3 liner zones, 8 ports
**Mesh:** 2 mm hex elements, 15 layers through wall, refined at port cutouts
**Boundary Conditions:**
- Inner surface: $q'' = \epsilon\sigma(T_{drum}^4 - T_{charge}^4) + h(T_{drum} - T_{charge})$ + $P_{ind}(z)$
- Outer surface: $T = T_{aerogel\_interface}$ (from vessel model)
- Port cutouts: Convection to gas ($h = 500$ W/m²·K)
- Ends: Insulated (adiabatic)

**Steady-State Results (Stage 8, 2200°C inner):**
| Location | Temperature (°C) | Gradient (°C/mm) |
|----------|------------------|------------------|
| Inner surface (ID) | 2200 | - |
| Liner B interface (10 mm) | 1850 | 35 |
| Mid-wall | 1250 | 17 |
| Liner C interface (30 mm) | 750 | 14 |
| Outer surface (OD) | 700 | - |

### 4.2 Structural Model — Combined Loading

**Load Cases (Simultaneous):**
1. **Pressure:** 5 bar internal (N₂/Ar)
2. **Thermal:** Steady-state gradient above
3. **Centrifugal:** 500 RPM (84.5 G at ID, 93.5 G at OD)
4. **Thermal Shock:** $\Delta T/\Delta t = 100°C/s$ (emergency cool)

**Material Model:** Temperature-dependent elastic-plastic with Weibull failure
$$\sigma_{eq} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{s}:\mathbf{s}} \quad \text{(von Mises)}$$
$$P_f = 1 - \exp\left[-\left(\frac{\sigma_{max}}{\sigma_0}\right)^m \frac{V}{V_0}\right] \quad \text{(Weibull, } m=12, \sigma_0=500 \text{ MPa)}$$

**Results (Stage 8, 500 RPM, 5 bar):**
| Stress Component | Max Value (MPa) | Location | Allowable (MPa) | Margin |
|------------------|-----------------|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Hoop (pressure) | 42 | Mid-wall | 350 (1500°C) | 8.3× |
| Hoop (centrifugal) | 185 | Inner surface | 350 | 1.9× |
| Thermal (radial) | 220 | Liner B interface | 350 | 1.6× |
| **Combined von Mises** | **385** | **Liner B interface** | **350** | **0.91×** |

**Critical Finding:** Combined stress at Liner B interface (385 MPa) exceeds 350 MPa allowable at 1500°C. **Mitigation:** Limit Stage 8 RPM to 400 (54 G) when $T_{inner} > 2000°C$. At 400 RPM: centrifugal stress = 118 MPa, combined = 330 MPa (margin 1.06×).

### 4.3 Port Stress Concentrations

**Port Geometry:** 8 ports at 44.2° spacing, 12 mm radius, Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ sleeve
**SCF (Stress Concentration Factor):** 2.8 at port root (FEA)
**Mitigation:** Local wall thickening to 45 mm at ports (+10 mm), ZrO₂ reinforcement ring
**Fatigue Life (500 thermal cycles, ΔT = 2000°C):**
- Baseline (no reinforcement): 800 cycles to 1 mm crack
- With reinforcement: >5000 cycles (Paris law: $da/dN = C(\Delta K)^m$, $C=5\times10^{-12}$, $m=3.2$)

### 4.4 Thermal Shock Analysis (Emergency Cool)

**Scenario:** Cooling water loss → N₂ quench at 100°C/s from 2200°C
**Max Thermal Stress (transient):** 620 MPa at inner surface (exceeds 350 MPa)
**Result:** Weibull $P_f = 2.3\times10^{-3}$ per event (acceptable for emergency)
**Design Rule:** Emergency cool only if $T_{inner} < 1800°C$ OR drum at rest (0 RPM)

## 5. Cascade CFD (Gas-Solid Flow in Rotating Drum)

### 5.1 Model Formulation

**Solver:** ANSYS Fluent (RANS, k-ω SST) + DPM (Discrete Phase Model)
**Geometry:** Full 360° drum, 800 mm length, rotating wall (MRF), 8 port openings
**Mesh:** 2.5M poly-hexcore cells, boundary layers at wall (y⁺ ≈ 1)
**Time Step:** 0.001 s (resolves particle-drum collisions)
**Total Simulated Time:** 30 s physical (per stage)

**Particle Properties (per Stage):**
| Stage | Particle Type | Size Range | Density | Shape Factor | Mass Loading |
|-------|---------------|------------|---------|--------------|--------------|
| 1 | Wet feedstock | 1-50 mm | 1200-3500 | 0.7 | 0.15 |
| 2 | Polymer melt | 0.5-10 mm | 950 | 0.9 | 0.25 |
| 3 | Char + ash | 0.1-5 mm | 350 | 0.5 | 0.20 |
| 4 | Metal droplets | 0.5-5 mm | 7000 | 1.0 | 0.10 |
| 5 | Al film | N/A (film) | 2380 | - | 0.30 |
| 6 | Cu droplets | 1-10 mm | 8000 | 1.0 | 0.15 |
| 7 | Fe/REE droplets | 1-20 mm | 7000 | 1.0 | 0.25 |
| 8 | Mineral slag | 0.5-10 mm | 2800 | 0.7 | 0.40 |

### 5.2 Key CFD Outputs per Stage

| Stage | RPM | G-Force | Separation Index (SI) | Residence Time (s) | Mixing Index |
|-------|-----|---------|----------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1 | 10 | 0.3 | N/A (no sep) | 1200 | 0.95 |
| 2 | 150 | 12.6 | 0.85 (polymer/metal) | 1800 | 0.70 |
| 3 | 200 | 22.3 | 0.78 (char/gas) | 1800 | 0.75 |
| 4 | 400 | 89.2 | 0.95 (In/Pb/Sn/Zn) | 1500 | 0.60 |
| 5 | 300 | 50.2 | 0.92 (Al/slag) | 1500 | 0.65 |
| 6 | 350 | 68.1 | 0.98 (Cu/PM/slag) | 1800 | 0.55 |
| 7 | 450 | 112.8 | 0.94 (Fe/REE/slag) | 2100 | 0.50 |
| 8 | 300 | 50.2 | 0.90 (ZrO₂/REE/slag) | 1200 | 0.60 |

**Separation Index:** $SI = 1 - \frac{\sigma_{composition}}{\sigma_{initial}}$ (1 = perfect separation)
**Mixing Index:** Standard deviation of particle radial distribution / mean radius (0 = perfect stratification)

### 5.3 Centrifugal Stratification Physics

The **Centrifugal Multi-Component Stratification Operator (CMCSO)** governs radial position:
$$\frac{dr_i}{dt} = \frac{2}{9}\frac{(\rho_i - \rho_f)g_{eff}r_i^2}{\mu_f} \quad \text{(Stokes, corrected for hindered settling)}$$

Where $g_{eff} = \omega^2 r$, $\rho_f$ = fluid (melt) density, $\mu_f$ = melt viscosity.

**Validation (Stage 4, In-first):**
- CFD: In droplets (ρ=7.3 g/cm³) reach r=150 mm in 3.2 s at 400 RPM
- Theory: $t = \frac{9\mu_f}{2(\rho_{In}-\rho_f)\omega^2}\ln\frac{r_{final}}{r_{initial}} = 2.8$ s
- Experiment (PROD-17): 99.5% In at Port 4A in 5 min → **validated**

### 5.4 Gas Flow & Heat Transfer Coefficients

**Effective Convection Coefficient ($h_{eff}$) by Stage:**
| Stage | $h_{conv}$ (W/m²·K) | $h_{rad}$ (W/m²·K) | Total $h$ | Notes |
|-------|---------------------|-------------------|-----------|-------|
| 1 | 50 | 5 | 55 | N₂, low RPM |
| 2 | 80 | 15 | 95 | Polymer vapor, 150 RPM |
| 3 | 120 | 40 | 160 | Pyrolysis gas, 200 RPM |
| 4 | 200 | 100 | 300 | Metal vapor, 400 RPM |
| 5 | 250 | 180 | 430 | Al pool, 300 RPM |
| 6 | 300 | 400 | 700 | Cu pool, 350 RPM |
| 7 | 350 | 800 | 1150 | Fe pool, 450 RPM |
| 8 | 400 | 2500 | 2900 | Radiation dominant |

**Radiation Model:** Surface-to-surface (S2S) with view factors, $\epsilon = 0.85$ (drum), 0.92 (charge)

## 6. Stage Thermal Models (1D Transient Cascade)

### 6.1 Model Formulation (Per Stage)

Each stage modeled as 1D transient heat equation with moving boundary (charge level):
$$\rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(k \frac{\partial T}{\partial z}\right) + \frac{P_{ind}(z,t)}{A} - \frac{hP}{A}(T - T_{gas}) - \frac{\epsilon\sigma P}{A}(T^4 - T_{surr}^4)$$

Where $z$ = axial coordinate, $A$ = cross-section, $P$ = perimeter.

**State Variables per Stage:**
- $T(z,t)$ — axial temperature profile
- $m_{charge}(t)$ — charge mass (decreasing as ports open)
- $X_{comp}(t)$ — composition vector (from XRF/LIBS feedback)
- $h_{eff}(t)$ — effective heat transfer coeff (from CFD)

### 6.2 Stage 0-1: Acoustic & Drying (PROD-14)

**Energy Balance:**
$$m c_p \frac{dT}{dt} = P_{ind} - \dot{m}_{H_2O}\Delta H_{vap} - Q_{loss}$$

**Parameters:** $m = 50$ kg, $c_p = 900$ J/kg·K, $\Delta H_{vap} = 2257$ kJ/kg
**Target:** 20% moisture → 2% in 20 min at 150°C
**Power Required:** 50 kW (Z1-Z2) + 15 kW latent heat = 65 kW peak

### 6.3 Stage 2: Polymer Flow & Separation (PROD-15)

**Multi-Component Melting:**
$$\frac{dT}{dt} = \frac{P_{ind} - \sum \dot{m}_i \Delta H_{fus,i} - Q_{loss}}{m c_p}$$

**Polymer Melting Sequence (validated by DSC):**
| Polymer | T_melt (°C) | Mass % (Cat A) | ΔH_fus (kJ/kg) |
|---------|-------------|----------------|----------------|
| LDPE | 110 | 8% | 140 |
| HDPE | 130 | 12% | 180 |
| PP | 165 | 15% | 190 |
| PS | 240 | 10% | 85 |
| ABS | 220 | 8% | 100 |
| PET | 260 | 5% | 140 |
| PVC | 160 (decomp) | 8% | HCl release |
| PC | 230 | 4% | 120 |

**Centrifugal Separation:** Stokes settling at G=12.6, $\mu = 100-500$ Pa·s → 95% separation in 30 min

### 6.4 Stage 3: Pyrolysis & Char (PROD-16)

**Global Kinetics (Parallel Reactions):**
$$\frac{d\alpha}{dt} = \sum_{i=1}^3 A_i \exp(-E_{a,i}/RT) (1-\alpha)^{n_i}$$

| Reaction | A (s⁻¹) | E_a (kJ/mol) | n | Product |
|----------|---------|--------------|---|---------|
| Light volatiles | 1.2×10¹³ | 180 | 1.2 | Gas (CO, CO₂, CH₄) |
| Heavy tars | 3.5×10¹⁰ | 150 | 1.5 | Tar (cracks to gas) |
| Char formation | 8.0×10⁸ | 120 | 0.8 | Char (fixed C) |

**Char Yield:** 15-25% of organic input (Category dependent)
**Energy Balance:** Endothermic net (-120 kJ/kg feed) + exothermic char oxidation if O₂ present

### 6.5 Stage 4: Low-Temp Metals (PROD-17)

**Indium-First Strategy (Sequential Melting):**
| Metal | T_melt (°C) | ρ_liquid (g/cm³) | Port | Dwell |
|-------|-------------|------------------|------|-------|
| In | 156.6 | 7.31 | 4A | 5 min |
| Sn | 231.9 | 6.99 | 4B | 3 min |
| Pb | 327.5 | 10.66 | 4C | 3 min |
| Zn | 419.5 | 6.57 | 4C | 10 min |

**Density Stratification (CMCSO):**
$$\Delta r = \frac{2(\rho_i - \rho_j) \omega^2 r^3 t}{9\mu}$$
At 400 RPM, 200°C: In (7.31) vs Sn (6.99) → $\Delta r = 8$ mm in 5 min → clean separation

### 6.6 Stage 5: Aluminum Window (PROD-18)

**Mg Removal Kinetics (Flux Reaction):**
$$\text{Mg} + \text{NaCl} + \text{KCl} + \text{Cryolite} \rightarrow \text{MgF}_2 + \text{Na} + \text{K} + \text{Al}$$
**Rate:** $r = k_0 \exp(-E_a/RT) [\text{Mg}] [\text{Flux}]$, $E_a = 85$ kJ/mol
**Target:** [Mg] < 0.1% in Al product (wrought grade)

**Al Fractionation (Scheil-Gulliver):**
$$C_s = k C_0 (1-f_s)^{k-1}$$
Partition coefficients: $k_{Fe}=0.01$, $k_{Si}=0.13$, $k_{Cu}=0.17$, $k_{Mg}=0.34$

### 6.7 Stage 6: Copper & Precious Metals (PROD-19)

**PM Partitioning (CFDO-CB Operator):**
$$K_{PM} = \frac{C_{slime}}{C_{anode}} = \exp\left(-\frac{\Delta G_{seg}}{RT}\right)$$
| PM | ΔG_seg (kJ/mol) | K_PM | Recovery |
|----|-----------------|------|----------|
| Au | -45 | 10⁴ | >99.6% |
| Ag | -32 | 10³ | >99% |
| Pd | -28 | 10² | >98% |
| Pt | -22 | 10² | >83% |

**Anode Slime Mass:** 40-60 kg/batch (from 200 kg anodes)

### 6.8 Stage 7: Ferrous Cascade (PROD-20)

**Ferromagnetic Coupling Transition (Curie 770°C):**
- Below 770°C: $\mu_r = 200$ → hysteresis heating dominant ($P_h \propto f B^{1.6}$)
- Above 770°C: $\mu_r = 1$ → eddy current only
- **Resonance tracker pre-empts ZVS loss** during transition (PROD-23 Section 3.4)

**REE Magnet Partitioning (CDPPO-RSE):**
$$L_{REE} = \frac{C_{slag}}{C_{Fe}} = \exp\left(\frac{\Delta G_{ox}}{RT}\right) \quad \text{at } a_{FeO}=0.15, B=1.2$$
| REE | L_REE | Recovery to Port 7A |
|-----|-------|---------------------|
| Nd | 300 | 77% |
| Sm | 200 | 71% |
| Co | 10 | 55% |
| Dy | 250 | 70% |

**Carbon Control:** CO/CO₂ injection, XRF feedback at 2/min, $C_{target} = 0.5-4\%$ by stream

### 6.9 Stage 8: Mineral Residue & Zircon (PROD-21)

**Zircon Dissociation Kinetics (Shrinking Core):**
$$\frac{d r_c}{dt} = -\frac{k_0 \exp(-E_a/RT) P_{SiO_2}}{\rho_{ZrSiO_4}} \quad \text{at } P_{SiO_2} = 10^{-3} \text{ atm}$$
$E_a = 415$ kJ/mol, $k_0 = 2.5\times10^5$ m/s, $r_c$ = core radius
**Dissociation Time:** 30 min at 1700°C, 20 SLPM Ar sweep

**3Y-TZP Flash Sinter (CMOSO-RDFS):**
$$\frac{d \rho}{dt} = \frac{\sigma_{DC} E^2}{H_s} \quad \text{(electro-thermal coupling)}$$
$\sigma_{DC}$ jumps 100× at 1200°C → volumetric heating → 50%→97% TD in 60 s at 1800°C, 300 V/cm

**SiO₂ Condenser (Port 8B):**
- Quench: 1700°C → 200°C in 0.5 s (3000°C/s)
- Product: Fumed silica, 50 nm, 200 m²/g
- Capture efficiency: >90%

## 7. Vessel & Insulation FEA

### 7.1 Thermal Model — 2000°C Across 68 mm

**Geometry:** Full 360° vessel, 1200 mm length, 18 mm BFRP, 50 mm aerogel, 0.3 mm glaze
**Boundary Conditions:**
- Inner surface (BFRP/aerogel interface): $T = 700°C$ (from drum model)
- Outer surface (glaze): Radiation to ambient + solar load
- End flanges: PEEK CF40, $T < 200°C$

**Steady-State Results (Stage 8):**
| Layer | Temperature (°C) | ΔT Across Layer |
|-------|------------------|-----------------|
| Drum OD | 700 | - |
| Aerogel inner | 698 | 2 |
| Aerogel outer | 180 | 518 |
| BFRP inner | 175 | 5 |
| BFRP outer | 150 | 25 |
| Glaze outer | 148 | 2 |
| Ambient | 25 | - |

**Key Metric:** BFRP max temperature = 175°C (internal), 150°C (external) < 200°C limit → **SF = 1.33 on Tg=80°C** (with 120°C margin via aerogel + glaze)

### 7.2 Structural Model — Pressure + Thermal

**Load Cases:**
1. Design pressure: 10 bar (hoop stress = 41 MPa in 18 mm BFRP)
2. Thermal gradient: 150°C outer → 175°C inner (compressive hoop)
3. Seismic: IEEE 693 High (PGA = 1.0g)
4. Combined: Pressure + Thermal + Seismic

**Barlow Formula (Hoop Stress):**
$$\sigma_h = \frac{P r_i}{t} = \frac{1.0 \times 10^6 \times 0.45}{0.018} = 25 \text{ MPa} \quad \text{(thin-wall approx)}$$
**FEA (thick-wall, Lame):** $\sigma_h = 41$ MPa at inner surface

**Tsai-Wu Failure Criterion:**
$$F_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j + F_i\sigma_i = 1$$
**Result:** Failure index = 0.18 (pressure only), 0.24 (combined) → **SF > 4.0**

### 7.3 Aerogel Gap Structural Integrity

**Mechanical Standoffs:** ZrO₂ ceramic pins (Ø8×50 mm), 48 per vessel (6 rings × 8)
**Load:** Aerogel compression (0.8 MPa strength) + differential expansion
**Differential Expansion (2200°C drum → 150°C vessel):**
- Drum OD growth: +8.5 mm
- Vessel ID growth: +0.5 mm
- **Gap closure: 8 mm** (standoffs compress from 50 → 42 mm)
**Stress in Standoffs:** 0.8 MPa × (42/50)² = 0.56 MPa < 0.8 MPa allowable

## 8. Transient Thermal Cycling Analysis

### 8.1 Batch Cycle Thermal Profile

```
TIME (min)    EVENT                              DRUM T_MAX    VESSEL T_MAX
0-15          Stage 0 (Acoustic)                 80°C          35°C
15-35         Stage 1 (Drying)                   150°C         45°C
35-65         Stage 2 (Polymer)                  450°C         85°C
65-95         Stage 3 (Pyrolysis)                660°C         110°C
95-120        Stage 4 (Low-Temp Metals)          900°C         130°C
120-145       Stage 5 (Al Window)                720°C         135°C
145-175       Hold (Brass/Bronze)                1085°C        145°C
175-205       Stage 6 (Cu/PM)                    1200°C        155°C
205-240       Stage 7 (Ferrous)                  1600°C        170°C
240-270       Stage 8 (Mineral)                  2200°C        175°C
270-300       Cool-down (N₂ purge)               2200→80°C     175→40°C
```

### 8.2 Thermal Fatigue (Coffin-Manson)

**Drum (ZrB₂-SiC):**
$$\Delta \epsilon_p / 2 = \epsilon_f' (2N_f)^c$$
$\epsilon_f' = 0.005$, $c = -0.6$ (ceramic)
$\Delta T = 2120°C$ (2200→80°C), $\Delta \epsilon_{th} = \alpha \Delta T = 6.5\times10^{-6} \times 2120 = 0.0138$
$N_f = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{0.0138/2}{0.005}\right)^{1/-0.6} = 2,800$ cycles
**Design Life:** 500 batches → **SF = 5.6 on thermal fatigue**

**Vessel (BFRP):**
$\Delta T = 150°C$ (175→25°C), $\Delta \epsilon_{th} = 7.5\times10^{-6} \times 150 = 0.0011$
Matrix fatigue: $N_f > 10^5$ cycles at this strain → **SF > 200**

**Aerogel:**
Compression cycles: 50 mm → 42 mm → 50 mm (500 cycles)
Creep strain: <0.5% per cycle → 2.5% total < 5% failure threshold

### 8.3 Pressure Fatigue

**Drum:** 5 bar cyclic, 500 cycles. $\Delta \sigma = 42$ MPa (hoop). $N_f > 10^6$ at this stress ratio.

**Vessel:** 5 bar cyclic, 500 cycles. $\Delta \sigma = 41$ MPa. Tsai-Wu fatigue model → $N_f > 10^5$.

| **Speedup** | 100× vs. full FEA | 10 Hz digital twin sync (PROD-37) |

| **Online Adaptation** | RLS parameter update | Drift compensation |

### 11.2 POD-Galerkin ROM (Thermal)

**Training Data:** 1000 full-order snapshots (thermal FEA, 1 ms spacing, 1 s simulation)
**POD Basis:** 12 modes capture 99.9% energy
**Galerkin Projection:** 12 ODEs for mode coefficients
$$\frac{d\mathbf{a}}{dt} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{B}u + \mathbf{N}(\mathbf{a})$$
Where $\mathbf{a}$ = 12 modal coefficients, $u$ = power input vector (8 zones)

**ROM Performance:**
| Metric | Full FEA | ROM | Error |
|--------|----------|-----|-------|
| Solve time (1 s sim) | 45 s | 0.38 s | 118× speedup |
| $T_{max}$ error | — | 1.8°C | 0.08% |
| $\sigma_{vm}$ error | — | 4.2 MPa | 1.1% |
| Memory | 2.1 GB | 45 MB | 47× reduction |

### The Lock That Forges the Key

The Aegis-Forge I thermal model exists because **induction heating power is a nonlinear function of the very temperature it creates, and the material properties governing both are themselves strong functions of temperature.** This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not a modeling preference — it is physics. At Stage 7, Fe ferromagnetic permeability drops from 200 to 1 at 770°C, collapsing induction power by 60%. At Stage 4, gas convection cooling of In droplets ($h_{conv}$) determines whether centrifugal separation succeeds — and $h_{conv}$ is an output of the CFD, not an input.

The **empirical gap** (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between single-physics simulations and integrated cascade test data.
