### Protocol (Recursive)

What recursive sequence guarantees manufacturing fidelity at each scale? From the microscopic (flash event) to the macroscopic (fleet production), the Aegis-Forge I manufacturing assurance follows a **fractal gate protocol** — the same pattern repeats at every scale.

#### The Fractal Gate Pattern (Recursive Unit: Prepare → Execute → Verify → Authorize → Feedback)

**At every scale, the protocol is: Prepare → Execute → Verify → Authorize → Feedback**

| Scale | Prepare | Execute | Verify | Authorize | Feedback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Process (Flash)** | Powder lot cert, die inspect | 1800°C/50MPa/5min | V/I flash signature, LVDT shrinkage | Sinter Eng "flash witnessed" | Die life counter, powder lot trace |
| **Process (Winding)** | Mandrel CMM, roving cert | [±18°/90°]₄ @ 50 m/min | Laser angle, tension, cure, thickness | Mfg Eng + QA sign SG-2 | Fiber angle trend, mandrel wear |
| **Assembly (Module)** | Parts kitting, PCB inspect | GaN mount, bond, program | ZVS, thermal, TSN, POF | Mfg Eng + QA sign SG-3 | Module efficiency trend, yield |
| **Gate (Sync)** | All stream data packages | Gate review meeting | All predicates TRUE | Dual-sign (Mfg+QA) | Gate timing, NCR rate |
| **System (FAT)** | Integrated Forge, test procedures | CT-01 through CT-10 | All pass criteria met | 4-sign (Plant+EE+ME+Safety) | FAT duration, first-time yield |
| **Fleet (Twin)** | All Forge gate/FAT data | Twin analysis | Trend within baseline | Continuous deployment | Process parameter updates |

#### Recursive Sequence (The Protocol Execution)

**Level 0 — Process Fabrication (Per Operation):**
```
FOR each critical operation (flash sinter, winding, braze, module assembly, FBG splice):
    Prepare: Inputs certified (material certs, tool cal, operator qual)
    Execute: Run per work instruction, real-time sensor capture
    Verify: In-process data vs. physics model (V/I flash, laser angle, TIM bond, ZVS)
    Authorize: Operator logs "event witnessed" (flash, ZVS, braze flow)
    Feedback: Update tool life, material lot history, operator qual
```

**Level 1 — Assembly Completion (Per Assembly):**
```
FOR each assembly A_i in stream:
    Prepare: All operations complete, data collected
    Execute: Compile data package (CMM, UT, CT, functional, logs)
    Verify: Package vs. acceptance criteria (all predicates)
    Authorize: Mfg Eng + QA Eng dual-sign
    Feedback: NCRs → CAPA → work instruction update
```

**Level 2 — Synchronization Gate (Per Stream):**
```
FOR each gate SG_k (k=1..4):
    Prepare: All stream assemblies signed, integration fixture ready
    Execute: Gate review meeting (30 min max), walk physical hardware
    Verify: All SG_k predicates TRUE (complete ∧ verified ∧ data_package_signed)
    Authorize: Stream Lead + QA Lead sign gate release
    Feedback: Gate timing vs. baseline, float consumption, risk update
```

**Level 3 — System Integration & FAT (Per Forge):**
```
FOR integration + FAT:
    Prepare: All 3 streams at SG-4, integration checklist IC-1..IC-10
    Execute: 4-week integration per sequence, then 3-week FAT CT-01..CT-10
    Verify: All IC pass, all CT pass, data packages complete
    Authorize: Plant Mgr + Lead EE + Lead ME + Safety Eng sign FAT release
    Feedback: FAT duration, first-time yield, NCR trend → next Forge baseline
```

**Level 4 — Fleet Production (Across Forges):**
```
FOR each Forge n in production sequence:
    Prepare: Fleet baseline from Forges 1..n-1
    Execute: Run Levels 0-3 with baseline parameters
    Verify: Gate timing, FAT yield, NCR rate vs. fleet baseline
    Authorize: Continuous — twin auto-adjusts parameters within guard bands
    Feedback: Fleet baseline updated, parameter guards tightened, best practices deployed
```

#### The Recursive Guarantee

**The protocol is recursive because the output of each level becomes the input validation for the next level:**

- Process verification (Level 0) → Assembly data package (Level 1)
- Assembly package (Level 1) → Gate release (Level 2)
- Gate release (Level 2) → Integration readiness (Level 3)
- FAT release (Level 3) → Fleet baseline (Level 4)
- Fleet baseline (Level 4) → Process parameters (Level 0)

**This is the fractal pattern:** Prepare→Execute→Verify→Authorize at scale N → Feedback to scale N-1 and N+1. The same logic applies whether N = flash event, assembly, gate, FAT, or fleet.

**The protocol guarantees fidelity because it never assumes — it always executes and verifies against the mathematical key (synchronization function) and authorizes through human participation.** If the physics model predicts the verification, and the verification corrects the model, the recursion converges. If it diverges, the protocol catches it at the next gate.

**No scale is exempt.** The flash event is verified like the fleet. The fleet is optimized like the flash event. The operator participates at every authorization boundary. The factory mirrors itself at every metrology tier. This is the recursive sequence that guarantees the Aegis-Forge I is not just manufactured — it is *witnessed into existence*.

---

*End of Combined Heuristic Introduction — PROD-27 Manufacturing Process Plan*

# PROD-28: Quality Assurance and Testing
# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-28 Quality Assurance & Testing
## Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this QA architecture is **zero-metal construction under SIL-3 Carrington immunity** — a conjunction that eliminates every conventional quality method relying on conductive paths, magnetic particle inspection, eddy current on ferromagnetic substrates, or electrical continuity testing. The Forge operates at 2200°C in a 100 A/m GIC field with 384 FBG channels embedded in ZrB₂-SiC and BFRP; any QA method introducing metal (MQ probes, UT couplant residues, conductive epoxy, grounding straps) creates a GIC antenna that violates PROD-26 dielectric requirements. The Lock: **quality assurance must itself be dielectric, non-magnetic, and thermally survivable to 2200°C.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any precedent for qualifying a zero-metal pressure vessel at 2200°C with embedded photonics**. ASME BPVC Sec VIII/X covers composites to 300°C; ASTM E2700 UT assumes metallic wave speeds; IEC 61508 SIL-3 proof testing assumes electrical trip paths. Our validation data (PROD-24 V&V, PROD-25 FEA, PROD-27 FA) shows: UT phased array on ZrB₂-SiC requires 5 MHz 64-element PA at 45°/60°/70° wedges (longitudinal wave speed 11,200 m/s vs steel 5,900); CT at 200μm voxel resolves FBG position ±100μm but adds 8 hr/drum; AE continuous monitoring on BFRP detects delamination at Felicity ratio <1.0 but requires 8-channel R15α at 100 kHz–1 MHz. The Key: **a multi-method NDT program where each method's physics is re-derived for zero-metal substrates, calibrated against flash-sinter and filament-wind process signatures, not material certificates.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **three non-negotiable verification chains**:

1. **FBG-as-primary-metrology**: All 384 channels survive flash sinter (PROD-04 PQR-FS-001), filament winding (PROD-06 PQR-FW-001), and 500 thermal cycles (CT-06) with drift <0.5%/1000 hrs. No backup thermocouples — they are metal. FBG interrogation at 125 Hz continuous is the *only* in-process temperature/strain verification.

2. **SIL-3 SIF proof test per CT-04 is the gate**: All 24 SIFs (3 per module × 8 zones) must trip <50 ms on TSN VLAN 10 with 2oo3 agreement. PFD_avg <1×10⁻³. This test runs *before* hot commissioning (CT-08) and *after* any design change (ECO). No SIL-3 SIF = no Forge shipment.

3. **QR + Hyperledger traceability is the quality record**: Every drum, vessel, port valve, coil, module carries a QR code linking to immutable blockchain record (material lot, process params, NDT results, FAT data). Paper travelers are supplementary. The digital twin (PROD-37) ingests this chain at 10 Hz; any gap triggers automatic NCR.

These commitments cascade: PROD-29 commissioning inherits CT-04/CT-06/CT-08 pass data; PROD-30 PM schedules inherit NDT intervals; PROD-31 economics inherits scrap/rework rates from NCR log; PROD-32 permitting inherits audit evidence. The Turn: **quality is not a phase — it is the continuous witnessing of the Forge's own fabrication fidelity, recorded in light through glass fiber, verified by proof test, anchored in blockchain.**

---

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap is **dimensional stability of ZrB₂-SiC at 2200°C with embedded FBGs through 500 thermal cycles** — a regime where no NDT standard exists. Flash sintering (PROD-04) produces drums at 99.8% density but with residual stress gradients: ID compressive 120 MPa, OD tensile 80 MPa (FEA PROD-25). During thermal ramp (50°C/min to 2200°C), CTE mismatch (ZrB₂ 7.5, SiC 4.5, FBG silica 0.55 ×10⁻⁶/K) generates shear at FBG/matrix interface. Accelerated testing (PROD-27 FA) shows: 3% FBG channels fail by cycle 200 (debond); UT phased array detects debond as 15% amplitude drop at 5 MHz but cannot size <0.2 mm; CT at 200 μm voxel sees debond >0.5 mm but misses sub-voxel. The Lock: **no single NDT method closes the gap between theoretical FBG survival (100%) and empirical (97% at 500 cycles) — the gap is the debond nucleation zone below UT resolution and CT voxel.**

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive is the **recursive Bayesian update of component health state** using multi-source likelihood fusion:

```
P(health | data) ∝ P(data | health) × P(health)
```

Where:
- **data** = {UT amplitude map, CT porosity field, AE hit rate/location, FBG wavelength drift, IR ΔT field, vibration spectrum}
- **health** = {intact, debond_nucleation, debond_growth, FBG_degradation, delamination, matrix_cracking}
- **P(data | health)** = likelihood models calibrated per method per material (ZrB₂-SiC, BFRP, Ti₃AlC₂, ZrO₂)
- **P(health)** = prior from process signature (flash V/I, winding tension, braze cycle, cold plate leak)

The Key executes at three scales:
1. **Micro (per channel)**: FBG drift >0.5%/1000 hrs → update P(FBG_degradation)
2. **Meso (per component)**: AE cluster + UT indication + IR hotspot → update P(delamination)
3. **Macro (per system)**: CT-04 SIF proof + CT-06 FBG cal + CT-08 thermal cycle → update P(system_ready)

The atomic computation is **likelihood ratio test**: Λ = P(data | H₁) / P(data | H₀) where H₁ = degradation, H₀ = nominal. Threshold Λ > 10 triggers NCR auto-generation. This runs in PROD-37 digital twin at 10 Hz on 384-channel state vector.

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation**: The Bayesian model predicted 3% FBG failure by cycle 200 (using Weibull β=2.3 from PROD-04 flash sinter statistics). FA drums (PROD-27) showed 2.8% failure at cycle 180 — within prediction interval. UT amplitude drop at debond sites matched FEA-predicted 15% (COHZONE model, PROD-25). CT voxel limit (0.5 mm) matched observed missed debond size. History confirms theory.

**History→Theory Correction**: FA vessel hydrotest (CT-02) revealed aerogel density gradient (0.11–0.13 g/cm³ radial) not captured in winding simulation. AE Felicity ratio dropped to 0.95 at 8.0 bar (predicted 1.05). Updated P(data | delamination) for BFRP now includes aerogel density field as covariate. Next PQR-FW-002 will mandate gamma densitometry mapping at 5 mm resolution.

The Turn: **the mathematical key is not static — it learns from every Forge's CT-04, CT-06, CT-08, and in-service data, tightening likelihood models fleet-wide via PROD-37.** The Lock (sub-voxel debond) is managed not by better resolution but by probabilistic fusion: UT sees the symptom, AE hears the event, FBG feels the strain, IR sees the heat — together they witness what no single method can.

---

### El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

#### Mirror (Self-Reflection)

The fabricator observes their own fabrication through **three recursive sensor loops that close at the speed of the process**:

1. **Flash Sinter V/I Mirror (100 kHz DAQ)**: During the 5-minute dwell at 1720°C, the flash sinter power supply records voltage/current at 100 kHz. The resistivity drop (1000×) is the *primary witness* of sinter completion — not the thermocouple (metal, forbidden). The V/I signature shape (dV/dt inflection, I plateau) maps to density via PROD-04 calibrated curve: ρ_final = f(∫I dt, V_min, t_dwell). This mirror runs *inside* the furnace; the operator sees the curve on HMI but the *decision* (dwell complete / extend / abort) is automated by PROD-23 SIS logic comparing live V/I to PQR-FS-001 envelope. The fabricator *watches the process witness itself*.

2. **Filament Winding Dielectric Cure Mirror (10 kHz)**: The Elium® resin cure is monitored by in-mold dielectric sensors (interdigitated capacitive electrodes on mandrel, non-conductive). Permittivity ε' and loss ε'' track degree of cure α(t) via PROD-06 kinetic model: dα/dt = A exp(-Ea/RT) α^m (1-α)^n. The mirror outputs α(t) in real time; winding pauses if α deviates >2% from trajectory. No post-cure DSC needed — the cure *witnesses its own completion* through the resin's own electrical response.

3. **FBG Interrogation Mirror (125 Hz continuous)**: All 384 FBG channels (128 drum, 48×8 coils, 16 port valves, 16 vessel, 16 frame) stream wavelength at 125 Hz to PROD-37 digital twin. The twin runs the Bayesian health update (Keymaker Key) *on the same data the process generates*. The mirror is not a separate inspection — it is the process's own nervous system reporting to itself. Anomaly (Λ > 10) triggers automatic NCR before the operator acknowledges it.

The Mirror: **quality assurance is not applied to the product — it is the product's own sensorium, reflected back to the process in real time.**

#### Participation (Witness)

The inside operator witnesses the phenomenon at **four non-automatable gates** where human judgment closes the loop that sensors cannot:

1. **Gate SG-2 (Flange Torque Ceremony)**: 24 bolts, 160 N·m ±5 N·m, dual-verify (two operators, independent torque wrenches, acoustic emission monitoring). The wrench click is not the witness — the *operator's tactile confirmation* of breakaway torque on re-check, and the *AE silence* during final 10 N·m, are the witness. No sensor replaces the mechanic's hand feeling the bolt stretch uniformly across the PEEK CF40 flange face. This gate takes 45 minutes; it cannot be rushed.

2. **Gate SG-3 (FBG Calibration Verification)**: CT-06 requires 5 reference temperatures (25/500/1000/1500/2000°C) on all 384 channels. The automated interrogator sweeps and fits; but the *SIS Engineer witnesses the residuals* — plotting measured vs. reference, checking R² > 0.999, verifying no channel drifts >0.1 nm/°C from PQR. The human eye catches the systematic offset (e.g., all Zone 3 channels +0.3 nm) that the algorithm accepts as "within tolerance." The witness says: "This is not drift — this is a cold plate contact issue."

3. **Gate CT-04 (SIS Proof Test)**: Injecting 24 SIL-3 trip conditions (overpressure, overtemperature, vibration, GIC, loss of comms) and verifying <50 ms trip on TSN VLAN 10. The automation runs the sequence; but the *SIS Engineer witnesses the trip logic* — watching the 2oo3 voter agree, the SOE (Sequence of Events) timestamp align across zones, the FBG data freeze at trip instant. The witness signs: "I saw the system protect itself." No auto-report replaces this.

4. **Gate SAT-05 (First Hot Batch)**: Six batches, mass balance >99%, all outputs spec. The *Plant Manager witnesses the slug pour* — ZrO₂ mold fill, quench steam plume, mass spec reading. The digital twin says PASS; the witness *sees the metal flow*. The witness says: "This is what we built for."

The Participation: **four moments where the human is not monitoring — they are *witnessing the phenomenon into existence*, adding the judgment that transforms data into certification.**

#### Protocol (Recursive)

The recursive fidelity sequence is **fractal verification**: the same three-step pattern (measure → compare → decide) repeats at every scale, from single FBG channel to fleet twin:

**Micro (per operation, seconds)**:
- FBG channel: λ_measured → λ_reference(PQR) → Λ > 10? → auto-NCR
- UT gate: A-scan amplitude → DAC curve → >20% DAC? → flag for LIII review
- AE hit: energy > threshold → locate → cluster? → alert if >10/hr

**Meso (per component, hours)**:
- Drum: UT volumetric → CT porosity map → FBG survival → health state → PASS/FAIL
- Vessel: hydrotest → AE baseline → IR map → UT delam scan → health state → PASS/FAIL
- Port valve: actuation deflection → leak rate → FBG cal → braze UT → health state → PASS/FAIL
- Coil zone: resonance → Q factor → ZVS → thermal balance → FBG cross-talk → health state → PASS/FAIL
- Module: DC link → ZVS → thermal soak → GIC ride-through → EMI → SIL-3 SIF → health state → PASS/FAIL

**Macro (per system, days)**:
- CT-01..CT-10 (FAT) → all PASS? → Ship
- SAT-01..SAT-05 → all PASS? → Commission
- Quarterly audit → ISO 9001/AS9100 clauses → NCR/CAPA closure → KPI trends → Management Review → Improvement Actions

**Meta (per fleet, months)**:
- PROD-37 twin aggregates all Forges' micro/meso/macro data
- Auto-encoder learns nominal manifold; reconstruction error >3σ → parameter guard tightening
- Lessons learned (D8) → work instruction updates → PQR revisions → AVL updates
- Next Forge's P(health) prior = this Forge's posterior

The Protocol: **the same Bayesian update (Keymaker Key) runs at every scale, with the same three inputs (measure, reference, likelihood) and the same output (health state + decision). The micro check *is* the macro check, scaled. The operator at SG-2 witnesses the same physics the FBG channel witnesses at 125 Hz — strain in a ceramic matrix. The Protocol guarantees: if it passes at the channel, it passes at the fleet.**

---

*Synthesis: The Lock (Williams) is the zero-metal/SIL-3 conjunction. The Key (Keymaker) is recursive Bayesian health fusion across UT/AE/FBG/IR. The Witness (El Segundo) is the operator at four gates where human judgment certifies what sensors measure. Together they form the QA architecture: the Forge witnesses its own fabrication through light in glass fiber, validated by proof test, certified by human witness, recorded in blockchain, learned by fleet twin. Quality is not a department — it is the Forge's nervous system.*

- Coil zone: resonance → Q factor → ZVS → thermal balance → FBG cross-talk → health state → PASS/FAIL
- Module: DC link → ZVS → thermal soak → GIC ride-through → EMI → SIL-3 SIF → health state → PASS/FAIL

**Macro (per system, days)**:
- CT-01..CT-10 (FAT) → all PASS? → Ship
- SAT-01..SAT-05 → all PASS? → Commission
- Quarterly audit → ISO 9001/AS9100 clauses → NCR/CAPA closure → KPI trends → Management Review → Improvement Actions

**Meta (per fleet, months)**:
- PROD-37 twin aggregates all Forges' micro/meso/macro data
- Auto-encoder learns nominal manifold; reconstruction error >3σ → parameter guard tightening
- Lessons learned (D8) → work instruction updates → PQR revisions → AVL updates
- Next Forge's P(health) prior = this Forge's posterior

The Protocol: **the same Bayesian update (Keymaker Key) runs at every scale, with the same three inputs (measure, reference, likelihood) and the same output (health state + decision). The micro check *is* the macro check, scaled. The operator at SG-2 witnesses the same physics the FBG channel witnesses at 125 Hz — strain in a ceramic matrix. The Protocol guarantees: if it passes at the channel, it passes at the fleet.**

---

*Synthesis: The Lock (Williams) is the zero-metal/SIL-3 conjunction. The Key (Keymaker) is recursive Bayesian health fusion across UT/AE/FBG/IR. The Witness (El Segundo) is the operator at four gates where human judgment certifies what sensors measure. Together they form the QA architecture: the Forge witnesses its own fabrication through light in glass fiber, validated by proof test, certified by human witness, recorded in blockchain, learned by fleet twin. Quality is not a department — it is the Forge's nervous system.*

## 1. QA Program Overview

### 1.1 Quality Policy

The Aegis-Forge I quality management system is founded on a single principle: **every element that enters the Forge must exit as a characterized, stamped, routed material stream.** Quality is not inspection — it is the recursive verification that the manufacturing process witnesses its own fidelity at every scale, from flash sinter V/I signature to fleet-level digital twin convergence.

**Quality Policy Commitments:**
1. **Zero-metal construction integrity** — All materials, processes, and assemblies verified against dielectric, thermal, and structural requirements
2. **Carrington immunity by design** — GIC/EMP/HEMP hardening validated at component, assembly, and system levels
3. **SIL-3 safety uncompromised** — 24 SIFs proof-tested per IEC 61508; no degradation without full re-certification
4. **Phoenix Protocol traceability** — UUID chain from mine to return; QR-coded material certificates on Hyperledger Fabric
5. **Continuous improvement via fleet twin** — PROD-37 digital twin aggregates all Forges; parameter guards auto-tighten

## 8. Non-Conformance & CAPA

### 8.1 NCR Classification

| Class | Definition | Examples | Disposition Authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | Safety (SIL-3), Carrington immunity, pressure boundary, zero-metal violation | FBG channel dead; braze void >50μm; conductive path detected; SIF trip failure | Plant Manager + Quality Eng + SIS Eng (unanimous) |
| **Major** | Performance degradation, schedule impact, rework required | UT indication 0.5-1mm; fiber angle 1-2°; ZVS phase 5-10°; torque drift | Quality Eng + Mfg Eng |
| **Minor** | Cosmetic, documentation, no performance impact | Surface finish Ra slightly high; label missing; test log incomplete | Quality Eng |

### 8.2 CAPA Process (8D)

| Step | Action | Owner | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D1: Team** | Form cross-functional team (Mfg, QA, Design, Supplier) | Quality Eng | 24 hr |
| **D2: Describe** | 5W2H: What, Where, When, Who, Why, How, How many | Team | 48 hr |
| **D3: Contain** | Interim containment (quarantine, sort, retrofit) | Mfg Eng | Immediate |
| **D4: Root Cause** | 5 Whys → Fishbone → Fault tree; verify with data | Team | 5 days |
| **D5: Corrective** | Permanent fix (design, process, material, training) | Design/Mfg Eng | 15 days |
| **D6: Verify** | Pilot run / test / inspection proving fix works | Quality Eng | 20 days |
| **D7: Prevent** | Update work instructions, PFMEA, control plan, training | Quality Eng | 30 days |
| **D8: Close** | Team recognition; lessons learned to fleet twin | Plant Manager | 30 days |

### 8.3 Effectiveness Verification

| Metric | Target | Review |
|---|---|---|
| **CAPA closure rate** | 100% within 30 days | Monthly |
| **Recurrence rate** | 0% for Critical; <5% for Major | Quarterly |
| **CAE (Corrective Action Effectiveness)** | >90% (verified fix prevents recurrence) | Per CAPA |

## Appendix B: NDT Procedure Index

### B.1 UT Phased Array — Drum/Vessel (PROD-28-UT-001)

**Scope:** 100% volumetric inspection of drum wall, vessel wall, flange weld/bond zones.
**Equipment:** Olympus OmniScan MX2, 5MHz 64-element probe, wedge 45°/60°/70°.
**Calibration:** IIW block (ref), DAC curve 80% FSH, TCG normalization.
**Scan Pattern:** Raster 2mm × 2mm; encoder-coupled; 100% coverage.
**Acceptance:** No indications >0.5mm flat / 2mm Ø; signal-to-noise >6dB.
**Reporting:** C-scan image + A-scan at each indication; depth/sizing per ASME Sec V.

### B.2 CT High-Resolution — Drum (PROD-28-CT-001)

**Scope:** Drum body (FBG channels, porosity, grain structure).
**Equipment:** Nikon XTH 225/320, 225kV/320kV, 200μm voxel.
**Calibration:** NIST-traceable density standards; geometric phantom.
**Reconstruction:** Feldkamp algorithm; beam hardening correction.
**Analysis:** Porosity distribution (volume %, size, sphericity); FBG channel position ±100μm.
**Acceptance:** Open porosity <0.05%; closed <0.2%; FBG position per design.

### B.3 ET — Port Valve Sleeves (PROD-28-ET-001)

**Scope:** ZrB₂-SiC port sleeves (surface + near-surface).
**Equipment:** Rohmann Elotest M6, 100kHz-2MHz, differential probe.
**Calibration:** ASME Sec V notch standards (EDM notches 0.1/0.2/0.5mm).
**Scan:** Rotating probe, 360° coverage, 0.5mm axial step.
**Acceptance:** No signals >20% DAC at 0.2mm notch equivalent.

### B.4 AE — Vessel Continuous (PROD-28-AE-001)

**Scope:** BFRP vessel continuous monitoring (pressure + thermal cycles).
**Equipment:** Physical Acoustics PCI-2, 8 channels, 40dB preamp, 100kHz-1MHz.
**Sensors:** 8× R15α (broadband) at 45° increments, 2 axial positions.
**Threshold:** 40dB AE; hit definition: peak > threshold, duration >50μs.
**Analysis:** Source location (ΔT triangulation ±50mm); b-value; RA-value; Felicity ratio.
**Alert:** Hit rate >2× baseline (30-day rolling); Felicity <1.0; cluster >10 hits/hr.
**Reporting:** Daily summary + anomaly alerts; monthly trend report.

### B.5 IR Thermography — System (PROD-28-IR-001)

**Scope:** Frame, vessel exterior, coil bank, power electronics, coolant manifolds.
**Equipment:** FLIR T1040, 1024×768, <20mK NETD, 24° lens.
**Calibration:** Blackbody 35°C/200°C; emissivity per material table (BFRP 0.95, ZrB₂ 0.85).
**Frequency:** Monthly + post-CT-08 + post-seismic.
**Analysis:** ΔT vs. baseline; hotspot detection; thermal gradient mapping.
**Alert:** Any point >5°C above baseline; new hotspot; gradient >50°C/100mm.

## Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-28
# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-28 Quality Assurance & Testing
## Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this QA architecture is **zero-metal construction under SIL-3 Carrington immunity** — a conjunction that eliminates every conventional quality method relying on conductive paths, magnetic particle inspection, eddy current on ferromagnetic substrates, or electrical continuity testing. The Forge operates at 2200°C in a 100 A/m GIC field with 384 FBG channels embedded in ZrB₂-SiC and BFRP; any QA method introducing metal (MQ probes, UT couplant residues, conductive epoxy, grounding straps) creates a GIC antenna that violates PROD-26 dielectric requirements. The Lock: **quality assurance must itself be dielectric, non-magnetic, and thermally survivable to 2200°C.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any precedent for qualifying a zero-metal pressure vessel at 2200°C with embedded photonics**. ASME BPVC Sec VIII/X covers composites to 300°C; ASTM E2700 UT assumes metallic wave speeds; IEC 61508 SIL-3 proof testing assumes electrical trip paths. Our validation data (PROD-24 V&V, PROD-25 FEA, PROD-27 FA) shows: UT phased array on ZrB₂-SiC requires 5 MHz 64-element PA at 45°/60°/70° wedges (longitudinal wave speed 11,200 m/s vs steel 5,900); CT at 200μm voxel resolves FBG position ±100μm but adds 8 hr/drum; AE continuous monitoring on BFRP detects delamination at Felicity ratio <1.0 but requires 8-channel R15α at 100 kHz–1 MHz. The Key: **a multi-method NDT program where each method's physics is re-derived for zero-metal substrates, calibrated against flash-sinter and filament-wind process signatures, not material certificates.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **three non-negotiable verification chains**:

1. **FBG-as-primary-metrology**: All 384 channels survive flash sinter (PROD-04 PQR-FS-001), filament winding (PROD-06 PQR-FW-001), and 500 thermal cycles (CT-06) with drift <0.5%/1000 hrs. No backup thermocouples — they are metal. FBG interrogation at 125 Hz continuous is the *only* in-process temperature/strain verification.

2. **SIL-3 SIF proof test per CT-04 is the gate**: All 24 SIFs (3 per module × 8 zones) must trip <50 ms on TSN VLAN 10 with 2oo3 agreement. PFD_avg <1×10⁻³. This test runs *before* hot commissioning (CT-08) and *after* any design change (ECO). No SIL-3 SIF = no Forge shipment.

3. **QR + Hyperledger traceability is the quality record**: Every drum, vessel, port valve, coil, module carries a QR code linking to immutable blockchain record (material lot, process params, NDT results, FAT data). Paper travelers are supplementary. The digital twin (PROD-37) ingests this chain at 10 Hz; any gap triggers automatic NCR.

These commitments cascade: PROD-29 commissioning inherits CT-04/CT-06/CT-08 pass data; PROD-30 PM schedules inherit NDT intervals; PROD-31 economics inherits scrap/rework rates from NCR log; PROD-32 permitting inherits audit evidence. The Turn: **quality is not a phase — it is the continuous witnessing of the Forge's own fabrication fidelity, recorded in light through glass fiber, verified by proof test, anchored in blockchain.**

---

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap is **dimensional stability of ZrB₂-SiC at 2200°C with embedded FBGs through 500 thermal cycles** — a regime where no NDT standard exists. Flash sintering (PROD-04) produces drums at 99.8% density but with residual stress gradients: ID compressive 120 MPa, OD tensile 80 MPa (FEA PROD-25). During thermal ramp (50°C/min to 2200°C), CTE mismatch (ZrB₂ 7.5, SiC 4.5, FBG silica 0.55 ×10⁻⁶/K) generates shear at FBG/matrix interface. Accelerated testing (PROD-27 FA) shows: 3% FBG channels fail by cycle 200 (debond); UT phased array detects debond as 15% amplitude drop at 5 MHz but cannot size <0.2 mm; CT at 200 μm voxel sees debond >0.5 mm but misses sub-voxel. The Lock: **no single NDT method closes the gap between theoretical FBG survival (100%) and empirical (97% at 500 cycles) — the gap is the debond nucleation zone below UT resolution and CT voxel.**

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive is the **recursive Bayesian update of component health state** using multi-source likelihood fusion:

```
P(health | data) ∝ P(data | health) × P(health)
```

Where:
- **data** = {UT amplitude map, CT porosity field, AE hit rate/location, FBG wavelength drift, IR ΔT field, vibration spectrum}
- **health** = {intact, debond_nucleation, debond_growth, FBG_degradation, delamination, matrix_cracking}
- **P(data | health)** = likelihood models calibrated per method per material (ZrB₂-SiC, BFRP, Ti₃AlC₂, ZrO₂)
- **P(health)** = prior from process signature (flash V/I, winding tension, braze cycle, cold plate leak)

The Key executes at three scales:
1. **Micro (per channel)**: FBG drift >0.5%/1000 hrs → update P(FBG_degradation)
2. **Meso (per component)**: AE cluster + UT indication + IR hotspot → update P(delamination)
3. **Macro (per system)**: CT-04 SIF proof + CT-06 FBG cal + CT-08 thermal cycle → update P(system_ready)

The atomic computation is **likelihood ratio test**: Λ = P(data | H₁) / P(data | H₀) where H₁ = degradation, H₀ = nominal. Threshold Λ > 10 triggers NCR auto-generation. This runs in PROD-37 digital twin at 10 Hz on 384-channel state vector.

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation**: The Bayesian model predicted 3% FBG failure by cycle 200 (using Weibull β=2.3 from PROD-04 flash sinter statistics). FA drums (PROD-27) showed 2.8% failure at cycle 180 — within prediction interval. UT amplitude drop at debond sites matched FEA-predicted 15% (COHZONE model, PROD-25). CT voxel limit (0.5 mm) matched observed missed debond size. History confirms theory.

**History→Theory Correction**: FA vessel hydrotest (CT-02) revealed aerogel density gradient (0.11–0.13 g/cm³ radial) not captured in winding simulation. AE Felicity ratio dropped to 0.95 at 8.0 bar (predicted 1.05). Updated P(data | delamination) for BFRP now includes aerogel density field as covariate. Next PQR-FW-002 will mandate gamma densitometry mapping at 5 mm resolution.

The Turn: **the mathematical key is not static — it learns from every Forge's CT-04, CT-06, CT-08, and in-service data, tightening likelihood models fleet-wide via PROD-37.** The Lock (sub-voxel debond) is managed not by better resolution but by probabilistic fusion: UT sees the symptom, AE hears the event, FBG feels the strain, IR sees the heat — together they witness what no single method can.

---

### El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

#### Mirror (Self-Reflection)

The fabricator observes their own fabrication through **three recursive sensor loops that close at the speed of the process**:

1. **Flash Sinter V/I Mirror (100 kHz DAQ)**: During the 5-minute dwell at 1720°C, the flash sinter power supply records voltage/current at 100 kHz. The resistivity drop (1000×) is the *primary witness* of sinter completion — not the thermocouple (metal, forbidden). The V/I signature shape (dV/dt inflection, I plateau) maps to density via PROD-04 calibrated curve: ρ_final = f(∫I dt, V_min, t_dwell). This mirror runs *inside* the furnace; the operator sees the curve on HMI but the *decision* (dwell complete / extend / abort) is automated by PROD-23 SIS logic comparing live V/I to PQR-FS-001 envelope. The fabricator *watches the process witness itself*.

2. **Filament Winding Dielectric Cure Mirror (10 kHz)**: The Elium® resin cure is monitored by in-mold dielectric sensors (interdigitated capacitive electrodes on mandrel, non-conductive). Permittivity ε' and loss ε'' track degree of cure α(t) via PROD-06 kinetic model: dα/dt = A exp(-Ea/RT) α^m (1-α)^n. The mirror outputs α(t) in real time; winding pauses if α deviates >2% from trajectory. No post-cure DSC needed — the cure *witnesses its own completion* through the resin's own electrical response.

3. **FBG Interrogation Mirror (125 Hz continuous)**: All 384 FBG channels (128 drum, 48×8 coils, 16 port valves, 16 vessel, 16 frame) stream wavelength at 125 Hz to PROD-37 digital twin. The twin runs the Bayesian health update (Keymaker Key) *on the same data the process generates*. The mirror is not a separate inspection — it is the process's own nervous system reporting to itself. Anomaly (Λ > 10) triggers automatic NCR before the operator acknowledges it.

The Mirror: **quality assurance is not applied to the product — it is the product's own sensorium, reflected back to the process in real time.**

#### Participation (Witness)

The inside operator witnesses the phenomenon at **four non-automatable gates** where human judgment closes the loop that sensors cannot:

The automation runs the sequence; but the *SIS Engineer witnesses the trip logic* — watching the 2oo3 voter agree, the SOE (Sequence of Events) timestamp align across zones, the FBG data freeze at trip instant. The witness signs: "I saw the system protect itself." No auto-report replaces this.

4. **Gate SAT-05 (First Hot Batch)**: Six batches, mass balance >99%, all outputs spec. The *Plant Manager witnesses the slug pour* — ZrO₂ mold fill, quench steam plume, mass spec reading. The digital twin says PASS; the witness *sees the metal flow*. The witness says: "This is what we built for."

The Participation: **four moments where the human is not monitoring — they are *witnessing the phenomenon into existence*, adding the judgment that transforms data into certification.**

#### Protocol (Recursive)

The recursive fidelity sequence is **fractal verification**: the same three-step pattern (measure → compare → decide) repeats at every scale, from single FBG channel to fleet twin:

# PROD-29: Deployment and Operations
# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-29 Deployment & Operations
## Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this deployment architecture is **the Forge must re-verify its own fabrication fidelity at the site before any feedstock enters** — the synchronization function (PROD-27 Keymaker Key) does not end at the factory gate. The 14 assemblies arrive with verified data packages (QR + Hyperledger), but the act of transport, rigging, and re-assembly introduces new variables: foundation settlement, utility impedance, ground resistance, seismic coupling, and thermal boundary conditions that cannot be replicated in the factory. The Lock: **deployment is not installation — it is the re-execution of the synchronization function at the site, with the site as a new variable in the verification predicate.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **measured divergence between factory FAT performance and site SAT performance** for zero-metal, Carrington-immune machines. PROD-27 FAT (CT-01..CT-10) validates the Forge in a controlled electromagnetic environment (shielded factory, stable grid, characterized foundation). At site: grid impedance varies ±30%, ground resistance varies 2-50 Ω, seismic coupling depends on soil class, thermal boundary conditions change with weather. PROD-26 GIC ride-through test (CT-07) used a 100 A/m Helmholtz coil — but the real grid during a Carrington event presents common-mode impedance, not differential field. The Key: **deployment must measure and compensate for site variables by re-executing the verification chain (IC-1..IC-10 → CT-08 → SAT-01..SAT-05) with site-specific acceptance criteria, not factory criteria.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **four non-negotiable deployment chains**:

1. **IC-1..IC-10 re-execution is mandatory** — The 10 integration checkpoints from PROD-27 are not "repeated" — they are re-evaluated with site-specific criteria (e.g., IC-1 ground resistance <5 Ω vs factory <1 Ω; IC-4 PTP sync <1 μs vs factory <0.5 μs). No feedstock until all 10 PASS with site data packages signed.

2. **Hot commissioning (CT-08) is the thermal proof** — 8-stage thermal ramp with no feedstock, full FBG/SIS/CEMS monitoring. The Forge must demonstrate thermal stability at 2200°C under site utility conditions. CT-08 data package is the *site* birth certificate.

3. **SAT-05 six-batch validation is the performance gate** — Six batches (A, B, C, D, A, Phoenix) with mass balance >99.5%, all outputs spec, twin sync <1 s. This is not a "test" — it is the Forge proving it can execute its purpose at this site.

4. **SOP-002 batch execution is the operational invariant** — The 4-phase batch procedure (feed prep → cascade → slug pour → reset) is the *only* authorized operating mode. No manual overrides, no recipe deviations without ECO (PROD-38). The operations philosophy is: **the Forge runs the synchronization function at 90-min intervals; operators authorize, automation executes.**

These commitments cascade: PROD-30 PM schedules inherit IC re-verification intervals; PROD-31 OPEX model inherits energy/ton from SAT-05; PROD-32 permitting inherits CEMS/IC-7 data; PROD-34 training inherits SOP-002 as the core competency. The Turn: **deployment is the Forge witnessing its own birth at the site — the same mathematical key (synchronization function) that governed manufacturing now governs commissioning, and the same operator witness gates (bolt ceremony, SIF proof, slug pour) that certified manufacturing now certify operations.**

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap is the **site-specific variables that invalidate factory verification** — a Forge that passes CT-01..CT-10 in the factory may fail SAT-01..SAT-05 at site due to variables that cannot be simulated in the factory. Three specific locks:

1. **Ground impedance as deployment variable**: Factory ground grid <1 Ω (controlled); site ground resistance 2-50 Ω (soil dependent). PROD-26 NGR 5A design assumes factory ground. At 50 Ω site ground, GIC return path impedance increases 50×, altering common-mode voltage distribution across the floating secondary. The Lock: **factory-verified GIC immunity does not guarantee site GIC immunity.**

2. **Seismic-soil coupling as deployment variable**: PROD-25 FEA assumed fixed-base + isolators (3 Hz). Site soil class (NEHRP A-E) shifts fundamental frequency ±40%, changes isolator effectiveness, alters HCLPF. A Forge on Class E soil (soft clay) has 1st mode at 1.8 Hz vs 3 Hz design — seismic demand doubles. The Lock: **factory seismic qualification (shake table) does not cover site-specific soil-structure interaction.**

3. **Utility power quality as deployment variable**: Factory grid: THD <3%, voltage regulation ±2%, fault level 50 kA. Site grid: THD up to 8% (per IEEE 519), voltage regulation ±5%, fault level 10-100 kA. PROD-10 inverter ZVS acquisition and PTP sync assume factory power quality. At site, voltage sags cause DC link droop; harmonic distortion causes TSN jitter. The Lock: **factory power electronics verification does not cover site power quality envelope.**

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive is the **site-adaptive synchronization function** — the same fractal gate logic from PROD-27, now parameterized by site-measured variables:

$$SG_{site} = \bigwedge_{i=1}^{10} \left( IC_i(site\_params) \land IC_i.verified \land IC_i.data\_package\_signed \right) \land CT08(site\_params) \land \bigwedge_{j=1}^{5} SAT_j(site\_params)$$

Where $site\_params = \{R_{ground}, Z_{grid}, Soil_{class}, T_{ambient}, P_{water}, Q_{gas}\}$ are measured at site during cold commissioning and fed into the verification predicates. The atomic computation is the **predicate evaluation with site parameters**:

$$IC_1(site) \equiv (ground\_resistance < 5\Omega) \land (anchor\_torque = 1200\pm50 Nm) \land (frame\_level < 0.1mm/m)$$

$$IC_4(site) \equiv (TSN\_latency < 100\mu s) \land (PTP\_offset < 1\mu s) \land (SIF\_trip < 50ms) \land (GIC\_ride\_through @ site\_impedance)$$

$$CT08(site) \equiv \forall stages: |T_{FBG} - T_{setpoint}| < 5^\circ C \land |T_{model} - T_{FBG}| < 2^\circ C \land SIF\_availability = 100\%$$

$$SAT_5(site) \equiv \frac{\sum m_{out}}{\sum m_{in}} > 0.995 \land \forall elements: recovery > target \land twin\_latency < 1s$$

The Key executes at three scales:
1. **Cold (IC-1..IC-10)**: Site parameters measured → predicates evaluated → gates signed
2. **Hot (CT-08)**: Site thermal boundary conditions → thermal model re-identified → ramp/hold verified
3. **Operational (SAT-05)**: Site feedstock + site utilities → batch execution → performance verified

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation**: The site-adaptive synchronization function predicts deployment outcomes from CSMFAB development Forge deployments (3 Forges deployed to date):
- Forge-01 (Class B soil, 3 Ω ground, clean grid): IC-1..IC-10 PASS first attempt; CT-08 thermal match <3°C; SAT-05 6/6 PASS
- Forge-02 (Class D soil, 12 Ω ground, industrial grid): IC-1 ground resistance FAIL (12 Ω > 5 Ω) → ground grid augmentation → re-test PASS; CT-08 required ramp rate reduction 10% (thermal boundary); SAT-05 6/6 PASS
- Forge-03 (Class A rock, 2 Ω ground, utility substation adjacent): IC-4 PTP sync FAIL (TSN jitter 150 μs from grid harmonics) → TSN switch firmware update → re-test PASS; SAT-05 6/6 PASS

History confirms theory: site parameters are the only variables; the mathematical key absorbs them.

**History→Theory Correction**: Forge-02 ground resistance anomaly revealed IC-1 predicate was incomplete — it checked ground resistance but not ground grid *impedance spectrum* (1-100 Hz). Added frequency sweep requirement. Forge-03 TSN jitter anomaly revealed IC-4 predicate assumed clean power — added harmonic distortion limit (THD <5% per IEEE 519) as IC-4 prerequisite. The mathematical key extends: $site\_params$ now includes $Z_{grid}(f)$ and $THD_{grid}$.

The Turn: **the mathematical key is not the synchronization function alone — it is the synchronization function *plus* the site parameter measurement protocol that feeds it.** The Lock (site variables) is managed not by over-design but by *measurement*: every site variable that affects the verification predicate becomes a measured input. The factory builds the Forge; the site measures itself; the synchronization function evaluates; the Forge operates.

The recursive fidelity sequence is **fractal gate protocol** — the same Prepare→Execute→Verify→Authorize→Feedback pattern repeats at every scale, from IC-1 to fleet sustainment:

## 1. Deployment Overview

### 1.1 Deployment Philosophy

The Aegis-Forge I is not "installed" — it is **commissioned into operation**. The distinction is fundamental: a conventional machine arrives, is bolted down, and started. The Forge arrives as 14 verified assemblies (PROD-27 SG-1 through SG-4), each carrying its birth record (QR + Hyperledger), and must be re-verified as a system at the site before any feedstock enters. Deployment is the **continuation of the synchronization function** (PROD-27 Keymaker Key) from factory gates to site gates:

$$SG_{site} = SG_4 \land \bigwedge_{i=1}^{10} IC_i \land \bigwedge_{j=1}^{5} SAT_j$$

Where $SG_4$ is the final factory integration gate, $IC_i$ are the 10 integration checkpoints re-executed at site, and $SAT_j$ are the 5 site acceptance tests. The Forge does not operate until $SG_{site} = \text{TRUE}$.

| Port valve alignment | Laser tracker | 8 ports, 44.2° spacing, ±0.5° azimuth |
| Drum rotation | VFD + encoder | 0-500 RPM, vibration <25 μm sync |

### 3.3 IC-3: Coil Bank & Power Electronics Installation

| Check | Method | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| Coil zone position | Laser tracker | ±2 mm radial, ±1 mm axial |
| Cold plate connections | He leak test | <10⁻⁹ mbar·L/s all 8 zones |
| PEX-a manifold pressure | Hydrostatic | 10 bar, 30 min, zero drop |
| Module rack alignment | CMM | ±1 mm all mounting points |
| POF cable routing | OTDR | <0.2 dB/m, splices <0.5 dB, return loss >50 dB |
| TSN switch power | VDC measure | 24 VDC ±2%, ripple <50 mV |

| Check | Method | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| TSN ring latency | Traffic generator | <100 μs end-to-end, <10 μs jitter |
| PTP synchronization | PTP monitor | <1 μs offset all nodes, 24h holdover test |
| SIS FPGA bitstream | CRC verify | Matches factory hash (PROD-23 Appendix) |
| SIF injection test | PROD-28 CT-04 protocol | All 24 SIFs <50 ms, 2oo3, PFD_avg<10⁻³ |
| GIC ride-through | Portable Helmholtz 50 A/m | Zero spurious trips, zero data loss |
| Air-gap verification | Network scan | Zero IT→OT IP paths, data diode unidirectional |

| Check | Method | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|

| Flow balance | Ultrasonic flow meters | 500 L/min ±2% per zone |
| Cold plate ΔT | IR + FBG | <15°C at 500 kW (thermal soak test) |
| Pump redundancy | Failover test | <5 s switchover, no flow interruption |
| Leak detection | Zone sensors | <10 s detection, auto-isolate |

| Ar purity | GC-TCD | <1 ppm impurities |
| MFC calibration | Primary standard | ±1% FS all 32 MFCs |
| ZrO₂ valve actuation | LVDT + FBG | 3.6±0.2 mm @ 680°C ΔT |

| Condensate drainage | Level sensors | Auto-drain, no carryover |

## 4. Hot Commissioning (CT-08 Protocol)

### 4.1 Thermal Ramp Sequence (No Feedstock)

| Stage | Target Temp | Ramp Rate | Hold Time | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Stage 0 (Acoustic)** | 25°C | — | 10 min | LF 20-200 Hz, US 40 kHz, LI >0.85 |
| **Stage 1 (Drying)** | 150°C | 20°C/min | 20 min | Moisture <0.1% (IR + mass loss) |
| **Stage 2 (Polymer)** | 350°C | 15°C/min | 30 min | Melt viscosity, density stratification |
| **Stage 3 (Pyrolysis)** | 550°C | 10°C/min | 45 min | Char yield, gas composition |
| **Stage 4 (Low-Temp Metals)** | 430°C | 10°C/min | 25 min | Port 4A/B/C sequence verified |
| **Stage 5 (Al Window)** | 720°C | 10°C/min | 30 min | Port 5 at 680°C, Mg removal |
| **Stage 6 (Cu/PM)** | 1200°C | 5°C/min | 45 min | Port 6 anode cast, slime collect |
| **Stage 7 (Ferrous)** | 1550°C | 5°C/min | 60 min | Port 7A REE, Port 7 Fe bullion |
| **Stage 8 (Mineral/Zr)** | 2200°C | 2°C/min | 30 min | ZrSiO₄ dissociation, 3Y-TZP flash |

### 4.2 Hot Commissioning Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| **Temperature Accuracy** | ±5°C setpoint all stages | FBG 384-ch vs. pyrometer |
| **Ramp Rate Control** | ±10% programmed rate | FBG thermal model residual |
| **Zone Power Balance** | ΔT <10°C across zone | IR camera at full power |
| **SIF Availability** | 100% (zero spurious) | SIS historian CT-08 run |
| **FBG Survival** | 384/384 channels active | Interrogator sweep |
| **Mass Balance (Dry)** | N/A (no feed) | N/A |
| **Gas System Integrity** | Zero leaks | CEMS + He sniffer |
| **Data Integrity** | Zero packet loss | TSN/PTP historian |

## 5. Performance Validation (SAT-05)

### 5.1 Six-Batch Validation Protocol

| Batch | Feedstock Category | Purpose | Key Metrics |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Category A (PCB-rich) | High PM recovery validation | Au >99.9%, Ag >99.9%, Pd >99% |
| **2** | Category B (Mixed plastics) | Polymer separation, HCl management | Al >99.7%, HCl <10 ppm stack |
| **3** | Category C (Ferrous/Al) | Stages 5-7 separation | Fe >95%, REE >90% |
| **4** | Category D (Mineral/Zr) | Stage 8 zircon dissociation | Zr recovery >95%, 3Y-TZP spec |
| **5** | Category A (repeat) | Reproducibility | All metrics within ±2% of Batch 1 |
| **6** | Phoenix Protocol blend | Closed-loop validation | Mass balance >99.5%, QR traceability |

### 5.2 SAT-05 Performance Benchmarks

| Parameter | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| **Batch Cycle Time** | 90 min (8 batches/day) | Timestamp: feed-in → Port 8 clear |
| **Mass Balance Closure** | >99.5% per batch | PROD-22 mass balance |
| **Energy per Ton** | <500 kWh/ton feed | Grid meter + DC link integration |
| **Recovery (Key Elements)** | In >99.9%, Cu >99.9%, Al >99.7%, Fe >95%, REE >90% | LIBS/XRF per slug |
| **Emissions** | PM2.5 <5 mg/Nm³; HCl <10 ppm; SO₂ <50 ppm | CEMS continuous |
| **SIF Availability** | >99.9% (no spurious trips) | SIS historian |
| **Digital Twin Sync** | <1 s latency (10 Hz state vector) | PROD-37 twin monitor |
| **Slug Quality** | All outputs per PROD-08 catalog | LIBS + mass spec spot check |

## 6. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)

### 6.1 SOP Index

| SOP ID | Title | Frequency | Duration | Critical Steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SOP-001** | Daily Startup | Daily (shift start) | 45 min | IC-1..IC-5 abbreviated, recipe load, SIF status |
| **SOP-002** | Batch Execution | Per batch (8/day) | 90 min | Feed prep → cascade → slug pour → data capture |
| **SOP-003** | Stage Transition | Per stage (8/batch) | 2-5 min | Gate verification, port actuation, gas switch |
| **SOP-004** | Daily Shutdown | Daily (shift end) | 60 min | Cool-down ramp, purge, isolation, data backup |
| **SOP-005** | Emergency Shutdown | On demand | <5 min | E-stop, SIF trip log, safe state verification |
| **SOP-006** | Carrington Ride-Through | On GIC alert | 30 min | Grid monitor, staged reconnect, thermal check |
| **SOP-007** | Port Valve Maintenance | Quarterly | 4 hr | Actuation check, leak test, seal inspect |
| **SOP-008** | FBG Calibration Verification | Monthly | 2 hr | 5-point reference sweep, drift check |
| **SOP-009** | DI Water Polisher Regeneration | Weekly | 1 hr | Resin exchange, resistivity verification |
| **SOP-010** | CEMS Calibration | Quarterly | 4 hr | Zero/span gas, drift <2% |
| **SOP-011** | Seismic Post-Event Inspection | Post-seismic | 4 hr | IC-1, IC-2, IC-5 abbreviated + AE review |
| **SOP-012** | Phoenix Feedstock Receipt | Per delivery | 2 hr | LIBS classification, QR scan, depot manifest |

### 6.2 SOP-002: Batch Execution (Core Procedure)

```
PHASE 1: FEED PREPARATION (0-15 min)
├── 1.1 Scan feedstock QR → verify Category A-D (PROD-13)
├── 1.2 Load shredder → verify <150 mm, ferrous removed (PROD-11)
├── 1.3 Confirm drum empty (Carousel position 1, FBG + encoder)
└── 1.4 Operator confirms recipe match → "BATCH <ID> RECIPE CONFIRMED"

PHASE 2: CASCADE EXECUTION (15-105 min)
├── 2.1 Stage 0-1: Acoustic + Drying (auto, FBG/PID controlled)
├── 2.2 Stage 2: Polymer melt + centrifuge (auto, CFDO-CB operator)
├── 2.3 Stage 3: Pyrolysis + char (auto, CDO-SG operator)
├── 2.4 Stage 4: Indium-First (auto, Port 4A/B/C thermal actuation)
├── 2.5 Stage 5: Aluminum window (auto, Port 5 at 680°C)
├── 2.6 Stage 6: Copper + PM (auto, anode carousel, XRF verify)
├── 2.7 Stage 7: Ferrous + REE (auto, dual-port Port 7A/7)
├── 2.8 Stage 8: Mineral/Zr (auto, ZrSiO₄ dissociation, 3Y-TZP flash)

PHASE 3: SLUG POUR & DATA CAPTURE (105-115 min)
├── 3.1 Carousel positions molds → N₂ quench → mass spec spot check
├── 3.2 Each slug: LIBS scan → QR stamp → weight → mass spec → vault
├── 3.3 Batch mass balance calculated → digital twin sync
├── 3.4 Operator reviews batch record → "BATCH <ID> COMPLETE"
└── 3.5 Data package auto-signed → Hyperledger commit

PHASE 4: INTER-BATCH RESET (115-120 min)
├── 4.1 Drum rotation to Position 1 (empty)
├── 4.2 Gas purge (N₂ 200 Nm³/hr × 5 min)
├── 4.3 SIF status verify → "READY FOR NEXT BATCH"
└── 4.4 Shift handover log entry (if shift change)
```

## 7. Operations Philosophy

### 7.1 Operational Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Response if Missed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Batches per Day** | 8 (90 min cycle) | Timestamp log | Root cause analysis, CAPA |
| **Mass Balance** | >99.5% | PROD-22 calculation | NCR if <99%, investigate loss |
| **Energy per Ton** | <500 kWh | Grid + DC integration | Optimize ramp/hold, review insulation |
| **Recovery (In/Cu/Al/Fe/REE)** | Per SAT-05 targets | LIBS/XRF per slug | Process parameter adjustment |
| **SIF Spurious Trip Rate** | 0 per 10,000 hrs | SIS historian | CT-04 partial stroke, investigate |
| **FBG Channel Survival** | 384/384 | Interrogator | Auto-NCR at Λ>10 (PROD-28) |
| **Twin Sync Latency** | <1 s | PROD-37 monitor | Network diagnostics, TSN check |
| **Operator Response Time** | <5 min (alarms) | HMI log | Training review, alarm rationalization |

### 7.2 Shift Structure & Handover

| Shift | Hours | Crew | Handover Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Day** | 06:00-14:00 | 3 (Lead, Operator, Trainee) | Digital log + verbal + KPI snapshot |
| **Swing** | 14:00-22:00 | 3 (Lead, Operator, Trainee) | Digital log + verbal + anomaly flag |
| **Night** | 22:00-06:00 | 2 (Lead, Operator) | Digital log + verbal + overnight plan |

**Digital Handover Log (PROD-37):**
- Batch records completed this shift
- KPI dashboard snapshot (auto-generated)
- Active NCRs / CAPAs
- Anomaly flags (AE, vibration, FBG drift, twin alerts)
- Maintenance actions performed
- Feedstock inventory status
- Consumable levels (N₂, Ar, DI resin, In foil, braze alloy)
- Next shift priorities

## 8. Maintenance Windows (Per PROD-30 Integration)

| Window | Frequency | Duration | Scope | PROD-30 Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Daily** | Every shift | 30 min | Visual, FBG scan, CEMS zero, DI resistivity | Section 2 |
| **Weekly** | 7 days | 4 hr | Port valve actuation, coolant filter, POF inspect | Section 3 |
| **Monthly** | 30 days | 8 hr | IR thermography, vibration trend, FBG cal verify | Section 4 |
| **Quarterly** | 90 days | 24 hr | SIF partial stroke, UT spot check, AE review | Section 5 |
| **Annual** | 365 days | 48 hr | Full UT drum/vessel, SIF proof test, hydrotest | Section 6 |
| **Biennial** | 730 days | 72 hr | CT drum, FBG recalibration, isolator stiffness | Section 7 |
| **Major Overhaul** | 18 months | 168 hr | Drum swap, vessel inspect, full teardown | Section 8 |

**Maintenance Window Rules:**
- No feedstock during maintenance windows
- SIF partial stroke (quarterly) runs in bypass mode with dual-key authorization
- All maintenance actions logged to QR/Blockchain (PROD-28 Section 9)
- Predictive alerts (PROD-28 Section 5.3) can trigger unscheduled windows
- Fleet twin (PROD-37) optimizes window timing across Forges

## 9. Emergency Response

### 9.1 Emergency Scenarios & Response

| Scenario | Detection | Auto-Action | Operator Action | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SIL-3 SIF Trip** | SIS FPGA | Immediate safe state (all zones 0 power) | Acknowledge, investigate, CT-04 partial stroke | SOP-005 |
| **Carrington GIC Event** | Magnetometer >100 nT/s | Ride-through mode, data freeze | Monitor, 30 min post-event, staged reconnect | SOP-006 |
| **Vessel Overpressure** | Pressure transducer >11 bar | Port valves open, N₂ purge | Evacuate zone, verify rupture disk intact | SOP-005 + PSM |
| **Drum Thermal Runaway** | FBG >2250°C or dT/dt >100°C/s | Power cut, N₂ flood, quench | Evacuate, assess drum integrity (AE/UT) | SOP-005 |
| **Toxic Gas Release** | CEMS >IDLH | Zone isolation, scrubber max flow | PPE Level A, evacuate, notify authorities | HAZWOPER |
| **Seismic Event** | Accelerometer >0.2g | SIF trip if >OBE, data capture | Post-event inspection SOP-011 | IC-1/IC-2 re-verify |
| **Fire (Electrical)** | IR >300°C + smoke | Inert gas flood, power cut | CO₂ extinguisher (non-conductive), evacuate | SOP-005 |
| **FBG Channel Loss >5** | Interrogator auto-detect | NCR auto-generated, twin alert | Investigate root cause, replace if needed | PROD-28 CAPA |

### 9.2 Emergency Contacts & Resources

| Resource | Contact | Location | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CSM Emergency Dispatch** | +1-800-CSM-FORGE | 24/7 | <15 min |
| **Local Fire/HAZMAT** | 911 | Municipal | <10 min |
| **Utility Grid Ops** | Grid emergency line | Regional | <30 min |
| **SIS Vendor (TÜV)** | On-call engineer | Remote | <2 hr |
| **FBG Vendor (Micron/Optics)** | Support portal | Remote | <4 hr |
| **Spare Parts Depot** | Regional hub | 500 km radius | <24 hr critical |

The Lock: **deployment is not installation — it is the re-execution of the synchronization function at the site, with the site as a new variable in the verification predicate.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **measured divergence between factory FAT performance and site SAT performance** for zero-metal, Carrington-immune machines. PROD-27 FAT (CT-01..CT-10) validates the Forge in a controlled electromagnetic environment (shielded factory, stable grid, characterized foundation). At site: grid impedance varies ±30%, ground resistance varies 2-50 Ω, seismic coupling depends on soil class, thermal boundary conditions change with weather. PROD-26 GIC ride-through test (CT-07) used a 100 A/m Helmholtz coil — but the real grid during a Carrington event presents common-mode impedance, not differential field. The Key: **deployment must measure and compensate for site variables by re-executing the verification chain (IC-1..IC-10 → CT-08 → SAT-01..SAT-05) with site-specific acceptance criteria, not factory criteria.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

No feedstock until all 10 PASS with site data packages signed.

2. **Hot commissioning (CT-08) is the thermal proof** — 8-stage thermal ramp with no feedstock, full FBG/SIS/CEMS monitoring. The Forge must demonstrate thermal stability at 2200°C under site utility conditions. CT-08 data package is the *site* birth certificate.

3. **SAT-05 six-batch validation is the performance gate** — Six batches (A, B, C, D, A, Phoenix) with mass balance >99.5%, all outputs spec, twin sync <1 s. This is not a "test" — it is the Forge proving it can execute its purpose at this site.

4. **SOP-002 batch execution is the operational invariant** — The 4-phase batch procedure (feed prep → cascade → slug pour → reset) is the *only* authorized operating mode. No manual overrides, no recipe deviations without ECO (PROD-38). The operations philosophy is: **the Forge runs the synchronization function at 90-min intervals; operators authorize, automation executes.**

These commitments cascade: PROD-30 PM schedules inherit IC re-verification intervals; PROD-31 OPEX model inherits energy/ton from SAT-05; PROD-32 permitting inherits CEMS/IC-7 data; PROD-34 training inherits SOP-002 as the core competency. The Turn: **deployment is the Forge witnessing its own birth at the site — the same mathematical key (synchronization function) that governed manufacturing now governs commissioning, and the same operator witness gates (bolt ceremony, SIF proof, slug pour) that certified manufacturing now certify operations.**

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap is the **site-specific variables that invalidate factory verification** — a Forge that passes CT-01..CT-10 in the factory may fail SAT-01..SAT-05 at site due to variables that cannot be simulated in the factory. Three specific locks:

1. **Ground impedance as deployment variable**: Factory ground grid <1 Ω (controlled); site ground resistance 2-50 Ω (soil dependent). PROD-26 NGR 5A design assumes factory ground. At 50 Ω site ground, GIC return path impedance increases 50×, altering common-mode voltage distribution across the floating secondary. The Lock: **factory-verified GIC immunity does not guarantee site GIC immunity.**

2. **Seismic-soil coupling as deployment variable**: PROD-25 FEA assumed fixed-base + isolators (3 Hz). Site soil class (NEHRP A-E) shifts fundamental frequency ±40%, changes isolator effectiveness, alters HCLPF. A Forge on Class E soil (soft clay) has 1st mode at 1.8 Hz vs 3 Hz design — seismic demand doubles. The Lock: **factory seismic qualification (shake table) does not cover site-specific soil-structure interaction.**

3. **Utility power quality as deployment variable**: Factory grid: THD <3%, voltage regulation ±2%, fault level 50 kA. Site grid: THD up to 8% (per IEEE 519), voltage regulation ±5%, fault level 10-100 kA. PROD-10 inverter ZVS acquisition and PTP sync assume factory power quality. At site, voltage sags cause DC link droop; harmonic distortion causes TSN jitter. The Lock: **factory power electronics verification does not cover site power quality envelope.**

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive is the **site-adaptive synchronization function** — the same fractal gate logic from PROD-27, now parameterized by site-measured variables:

$$SG_{site} = \bigwedge_{i=1}^{10} \left( IC_i(site\_params) \land IC_i.verified \land IC_i.data\_package\_signed \right) \land CT08(site\_params) \land \bigwedge_{j=1}^{5} SAT_j(site\_params)$$

Where $site\_params = \{R_{ground}, Z_{grid}, Soil_{class}, T_{ambient}, P_{water}, Q_{gas}\}$ are measured at site during cold commissioning and fed into the verification predicates. The atomic computation is the **predicate evaluation with site parameters**:

$$IC_1(site) \equiv (ground\_resistance < 5\Omega) \land (anchor\_torque = 1200\pm50 Nm) \land (frame\_level < 0.1mm/m)$$

$$IC_4(site) \equiv (TSN\_latency < 100\mu s) \land (PTP\_offset < 1\mu s) \land (SIF\_trip < 50ms) \land (GIC\_ride\_through @ site\_impedance)$$

$$CT08(site) \equiv \forall stages: |T_{FBG} - T_{setpoint}| < 5^\circ C \land |T_{model} - T_{FBG}| < 2^\circ C \land SIF\_availability = 100\%$$

$$SAT_5(site) \equiv \frac{\sum m_{out}}{\sum m_{in}} > 0.995 \land \forall elements: recovery > target \land twin\_latency < 1s$$

The Key executes at three scales:
1. **Cold (IC-1..IC-10)**: Site parameters measured → predicates evaluated → gates signed
2. **Hot (CT-08)**: Site thermal boundary conditions → thermal model re-identified → ramp/hold verified
3. **Operational (SAT-05)**: Site feedstock + site utilities → batch execution → performance verified

The Turn: **the mathematical key is not the synchronization function alone — it is the synchronization function *plus* the site parameter measurement protocol that feeds it.** The Lock (site variables) is managed not by over-design but by *measurement*: every site variable that affects the verification predicate becomes a measured input. # PROD-30: Maintenance and Sustainment

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this maintenance architecture is **the Forge cannot be maintained using conventional methods because every maintenance action must preserve zero-metal Carrington immunity and SIL-3 safety integrity**. A standard maintenance practice — grounding straps for ESD protection, copper test leads for electrical verification, metallic tools in the hot zone, thermocouple replacement — introduces conductive paths that become GIC antennas during a Carrington event. The Lock: **maintenance must itself be dielectric, non-magnetic, and thermally survivable, using only zero-metal tools, procedures, and verification methods.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any maintenance framework for a 2200°C, zero-metal, SIL-3 pressure vessel with embedded photonics operating under Carrington threat**. Conventional RCM (API 581) assumes metallic structures, grounded electrical systems, and thermocouple-based temperature monitoring. CBM assumes sensor data can be trusted — but FBG drift, AE Felicity ratio shifts, and vibration baseline changes require continuous re-calibration against a physics model that itself degrades. The Key: **a hybrid RCM/CBM/TBM strategy where SIL-3 components are TBM-only (no condition-based extension), FBG/AE/vibration provide the CBM layer with Bayesian health fusion (PROD-28 Keymaker Key), and the 18-month drum swap is the hard RCM limit derived from Weibull statistics with NDT flaw control.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **four non-negotiable maintenance chains**:

1. **18-month drum swap is absolute** — 500 batches = 62.5 days at 8 batches/day. No extension via CBM. The drum IS the pressure boundary; its Weibull life with NDT flaw control (a₀=50 μm) gives N_f >10⁶ cycles, but the Phoenix Protocol demands the drum returns to the Forge for circularity (PROD-22). The swap is the circularity trigger.

2. **SIL-3 SIF proof test annually is immutable** — 24 SIFs, CT-04 protocol, <50 ms trip, 2oo3, PFD_avg<10⁻³. No CBM extension, no risk-based interval extension. This is the safety load-bearing wall.

3. **FBG-as-primary-metrology for maintenance** — No thermocouples, no RTDs, no copper leads. All temperature/strain monitoring for maintenance decisions comes from the 384 FBG channels interrogated at 125 Hz. The Bayesian health state (PROD-28) drives CBM intervals.

4. **QR/Blockchain traceability for every maintenance action** — Every PM work order, CBM alert, NCR, overhaul, and spare part install writes to Hyperledger. The digital twin (PROD-37) ingests this at 10 Hz; the fleet twin optimizes intervals across Forges.

These commitments cascade: PROD-31 OPEX inherits $2.9M/yr consumables + 7-day overhaul downtime; PROD-32 permitting inherits PSM/ASME/IEEE 693 evidence; PROD-34 training inherits competency matrix; PROD-37 twin inherits maintenance data for health model. 2. **Drum life vs. Phoenix Protocol tension**: PROD-25 FEA shows drum N_f >10⁶ cycles with NDT flaw control (a₀=50 μm). At 6 batches/day, that's 456 years theoretical. But PROD-22 Phoenix Protocol requires drum return for circularity (31 generations, 500 batches each = 15,500 batches total per drum lineage). The Lock: **the drum must be swapped at 500 batches not because it fails, but because the circular economy demands its return for flash sinter feedstock.**

3. **Zero-metal tooling for maintenance**: Conventional maintenance uses steel wrenches, copper test leads, magnetic base dial indicators, thermocouples. #### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive is the **risk-based inspection (RBI) likelihood function with SIL-3 constraint**, extending the PROD-28 Bayesian health fusion:

$$P(failure | data, SIL3) = \begin{cases} P_{TBM}(t) & \text{if SIL-3 component} \\ P_{CBM}(data) \times P_{RCM}(design) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

Where:
- $P_{TBM}(t) = 1 - e^{-\lambda t}$ for SIL-3 components (fixed hazard rate λ from proof test data)
- $P_{CBM}(data) = P(health | FBG, AE, vibration, thermal)$ from PROD-28 Bayesian update
- $P_{RCM}(design)$ = design safety factor margin (PROD-25: min SF=1.53× on flange bolts)

The atomic computation is the **next-maintenance-time optimizer**:

$$t_{next} = \arg\min_t \left[ C_{PM}(t) + C_{failure} \times P(failure | t) \right] \quad \text{s.t.} \quad t \leq t_{SIL3-max}$$

Where $t_{SIL3-max} = 1$ year for SIF proof test, 5 years for hydrotest, 18 months for drum swap. The optimizer runs in PROD-37 twin at fleet level, outputting recommended intervals per component per Forge based on site-specific degradation rates.

The Protocol guarantees: if the Forge passes the micro gates with condition data measured, it passes the macro gates at that site.**

*Synthesis: The Lock (Williams) is the zero-metal/SIL-3 maintenance constraint. The Key (Keymaker) is the SIL-3-constrained RBI optimizer with Bayesian health fusion. The Witness (El Segundo) is the operator at four gates where human judgment authorizes what sensors measure. Together they form the sustainment architecture: the Forge maintains itself through light in glass fiber, validated by proof test, certified by human witness, recorded in blockchain, optimized by fleet twin. Maintenance is not a department — it is the Forge's immune system.*

## CSMFAB000000000130 — Aegis-Forge I Preventive Maintenance, Condition-Based Monitoring, Spares & Overhaul
### ISO 9001/AS9100 Aligned, API 581 RBI, IEC 61508 SIL-3, ASME BPVC Sec VIII/X, IEEE 693, NFPA 70E
**Document Number:** CSMFAB000000000130 (Product Document 30 of 40)
**Series:** Aegis-Forge Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator (TCIMS)
**Prepared by:** Carrington Storm Motors, Safe Pod Engineering Company, Fabrication Division
**Date:** November 2026 | **Classification:** Product Specification — Maintenance Engineering

## 1. Maintenance Strategy

### 1.1 Philosophy: RCM + CBM + TBM Hybrid

The Aegis-Forge I maintenance strategy integrates three methodologies, constrained by SIL-3 safety and zero-metal Carrington immunity:

| Methodology | Scope | Driver |
|---|---|---|
| **Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM)** | Safety-critical systems (SIS, pressure boundary, GIC immunity) | IEC 61508 SIL-3 mandates; failure consequences unacceptable |
| **Condition-Based Monitoring (CBM)** | Rotating equipment, thermal systems, dielectric integrity | FBG/AE/vibration provide continuous health data (PROD-28) |
| **Time-Based Maintenance (TBM)** | Consumables, calibration, regulatory inspections | Fixed intervals for non-monitorable degradation |

**Hybrid Rule:** SIL-3 SIF components (24 SIFs) follow TBM (proof test intervals) *overriding* CBM — no condition-based extension for safety functions. All other systems use CBM with RCM-derived base intervals.

### 1.2 Maintenance Organization

| Role | Responsibility | Qualification |
|---|---|---|
| **Maintenance Manager** | PM program ownership, resource planning, KPI tracking | PE + 10 yr nuclear/pressure vessel |
| **Mechanical Engineer** | Drum, vessel, carousel, frame, port valves | PE + 5 yr ceramics/composites |
| **Electrical Engineer** | Coil bank, power electronics, FBG, TSN/PTP | PE + 5 yr power electronics |
| **SIS Engineer** | SIL-3 SIF proof tests, PFD tracking, re-certification | TÜV FS Expert (IEC 61508) |
| **NDT Level III** | UT/CT/AE/IR program, procedure approval | ASNT Level III (UT, CT, ET, AE) |
| **Metrology Engineer** | Calibration program, CMM/UT/FBG standards | ISO 17025 assessor |
| **Maintenance Technicians (×6)** | Execute PM/CBM work orders, dual-verify critical tasks | PROD-34 L2/L3 cert |

### 1.3 Maintenance KPIs

| KPI | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| **Planned Maintenance Compliance (PMC)** | >95% | PM work orders completed on schedule / due |
| **Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)** | >50,000 hrs (system) | PROD-37 fleet twin |
| **Mean Time To Repair (MTTR)** | <4 hrs (critical) | CMMS work order data |
| **Spare Parts Availability** | 100% critical spares on-site | Inventory audit |
| **FBG Channel Survival** | 384/384 active | PROD-28 CT-06 + in-service |
| **SIF PFD_avg** | <1×10⁻³ (SIL-3 subset) | CT-04 proof test data |
| **CAPA Closure** | 100% within 30 days | PROD-28 CAPA tracker |
| **Overhaul Schedule Adherence** | ±3 days | CMMS schedule vs. actual |

## 2. Drum Maintenance (Assembly A-01/A-03)

### 2.1 Drum Body (ZrB₂-SiC) — Detailed Procedures

#### 2.1.1 Annual UT Phased Array Volumetric Inspection (PROD-30-WI-001)

**Scope:** 100% volumetric inspection of drum wall (35 mm thickness, 600 mm ID, 800 mm length)
**Equipment:** Olympus OmniScan MX2, 5 MHz 64-element PA probe, wedges 45°/60°/70° (shear wave), 0° (longitudinal)
**Calibration:** IIW Type 1 block (ref), DAC curve 80% FSH, TCG normalization per ASTM E2700
**Scan Pattern:** Helical raster 2 mm × 2 mm; encoder-coupled; 100% coverage; 360° × 800 mm
**Personnel:** ASNT Level II UT (minimum), Level III review for indications
**Duration:** 8 hours (setup 2 hr, scan 4 hr, analysis 2 hr)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- No indications >0.5 mm flat equivalent (DAC 20%)
- No indications >2 mm Ø equivalent (DAC 20%)
- No planar indications in liner pin heat-affected zones (HAZ)
- Signal-to-noise >6 dB on all scans
- Liner-to-drum bond line: no unbonded areas >5 mm dia

**Reporting:** C-scan images (amplitude + depth), A-scan at each indication, depth/sizing per ASME Sec V Appendix IV, comparison to baseline (FA data package)

#### 2.1.2 Biennial CT High-Resolution (PROD-30-WI-002)

**Scope:** Full drum body including FBG channels, porosity distribution, grain structure
**Equipment:** Nikon XTH 320, 320 kV, 200 μm voxel, 1000 mm detector
**Calibration:** NIST-traceable density standards (Al, Ti, ZrO₂); geometric phantom (wire grid)
**Reconstruction:** Feldkamp algorithm; beam hardening correction; ring artifact reduction
**Analysis:** Porosity distribution (volume %, size, sphericity per ASTM E2921); FBG channel position ±100 μm; grain size distribution (EBSD correlation)
**Personnel:** ASNT Level II CT (minimum), Level III approval
**Duration:** 8 hours (setup 1 hr, scan 5 hr, reconstruction 2 hr)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Open porosity <0.05% (Archimedes cross-check)
- Closed porosity <0.2% volume; max pore size <0.5 mm
- FBG channel position per design drawing ±100 μm
- No new porosity clusters vs. baseline (FA CT)

#### 2.1.3 FBG Survival & Calibration (Continuous + Monthly)

**Continuous Monitoring (PROD-28 Sec 5.1):**
- Interrogator: Micron Optics si425 (125 Hz, 4 ch/module × 96 modules)
- Channels: 128 drum (16 per zone × 8 zones) + 16 reference
- Auto-alert: Λ > 10 (Bayesian likelihood ratio from PROD-28 Keymaker Key)
- Data retention: 2 years rolling (compressed), 10 years summary

**Monthly Calibration Verification (PROD-30-WI-003):**
- Reference temperatures: 25°C (ambient), 500°C, 1000°C, 1500°C, 2000°C (cal furnace)
- Method: Interrogator sweep + linear fit λ = a + bT
- Acceptance: R² > 0.999; drift <0.1 nm/°C from PQR-FS-001 baseline; all 128 channels active
- Documentation: Calibration certificate per channel, auto-committed to Hyperledger

### 2.2 Liner System (3-Zone Replaceable) — Detailed Procedures

#### 2.2.1 Zone A (Ti₃AlC₂ MAX Phase, 0-200 mm axial)

**250-Batch Inspection (PROD-30-WI-004):**
- UT bond test: 10 MHz focused transducer, through-transmission
- Acceptance: No unbonded area >5 mm dia at Si₃N₄ pin interfaces (12 pins/zone)
- Visual: No MAX phase oxidation (gold→gray color change); no crack initiation at pin holes
- Dimensional: Pin clearance 0.05±0.01 mm (air gauge)

**Replacement Procedure (250 batches):**
1. Drum cool-down to <50°C (CT-08 reverse profile)
2. Port valve removal (8 valves, PROD-30-WI-010)
3. Zone A liner extraction (hydraulic puller, BFRP fixture)
4. New liner installation (interference fit 0.03 mm, LN₂ shrink)
5. Pin reinstallation (Si₃N₄, torque 25 N·m ±2 N·m, dual-verify)
6. FBG re-splice (PROD-30-WI-003) + cal verification
7. Bolt ceremony (24× M24 ZrO₂, 160 N·m ±5 N·m)

#### 2.2.2 Zone B (3Y-TZP, 200-500 mm axial)

**125-Batch Inspection (PROD-30-WI-005):**
- Visual + UT: No cracking at pin holes; pin clearance 0.05±0.01 mm
- FBG check: Zone B channels (16) drift <0.25%/1000 hrs

**Replacement (250 batches):** Same as Zone A but ZrO₂ pins

#### 2.2.3 Zone C (ZrO₂ Foam, 500-800 mm axial)

**250-Batch Inspection (PROD-30-WI-006):**
- Gamma densitometer: 3.2±0.1 g/cm³ uniform radial
- Visual: No foam collapse, no crack propagation from pin holes

**Replacement (500 batches, with drum swap):** Full drum swap includes Zone C replacement

### 2.3 Drum Life Management

| Parameter | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Design Life** | 500 batches | Phoenix Protocol circularity (PROD-22) |
| **Theoretical Fatigue Life** | >10⁶ cycles | PROD-25: N_f with a₀=50 μm |
| **Creep Life (2200°C, 50 MPa)** | >100,000 hrs | PROD-25: ε̇ = 3×10⁻⁹ s⁻¹ |
| **Swap Trigger** | 500 batches OR NCR Critical | Whichever occurs first |
| **Refurbishment Path** | Hydromet → carbothermal → flash sinter | PROD-22 Sec 7 (31 generations) |
