## 3. Vessel Maintenance (Assembly A-06/A-07)

### 3.1 BFRP Pressure Vessel — Detailed Procedures

#### 3.1.1 AE Continuous Monitoring (PROD-28 Sec 5.1, PROD-30-WI-007)

**System:** Physical Acoustics PCI-2, 8 channels, 40 dB preamp, 100 kHz–1 MHz
**Sensors:** 8× R15α broadband at 45° increments, 2 axial positions (300 mm, 900 mm)
**Threshold:** 40 dB AE; hit definition: peak > threshold, duration >50 μs
**Analysis:** Source location (ΔT triangulation ±50 mm); b-value; RA-value; Felicity ratio
**Alert Logic (Auto):**
- Hit rate >2× baseline (30-day rolling) → Alert Level 1 (log only)
- Felicity ratio <1.0 for >1 hour → Alert Level 2 (NCR auto-generated)
- Cluster >10 hits/hr in 100 mm radius → Alert Level 3 (immediate inspection)

**Monthly AE Report (Auto-generated):**
- Daily hit rate trend (30-day rolling)
- Felicity ratio trend
- Source location map (cumulative)
- b-value / RA-value evolution
- Comparison to PROD-25 FEA stress concentrations

#### 3.1.2 Annual UT Phased Array (PROD-30-WI-008)

**Scope:** 100% vessel wall (18 mm BFRP/Elium®), flange transitions, gas ports, FBG penetrations
**Equipment:** Olympus OmniScan MX2, 2.25 MHz 64-element PA probe, wedges 45°/60°/70°
**Calibration:** ASTM E2700 reference blocks (BFRP laminate, 18 mm)
**Scan Pattern:** Raster 2 mm × 2 mm; 100% coverage
**Special Focus:** Gas port penetrations (stress concentration 4.2× per PROD-25), FBG penetrations, stiffening ring attachments

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- No delaminations >10 mm diameter
- No porosity clusters >3 pores in 25 mm²
- No fiber breakage indications (Tsai-Wu FI <0.25)
- Flange transition: no indications >5 mm

#### 3.1.3 Hydrotest (5-Year Interval, PROD-30-WI-009)

**Procedure:** Per ASME BPVC Section X, Article 8
- Test pressure: 15 bar N₂ (1.5× design pressure 10 bar)
- Hold time: 30 minutes minimum
- Temperature compensation: ±0.5°C monitoring
- Leak test: Helium mass spectrometer, sniff test all joints
- Acceptance: Zero pressure drop (temp compensated); He leak <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s

**Post-Hydrotest:** AE baseline re-establishment (24 hr monitoring at 10 bar)

#### 3.1.4 Monthly Visual Inspection (VT-1, PROD-30-WI-010)

**Scope:** External surface (glaze), flange faces, bolt heads, port penetrations, anchor points
**Criteria:**
- YInMn Blue glaze: No cracking, spalling, discoloration >5% area
- Flange faces: No PEEK CF40 creep >0.5 mm; bolt head contact uniform
- Anchor bolts: No corrosion, torque marks intact, isolation pads intact
- Aerogel: No settlement gaps >2 mm at vessel/frame interface

#### 3.1.5 Monthly IR Thermography (PROD-30-WI-011)

**Equipment:** FLIR T1040, 1024×768, <20 mK NETD, 24° lens
**Conditions:** Forge at steady-state Stage 8 (2200°C drum), 500 kW total power
**Analysis:** ΔT vs. baseline (commissioning IR map); hotspot detection; thermal gradient mapping
**Alert Thresholds:**
- Any point >5°C above baseline → Alert Level 1
- New hotspot not in baseline → Alert Level 2
- Thermal gradient >50°C/100 mm → Alert Level 2

#### 3.1.6 Annual Aerogel Density Verification (PROD-30-WI-012)

**Equipment:** Gamma densitometer (Cs-137, 5 mm collimated beam)
**Scan Pattern:** Radial profiles at 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°; 5 mm step; 3 axial stations
**Acceptance:** 0.12±0.01 g/cm³ uniform radial (no gradient >0.02 g/cm³ over 50 mm)
**Action if Failed:** Vacuum-assisted re-infusion (PROD-27 Sec 3 correction)

#### 3.1.7 Biennial Glaze Adhesion Pull-Off (PROD-30-WI-013)

**Standard:** ASTM D4541 (10% sample = 24 dollies on 900 mm ID vessel)
**Acceptance:** >10 MPa; failure mode cohesive in adhesive (not glaze)
**Action if Failed:** Localized glaze repair (plasma spray touch-up) or full re-spray

## 4. Port Valve Maintenance (Assembly A-04 ×8)

### 4.1 Quarterly Thermal Actuation Check (PROD-30-WI-014)

**Conditions:** Furnace at 680°C ΔT (ambient to 700°C), 50°C/min ramp
**Measurement:** LVDT on piston rod (0.01 mm resolution) + FBG strain on actuator body
**Acceptance:** 3.6±0.2 mm deflection; repeatable 3 consecutive cycles; no hysteresis >0.1 mm
**Data Capture:** Force-deflection curve; thermal strain vs. temperature; FBG wavelength shift

### 4.2 Quarterly Leak Rate Test (PROD-30-WI-015)

**Conditions:** Valve closed, 5 bar N₂ upstream, He mass spectrometer downstream
**Acceptance:** <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s (equivalent to <1 sccm He)
**Action if Failed:** Braze joint UT inspection; piston/sleeve dimension check; seal replacement

### 4.3 Annual Braze Joint UT (PROD-30-WI-016)

**Scope:** Ti₃AlC₂ actuator to ZrB₂-SiC sleeve (Ag-CuO-TiO₂ braze, 50±10 μm)
**Equipment:** 20 MHz focused UT, water coupling (dielectric)
**Acceptance:** No voids >50 μm; joint thickness 50±10 μm; TiO₂ reaction layer <5 μm
**Reference:** PROD-27 PQR-BR-001 baseline

### 4.4 Annual FBG Strain Calibration (PROD-30-WI-017)

**Method:** Known weights on piston (0, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 N)
**Acceptance:** 0.1 nm/με ±2% linearity; R² > 0.999; hysteresis <1%
**Cross-check:** LVDT displacement vs. FBG strain (thermal actuation)

### 4.5 500-Batch ZrO₂ Piston Inspection (PROD-30-WI-018)

**Scope:** Visual + dimensional (CMM) + surface profilometry
**Acceptance:** Clearance 0.05±0.01 mm; no wear >0.02 mm; Ra <0.4 μm; no radial cracking
**Action if Failed:** Replace piston + sleeve as matched set (PROD-09)

### 4.6 2000-Cycle Actuator Replacement (PROD-30-WI-019)

**Life Limit:** 2000 thermal cycles (250 days at 8 batches/day)
**Procedure:** Full port valve assembly removal → new actuator/piston install → actuation check + leak test + FBG cal
**Note:** Actuator includes Ti₃AlC₂ body, ZrO₂ piston, PEEK CF40 spring, FBG embed

---

## 5. Coil Bank Maintenance (Assembly A-09 ×8 zones)

### 5.1 Monthly Resonance & ZVS Verification (PROD-30-WI-020)

**Per Zone Procedure:**
1. Impedance analyzer sweep (1 kHz–200 kHz): resonant frequency, Q factor
2. Power analyzer: ZVS verification at 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% load
3. Thermal: IR camera at 100% load (30 min soak)
4. Data: Frequency vs. zone table ±1%; Q >150; ZVS phase <5°

**Zone-Specific Targets:**

| Zone | Stage | Target Freq | Power Range | Q Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z1 | 1 (Drying) | 100 kHz ±1% | 0–50 kW | >150 |
| Z2 | 2 (Polymer) | 100 kHz ±1% | 0–50 kW | >150 |
| Z3 | 3 (Pyrolysis) | 50 kHz ±1% | 50–80 kW | >150 |
| Z4 | 4 (Low-Temp) | 10 kHz ±1% | 80–150 kW | >150 |
| Z5 | 5 (Al) | 10 kHz ±1% | 80–150 kW | >150 |
| Z6 | 6 (Cu/PM) | 5 kHz ±1% | 100–200 kW | >150 |
| Z7 | 7 (Fe) | 2 kHz ±1% | 150–350 kW | >150 |
| Z8 | 8 (Mineral) | 1 kHz ±1% | 200–500 kW | >150 |

### 5.2 Monthly FBG Cross-Talk Check (PROD-30-WI-021)

**Method:** Interrogator single-channel excitation + adjacent channel monitoring
**Acceptance:** Adjacent channel isolation >40 dB; WDM channel spacing 0.8 nm maintained
**Action if Failed:** FBG re-splice (PROD-30-WI-003) or channel remapping

### 5.3 Quarterly Cold Plate Leak Test (PROD-30-WI-022)

**Method:** He mass spectrometer, 10 bar He, 30 min hold per zone
**Acceptance:** <10⁻⁹ mbar·L/s (PROD-28 Sec 3.4)
**Action if Failed:** Cold plate removal → TIM (In foil) inspection → re-bond or replace

### 5.4 Annual PEX-a Integrity (PROD-30-WI-023)

**Method:** Pressure decay test @ 10 bar, 1 hour
**Acceptance:** <0.1 bar/hr pressure drop
**Visual:** No kinking, abrasion, UV degradation, fitting corrosion

### 5.5 Biennial Inductor Visual + CT (PROD-30-WI-024)

**Visual:** Cu tube insulation (Al₂O₃ coating), support spacers (BFRP), connections
**CT:** 50 μm voxel, focus on conductor insulation, braze joints, support integrity
**Acceptance:** No insulation cracking; no conductor displacement >0.5 mm; no braze voids >100 μm

## 6. Power Electronics Maintenance (Assembly A-10 ×8 modules)

### 6.1 Monthly DC Link & ZVS Verification (PROD-30-WI-025)

**DC Link Charge Test:**
- Oscilloscope capture (100 MHz BW, 1 GS/s): 0→800V in 500 ms; no overshoot >850V
- Pre-charge resistor thermal check (IR): <80°C after charge

**ZVS Acquisition Verification:**
- V/I ramp from 10% to 100% load in 10% steps
- Phase <5° at all points; v_DS zero-crossing before gate drive
- Gate drive voltage: 6V ±0.2V (LMG1210), rise/fall <2 ns

### 6.2 Quarterly Thermal Soak Test (PROD-30-WI-026)

**Conditions:** 500 kW continuous, 30 minutes, cooling at design flow (500 L/min, 30°C inlet)
**Measurements:**
- GaN junction temperature (calculated from T_c + R_θJC × P_loss): <125°C
- Cold plate ΔT (inlet-outlet): <15°C
- Capacitor bank temperature: <85°C (electrolytic), <105°C (film)
- Thermal imaging: No hotspots >5°C above zone average

### 6.3 Quarterly GIC Ride-Through Test (PROD-30-WI-027)

**Equipment:** Portable Helmholtz coil (1 m diameter, 100 A/m, 0.1–10 Hz sweep)
**Procedure:** Per PROD-26 Sec 3.3, PROD-23 CT-07 protocol
**Acceptance:** Zero spurious SIF trips; zero data loss (TSN/PTP/FBG); zero inverter trips
**Monitoring:** All 384 FBG channels, TSN latency, PTP offset, DC link voltage

### 6.4 Annual EMI Verification (PROD-30-WI-028)

**Standard:** CISPR 11 Class A (conducted 150 kHz–30 MHz, radiated 30 MHz–1 GHz)
**Conditions:** All 8 zones at 100% load, Forge at Stage 8 steady-state
**Acceptance:** >20 dB margin on all limits
**Action if Failed:** Common-mode choke re-tune; POF routing check; filter capacitor ESR check

### 6.5 Quarterly SIL-3 SIF Injection Test (PROD-30-WI-029)

**Per Module (3 SIFs/module × 8 modules = 24 SIFs):**
- Overpressure (vessel >11 bar)
- Overtemperature (drum >2250°C or dT/dt >100°C/s)
- Vibration (frame >1.5g RMS)
- GIC (common-mode >5 V on floating secondary)
- Loss of comms (TSN VLAN 10 heartbeat >10 ms)

**Acceptance:** Trip <50 ms; 2oo3 channel agreement; SOE timestamp <1 ms skew; FBG data freeze at trip
**Documentation:** SIF test report per module; PFD_avg calculation update

### 6.6 Monthly POF Attenuation Check (PROD-30-WI-030)

**Equipment:** OTDR (1550 nm, 10 μs pulse, 100 km range)
**Acceptance:** <0.2 dB/m; splices <0.5 dB; return loss >50 dB
**Action if Failed:** Re-splice affected segments (PROD-30-WI-003); OTDR trace archive

### 6.7 Annual Capacitor Bank ESR Check (PROD-30-WI-031)

**Equipment:** Impedance analyzer (100 Hz–1 MHz)
**Acceptance:** ESR <1.5× initial (factory baseline); capacitance ±5% of nominal
**Trend:** ESR vs. time (exponential fit); predict end-of-life at 2× initial

### 6.8 GaN Module Replacement (50,000 hrs, PROD-30-WI-032)

**Hot-Swap Capability:** Module rack designed for live removal (TSN/PTP/POF disconnect <30 s)
**Procedure:**
1. Zone power reduction to 0% (PID ramp 10%/s)
2. TSN VLAN 10 graceful disconnect (PTP holdover 24 hr)
3. POF disconnect (BFRP connector, push-pull)
4. Cold plate quick-disconnect (PEX-a, zero-leak)
5. Module extract (BFRP handles, 2-person lift 800 kg)
6. New module install → reverse sequence → acceptance per PROD-28 Sec 2.5

## 7. Frame, Carousel & Bearings (Assembly A-12)

### 7.1 Annual Frame Dimensions (PROD-30-WI-033)

**Equipment:** CMM (Hexagon Global, 3000×2000×1500 mm, ±2 μm accuracy)
**Points:** 200+ measurement points (bolt holes, lifting lugs, isolator mounts, bearing seats)
**Acceptance:** ±1 mm length, ±0.5 mm diagonal, bolt hole pattern ±0.1 mm
**Comparison:** Baseline (FA CMM report) + thermal growth model (PROD-25)

### 7.2 Biennial Isolator Stiffness Test (PROD-30-WI-034)

**Method:** Static load test (hydraulic jack, 500 kN capacity) + LVDT displacement
**Vertical:** 2.5 MN/m ±5% (250 kN → 0.1 mm deflection)
**Horizontal:** 0.8 MN/m ±5% (80 kN → 0.1 mm deflection)
**Damping:** Logarithmic decrement from free decay >15%
**Acceptance:** Per PROD-25 Sec 4.2 updated values

### 7.3 Monthly Carousel Indexing (PROD-30-WI-035)

**Method:** Encoder (Heidenhain ROC 425, 26-bit) + FBG strain on bearing housing
**Procedure:** 8-position sequence (45° steps), 5 cycles each direction
**Acceptance:** <2 s per index; 0.01° resolution; position repeatability ±0.005°; vibration <0.5 g RMS

### 7.4 Continuous Bearing Vibration Monitoring (PROD-30-WI-036)

**Sensors:** 4× accelerometers (PCB 352C33, 100 mV/g, 0.5–10 kHz) + 2× FBG on bearing housing
**Sampling:** 1 kHz continuous; FFT (0.5–500 Hz); envelope analysis (1–5 kHz)
**Baseline:** Commissioning data (30 days steady operation)
**Alert Logic:**
- Overall RMS >2× baseline → Alert Level 1 (trend)
- Bearing defect frequency (BPFI/BPFO/BSF/FTF) amplitude >6 dB baseline → Alert Level 2 (NCR)
- Spectral kurtosis >4 → Alert Level 3 (immediate inspection)

### 7.5 2000-Batch Bearing Inspection (PROD-30-WI-037)

**Scope:** Si₃N₄ ball / ZrO₂ race hybrid ceramic bearings (4 per carousel)
**Procedure:** Removal → visual + dimensional (CMM) + spin test (1000 RPM, 30 min)
**Acceptance:**
- No spalling, pitting, discoloration on balls/races
- Runout <5 μm (radial + axial)
- Preload torque: 5 N·m ±10% (N₂ film 0.1 bar)
- Vibration at 1000 RPM: <0.5 g RMS
- FBG strain on housing: <50 με static

### 7.6 Quarterly Mold Dimensions (PROD-30-WI-038)

**Scope:** 8× ZrO₂ molds (carousel positions 1-8)
**Equipment:** CMM (per 7.1) + optical comparator (profile)
**Acceptance:** 0.1 mm tolerance (ISO 8062 CT7); wall thickness 25±0.1 mm; base flatness <0.05 mm
**Action if Failed:** Mold replacement (spare set on-site); dimension mapping to slug quality data

## 8. Major Overhaul (18-Month Drum Swap Cycle)

### 8.1 Overhaul Sequence (168 hours / 7 days)

| Day | Activity | Duration | Resources | Key Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Day 1** | Shutdown, cool-down (CT-08 reverse), isolation (LOTO) | 12 hr | 2 ME, 1 EE, 1 Safety | Drum <50°C; vessel <50°C; all zones 0 power |
| **Day 2** | Drum removal (crane), vessel flange unbolt (bolt ceremony reverse) | 16 hr | 2 ME, 1 EE, 1 QA | AE monitoring during unbolt; flange face inspection |
| **Day 3** | New drum installation (IC-2 re-execution), FBG splice + cal | 16 hr | 2 ME, 1 EE, 1 SIS | Bearing fit; FBG 128/128 active; cal R²>0.999 |
| **Day 4** | Vessel re-bolt (bolt ceremony), hydrotest (IC-2), AE baseline | 12 hr | 2 ME, 1 QA | Dual-verify 160 N·m; hydrotest PASS; AE baseline set |
| **Day 5** | Coil bank verification (IC-3 abbr), cold plate leak | 8 hr | 1 EE, 1 ME | Resonance ±1%; Q>150; leak <10⁻⁹ mbar·L/s |
| **Day 6** | Power electronics verification (IC-3 abbr), SIF proof (CT-04) | 12 hr | 1 EE, 1 SIS | ZVS <5°; SIF proof PASS; GIC ride-through PASS |
| **Day 7** | Hot commissioning (CT-08 abbr), SAT-05 Batch 1, handover | 16 hr | Full crew | CT-08 thermal match; Batch 1 mass balance >99.5% |

### 8.2 Overhaul Life Limits & Refurbishment Paths

| Component | Life Limit | Refurbishment Path | PROD-22 Circularity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ZrB₂-SiC Drum** | 500 batches | Hydromet (HCl leach) → carbothermal (ZrO₂+C) → flash sinter | Gen 1→31 (31 generations) |
| **BFRP Vessel** | 15,000 batches (20 yr) | Hydrotest + full UT/CT; glaze re-spray if needed | Solvolysis (Elium® recovery) → re-wind |
| **Port Valve Actuators** | 2000 cycles | Replace Ti₃AlC₂ actuator + ZrO₂ piston | Cl₂ extraction → re-synth (20 gen) |
| **PEEK CF40 Seals** | 1000 batches | Replace all flange seals | Mechanical recycle (shred → re-mold) |
| **GaN Inverter Modules** | 50,000 hrs | Replace module (hot-swap capable) | GaN die recovery (electrochemical) |
| **PEX-a Coolant Lines** | 10 years | Replace all PEX-a circuits | Thermal recycle (pyrolysis) |
| **FBG Interrogator** | 5 years | Replace interrogator + recalibrate all channels | Electronics recycle (WEEE) |
| **TSN Switches** | 7 years | Replace BFRP-housed switches | Electronics recycle |
| **Bearings (Si₃N₄/ZrO₂)** | 35,800 hrs (L10) | Replace bearing cartridge | Ceramic recycle (SPS) |

## 11. Predictive Maintenance (CBM)

### 11.1 Predictive Algorithms (PROD-37 Digital Twin)

| Parameter | Sensor | Algorithm | Alert Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FBG wavelength drift | 384 FBG @ 125 Hz | Recursive Bayesian (PROD-28) | Λ > 10 | Auto-NCR → CAPA |
| AE Felicity ratio | 8× R15α vessel | Exponential smoothing + change point | Felicity <1.0 >1 hr | NCR → UT inspection |
| Vibration RMS | Bearings, carousel, frame | Spectral kurtosis + envelope | >2× baseline (30-day) | NCR → bearing inspection |
| Thermal model residual | Zone RTUs (1 kHz) | RLS adaptive filter | >2°C RMS >10 min | NCR → cold plate check |
| POF attenuation | OTDR continuous | Linear regression + breakpoint | >0.25 dB/m or step >0.1 dB | NCR → splice inspection |
| Capacitor bank ESR | Monthly impedance | Exponential degradation model | ESR >1.5× initial | Schedule replacement |
| SIF response time | Quarterly test | Weibull degradation | >35 ms (target 25 ms) | NCR + partial stroke |

| FBG calibration | Monthly | Fixed (drift accumulation) | N/A |
| GIC ride-through | Quarterly | Fixed (grid impedance changes) | N/A |

### 11.3 Detailed Predictive Algorithm Specifications

#### 11.3.1 FBG Drift Bayesian Tracker (PROD-28 Sec 5.1 Keymaker Key)

**Mathematical Foundation:** Recursive Bayesian update on Weibull degradation parameter β

```python
# Pseudocode for FBG drift tracker (executes at 125 Hz per channel)
def fbg_drift_update(channel_id, lambda_measured, t):
    # Prior: beta ~ Gamma(alpha, beta)  -- shape/rate from commissioning
    # Likelihood: lambda = lambda_0 * exp(beta * t) + noise
    # Posterior: conjugate update
    
    alpha_post = alpha_prior + 0.5
    beta_post = beta_prior + 0.5 * (lambda_measured - lambda_predicted)^2 / sigma^2
    
    # Hazard rate h(t) = beta / eta * (t/eta)^(beta-1)
    # Likelihood ratio Lambda = h(t|data) / h(t|baseline)
    
    Lambda = compute_likelihood_ratio(alpha_post, beta_post, alpha_baseline, beta_baseline)
    
    if Lambda > 10:
        trigger_ncr(channel_id, "FBG_DRIFT", Lambda, t)
    elif Lambda > 5:
        trigger_alert(channel_id, "FBG_DRIFT_WARN", Lambda, t)
    
    return alpha_post, beta_post, Lambda
```

**Channel-Specific Baselines (PQR-FS-001):**
- Drum zones 1-8 (16 ch/zone): λ₀ = 1550.000 nm @ 25°C; sensitivity = 10.2 pm/°C ±0.3 pm/°C
- Vessel AE channels (8 ch): λ₀ = 1545.000 nm; sensitivity = 10.0 pm/°C ±0.2 pm/°C
- Port valve actuators (8 ch × 2 = 16 ch): λ₀ = 1555.000 nm; sensitivity = 1.8 pm/με ±0.1 pm/με
- Coil bank cold plates (8 ch): λ₀ = 1560.000 nm; sensitivity = 10.5 pm/°C ±0.4 pm/°C
- Reference channels (16 ch): λ₀ = various; used for common-mode rejection

**Data Compression:** 125 Hz raw → 1 Hz min/mean/max/σ stored (99.2% compression); 10-year retention on PROD-37 time-series DB

#### 11.3.2 AE Felicity Ratio Change-Point Detection

**Algorithm:** Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) + Binary Segmentation Change-Point

```
Felicity_ratio(t) = cumulative_energy(t) / cumulative_energy(t - Δt)
  where Δt = 1 hour rolling window

EWMA: z_t = λ * F_t + (1-λ) * z_{t-1}, λ = 0.1
Control limits: LCL = μ_0 - 2.7σ√(λ/(2-λ)), UCL = μ_0 + 2.7σ√(λ/(2-λ))
  μ_0 = 1.2 (baseline from PROD-25 FEA), σ = 0.05 (commissioning)

Change-point: Binary segmentation on z_t sequence (min segment = 24 hrs)
  Test statistic: max |z_t - z_{t-1}| > 3σ
  If detected: re-baseline μ_0, σ from new segment; trigger NCR if Felicity < 1.0
```

**Auto-Response Integration:**
- Alert Level 1 (Felicity 1.05–1.1): Log only, increase AE sampling to 1 MHz
- Alert Level 2 (Felicity 1.0–1.05 > 1 hr): Auto-NCR, schedule UT inspection within 72 hrs
- Alert Level 3 (Felicity < 1.0 > 1 hr): Auto-NCR + immediate partial shutdown (drum power <50%)

#### 11.3.3 Vibration Spectral Kurtosis + Envelope Analysis

**Algorithm (ISO 13373-2 / PROD-28 Sec 5.2):**
1. Raw acceleration: 1 kHz sampling, 4 ch per bearing housing (2 axial, 2 radial)
2. Demodulation: Hilbert transform of bandpass (1–5 kHz) → envelope signal
3. Spectral Kurtosis (SK): SK(f) = E[X⁴]/E[X²]² - 2 (Gaussian = 0)
4. Optimal band: max SK(f) over 1–5 kHz → band for envelope spectrum
5. Bearing defect frequencies (Si₃N₄/ZrO₂, 60 mm PD, 8 balls, 15° contact):
   - BPFI = 4.4 × RPM; BPFO = 3.6 × RPM; BSF = 2.3 × RPM; FTF = 0.45 × RPM
6. Alert: BPFI/BPFO/BSF amplitude > 6 dB baseline → NCR

**Baseline Re-Establishment:** Every 500 batches (drum swap) or after bearing replacement

#### 11.3.4 Thermal Model Residual RLS Adaptive Filter

**Algorithm (Recursive Least Squares - PROD-24/28 fusion):**
```
State: θ_t = [k_cond, k_conv, k_rad]^T  (thermal conductance parameters)
Measurement: y_t = T_actual - T_predicted (per zone, 1 kHz RTU)
Update: P_t = (I - K_t H) P_{t-1}; θ_t = θ_{t-1} + K_t (y_t - H θ_{t-1})
        K_t = P_{t-1} H^T (H P_{t-1} H^T + R)^{-1}
Alert: ||y_t||_RMS > 2°C over 10 min window → NCR + cold plate leak check
```

**Zone-Specific Parameters:**
- Zones 1-2 (100 kHz): k_cond dominates (conduction through drum wall)
- Zones 3-4 (50/10 kHz): k_conv + k_rad (gas convection + radiation)
- Zones 5-8 (10-1 kHz): k_rad dominates (2200°C radiation)

#### 11.3.5 POF Attenuation Linear Regression with Breakpoint Detection

**Algorithm:**
- Continuous OTDR: 1550 nm, 10 μs pulse, 1 Hz sweep (all 384 channels)
- Per-channel: α(t) = -10/L * log10(P_received/P_launch) dB/m
- Rolling linear regression (30-day window): α(t) = a + b*t
- Breakpoint: CUSUM on residuals > 5σ → step change (splice failure, macrobend)
- Alert: b > 0.001 dB/m/day OR step > 0.1 dB → NCR

### 12.4 Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Integration

**Trigger:** Any NCR Critical (PROD-28 Sec 4) or Alert Level 3 (Sec 11)
**Method:** 8D with physics-based fault tree (PROD-25/26/28 fusion)

#### 12.4.1 RCA Process Flow

```
D0: Team Formation (QA Lead + SME: ME/EE/SIS/NDT/Metrology)
D1: Problem Statement (What, Where, When, Extent, IS/IS NOT)
D2: Interim Containment (Forge status: run/reduced/stop; safety first)
D3: Root Cause Identification
    - Fault Tree Top Event: e.g., "FBG channel dropout Zone 3"
    - Gates: AND/OR logic from PROD-25 FEA + PROD-26 GIC + PROD-28 NCR history
    - Basic Events: FBG fiber fracture, interrogator failure, splice degradation, 
      thermal gradient > design, GIC event, vibration fatigue, installation error
    - Quantification: Bayesian network (PROD-37) with prior from Weibull (PROD-25)
D4: Permanent Corrective Action (design fix / procedure change / interval change)
D5: Verification (pilot implementation + 30-day monitoring)
D6: Implementation (ECO via PROD-38; training update via PROD-34)
D7: Prevention (lessons learned; PM/CBM interval update; spare part spec change)
D8: Team Recognition & Closure (Hyperledger commit + PROD-37 twin update)
```

#### 12.4.2 Example Fault Tree: Drum FBG Channel Dropout

```
TOP: Channel dropout Zone 3 (1 of 16 channels)
├── Fiber fracture (AND)
│   ├── Thermal stress > 200 MPa (OR)
│   │   ├── dT/dt > 150°C/s (SIF would trip)
│   │   ├── Cold plate leak → local quench (AE detect)
│   │   └── Coil resonance shift → hotspot (ZVS monitor)
│   └── Mechanical fatigue (OR)
│       ├── Vibration > 2g RMS (bearing failure)
│       ├── Drum distortion > 0.5 mm (CT detect)
│       └── Installation bend radius < 25 mm
├── Splice degradation (AND)
│   ├── Thermal cycling fatigue (500 cycles = design life)
│   ├── Moisture ingress (dielectric breach → GIC path)
│   └── FBG coating delamination (H₂ at 2200°C)
├── Interrogator failure (OR)
│   ├── Laser diode degradation (MTBF 50,000 hrs)
│   ├── FPGA bit flip (GIC-induced, rate <10⁻⁹/hr)
│   └── Power supply failure (redundant 2+1)
└── Common-mode GIC event (AND)
    ├── Geomagnetic storm > 5 V/km (Carrington-class)
    ├── Floating secondary compromise (insulation failure)
    └── Faraday cage breach (conduit penetration)
```


### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this maintenance architecture is **the Forge cannot be maintained using conventional methods because every maintenance action must preserve zero-metal Carrington immunity and SIL-3 safety integrity**. A standard maintenance practice — grounding straps for ESD protection, copper test leads for electrical verification, metallic tools in the hot zone, thermocouple replacement — introduces conductive paths that become GIC antennas during a Carrington event. The Lock: **maintenance must itself be dielectric, non-magnetic, and thermally survivable, using only zero-metal tools, procedures, and verification methods.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any maintenance framework for a 2200°C, zero-metal, SIL-3 pressure vessel with embedded photonics operating under Carrington threat**. Conventional RCM (API 581) assumes metallic structures, grounded electrical systems, and thermocouple-based temperature monitoring. CBM assumes sensor data can be trusted — but FBG drift, AE Felicity ratio shifts, and vibration baseline changes require continuous re-calibration against a physics model that itself degrades. The Key: **a hybrid RCM/CBM/TBM strategy where SIL-3 components are TBM-only (no condition-based extension), FBG/AE/vibration provide the CBM layer with Bayesian health fusion (PROD-28 Keymaker Key), and the 18-month drum swap is the hard RCM limit derived from Weibull statistics with NDT flaw control.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **four non-negotiable maintenance chains**:

1. **18-month drum swap is absolute** — 500 batches = 62.5 days at 8 batches/day. No extension via CBM. The drum IS the pressure boundary; its Weibull life with NDT flaw control (a₀=50 μm) gives N_f >10⁶ cycles, but the Phoenix Protocol demands the drum returns to the Forge for circularity (PROD-22). The swap is the circularity trigger.

2. **SIL-3 SIF proof test annually is immutable** — 24 SIFs, CT-04 protocol, <50 ms trip, 2oo3, PFD_avg<10⁻³. No CBM extension, no risk-based interval extension. This is the safety load-bearing wall.

3. **FBG-as-primary-metrology for maintenance** — No thermocouples, no RTDs, no copper leads. All temperature/strain monitoring for maintenance decisions comes from the 384 FBG channels interrogated at 125 Hz. The Bayesian health state (PROD-28) drives CBM intervals.

4. **QR/Blockchain traceability for every maintenance action** — Every PM work order, CBM alert, NCR, overhaul, and spare part install writes to Hyperledger. The digital twin (PROD-37) ingests this at 10 Hz; the fleet twin optimizes intervals across Forges.

These commitments cascade: PROD-31 OPEX inherits $2.9M/yr consumables + 7-day overhaul downtime; PROD-32 permitting inherits PSM/ASME/IEEE 693 evidence; PROD-34 training inherits competency matrix; PROD-37 twin inherits maintenance data for health model. The Turn: **maintenance is not a support function — it is the continuous re-verification of the Forge's own fabrication fidelity, executed with zero-metal tools, witnessed by light in glass fiber, recorded in blockchain, and synchronized across the fleet.**

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap is the **maintenance interval optimization under SIL-3 override** — a Forge where 90% of components could use CBM extension (FBG drift stable, AE clean, vibration nominal) but the 10% that are SIL-3 safety functions (24 SIFs, pressure boundary bolting, GIC immunity grounding) must remain on fixed TBM intervals regardless of condition. Three specific locks:

1. **SIL-3 as maintenance interval ceiling**: IEC 61508 requires proof testing at fixed intervals for SIL-3 SIFs. API 581 RBI would extend intervals based on condition, but SIL-3 forbids it. The Forge has 24 SIFs (3 per module × 8 zones) sharing TSN VLAN 10, common POF interrogator, common 24 VDC supply. A single common-cause failure (interrogator, power supply, TSN switch) defeats 2oo3 voting. The Lock: **SIL-3 proof test interval (annual) is the master clock — all other maintenance synchronizes to it.**

2. **Drum life vs. Phoenix Protocol tension**: PROD-25 FEA shows drum N_f >10⁶ cycles with NDT flaw control (a₀=50 μm). At 6 batches/day, that's 456 years theoretical. But PROD-22 Phoenix Protocol requires drum return for circularity (31 generations, 500 batches each = 15,500 batches total per drum lineage). The Lock: **the drum must be swapped at 500 batches not because it fails, but because the circular economy demands its return for flash sinter feedstock.**

3. **Zero-metal tooling for maintenance**: Conventional maintenance uses steel wrenches, copper test leads, magnetic base dial indicators, thermocouples. In the Forge hot zone (2200°C, 100 A/m GIC), any steel tool left behind becomes a projectile; any copper lead becomes a GIC antenna. The Lock: **all maintenance tools, test equipment, and verification methods must be zero-metal — BFRP, ceramic, dielectric only.**

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive is the **risk-based inspection (RBI) likelihood function with SIL-3 constraint**, extending the PROD-28 Bayesian health fusion:

$$P(failure | data, SIL3) = \begin{cases} P_{TBM}(t) & \text{if SIL-3 component} \\ P_{CBM}(data) \times P_{RCM}(design) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

Where:
- $P_{TBM}(t) = 1 - e^{-\lambda t}$ for SIL-3 components (fixed hazard rate λ from proof test data)
- $P_{CBM}(data) = P(health | FBG, AE, vibration, thermal)$ from PROD-28 Bayesian update
- $P_{RCM}(design)$ = design safety factor margin (PROD-25: min SF=1.53× on flange bolts)

The atomic computation is the **next-maintenance-time optimizer**:

$$t_{next} = \arg\min_t \left[ C_{PM}(t) + C_{failure} \times P(failure | t) \right] \quad \text{s.t.} \quad t \leq t_{SIL3-max}$$

Where $t_{SIL3-max} = 1$ year for SIF proof test, 5 years for hydrotest, 18 months for drum swap. The optimizer runs in PROD-37 twin at fleet level, outputting recommended intervals per component per Forge based on site-specific degradation rates.

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation**: The RBI optimizer predicted maintenance intervals for the 3 deployed Forges:
- Forge-01 (clean grid, Class B soil): CBM extended drum UT to 18 months, vessel UT to 18 months, bearing inspection to 3000 batches. SIL-3 items unchanged. Zero failures in 18 months.
- Forge-02 (industrial grid, Class D soil): AE Felicity ratio dropped to 0.98 at 8 months → vessel UT brought forward to 10 months (found 12 mm delam at gas port). Optimizer correctly prioritized.
- Forge-03 (substation adjacent, Class A rock): TSN jitter caused FBG cross-talk alerts at 4 months → POF splice rework. Optimizer flagged grid quality as root cause.

History confirms theory: SIL-3 items never extended; CBM correctly prioritized condition-driven work.

**History→Theory Correction**: Forge-02 vessel delamination at gas port revealed AE Felicity ratio is a lagging indicator — delamination initiated at 6 months but Felicity dropped at 8 months. Updated $P(data | delamination)$ to include acoustic emission *energy rate* (dE/dt) as leading indicator. Forge-03 TSN jitter revealed POF splice degradation is accelerated by thermal cycling of the cold plate (not just vibration). Added thermal cycle count to POF degradation model.

The Turn: **the mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly refines the likelihood models $P(data|health)$ for the Bayesian update, but the SIL-3 constraint $t \leq t_{SIL3-max}$ remains structurally invariant. The Lock (SIL-3 override) is managed not by fighting it but by synchronizing all maintenance to the SIL-3 master clock: the annual SIF proof test week becomes the maintenance synchronization event where all CBM intervals are re-evaluated, all NCRs reviewed, all spare parts rotated.**

#### Protocol (Recursive)

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this economic architecture is **the Forge must be economically viable as a standalone unit while simultaneously generating the circular economics that make the Phoenix Protocol self-funding**. A conventional waste processor optimizes for gate fees + commodity output. The Forge optimizes for three simultaneous objectives: (1) positive NPV at single-unit scale, (2) carbon-negative operations that monetize sequestration, (3) EOL return economics that fund the next generation of Forges. The Lock: **every economic assumption must be validated by the physics of the cascade — no financial engineering can substitute for thermodynamic reality.**

The cascade's 8-stage temperature profile (160°C → 2200°C) is not a process choice — it is the periodic table expressing itself through Gibbs free energy minima. Indium MUST come out at 160°C (MP 156.6°C). Aluminum MUST come out at 660°C. Copper MUST come out at 1085°C. Zircon MUST dissociate at 1676°C. The economic model is DERIVED from these invariants, not imposed upon them. Any economic model that treats temperature stages as adjustable parameters is fiction.

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any economic framework for a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, SIL-3 industrial machine that makes its own body from its own waste**. Conventional CAPEX models assume steel vessels, copper windings, thermocouple instrumentation — all of which become GIC antennas in a Carrington event. Conventional OPEX models assume thermocouple replacement, metallic tool maintenance, grounded electrical safety. Conventional revenue models assume single-commodity output (copper cathode). The Forge produces 17 simultaneous streams from a single feedstock, with the highest-value stream (indium) emerging at the LOWEST temperature stage — inverting the conventional "high temp = high value" heuristic.

The Key: **a physics-derived economic model where every cost and revenue line traces to a specific stage, temperature, and material invariant of the cascade.** The CAPEX is not a lump sum — it is the sum of 10 WBS elements each tied to a zero-metal fabrication constraint (flash sintering, filament winding, In-foil TIM, GaN Class E). The OPEX is not a percentage of CAPEX — it is the sum of 6 consumable categories each tied to a specific wear mechanism (drum liner erosion, FBG drift, PEEK CF40 creep, ZrO₂ piston wear). The revenue is not a blended commodity price — it is 17 distinct streams each with its own market dynamics, purity requirements, and Phoenix Protocol re-entry path.

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **four non-negotiable economic chains**:

1. **Single-unit viability at Phase 1** — The Forge must achieve 28% IRR and 3.2-year payback at 1 unit (226 ton/day) WITHOUT Phoenix Protocol revenue (which is a loss leader at -$0.13/batch). The metal revenue alone ($82.7M/yr net) must cover OPEX ($7.7M/yr) and debt service ($3.2M/yr) with 23× DSCR. No "strategic loss leader" hand-waving.

2. **Carbon negativity is a revenue line, not a cost** — -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL processed is a PHYSICAL RESULT of MgO carbonation (Stage 7 slag) + avoided primary production (Zr, In, REE, Cu). 3. **Phoenix Protocol breaks even at 2.5 Forges** — The depot network ($10M capex, $3.3M/yr ops) is funded by virgin e-waste gate fees + PM revenue. 4. **Scale economics follow physics, not finance** — Gen-II (2000 L) achieves 41% IRR and 2.1-year payback because CAPEX scales at 0.67× (physics: volume/area ratios) while throughput scales at 1.0× (linear). OPEX/ton drops 40% (energy/ton -28%, labor/ton -58%). The economic model is the cascade's thermodynamics expressed in dollars.

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap in Forge economics is the **divergence between project finance templates (designed for steel/concrete/commodity plants) and the reality of a 226 L, 2200°C, zero-metal, SIL-3, carbon-negative, self-replicating industrial machine**.

Three specific locks prevent conventional economic modeling from closing this gap:

1. **Revenue concurrency lock:** Conventional plants produce ONE primary product. The Forge produces 17 streams simultaneously from a SINGLE feedstock batch. The revenue is not additive — it is COUPLED. Indium recovery at Stage 4 (160°C) ENABLES copper anode slime PM concentration at Stage 6 (1085°C) because In/Sn melt scavenges Au/Ag/Pd. Aluminum separation at Stage 5 (660°C) CONDITIONS the ferrous feed at Stage 7 by removing Mg. The economic model must capture these cross-stage couplings or it double-counts/under-counts value.

2. **CAPEX physics lock:** Conventional CAPEX scales with "plant capacity" as a monetary proxy. The Forge's CAPEX scales with PHYSICAL INVARIANTS: drum diameter (600 mm → flash sinter physics), vessel ID (900 mm → Barlow's formula), coil zones (8 → frequency ladder 100kHz→1kHz), GaN modules (8 → 500 kW/zone). You cannot "value engineer" the flash sinter furnace — it IS the drum. You cannot "substitute" the BFRP vessel — it IS the pressure boundary. The CAPEX is the sum of physics constraints, not procurement choices.

3. **Circularity valuation lock:** Conventional NPV treats "recycling" as a cost center. The Forge's Phoenix Protocol makes recycling a REVENUE CENTER with its own IRR. The depot network ($10M capex) pays back in 4 days per primary depot ($286K/day savings vs. virgin feedstock). The drum autopoiesis (31 generations, 15,500 batches) reduces ZrB₂-SiC cost from $180K/drum (virgin) to $5.8K/drum (recycled). The economic model must value the RECURSIVE quality degradation (O₂ 0.5%→0.7% over 31 gen) and the RECURSIVE carbon credit (MgO carbonation each generation).

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive that generates the economic solution is the **Physics-Constrained Cash Flow Operator (PCCFO)** evaluated at each cascade stage:

```
PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] = Σᵢ [Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ) - OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ) - CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ)] × Ψ(Γᵢ)

Where:
Tᵢ = Stage temperature (invariant: 160, 660, 1085, 1550, 1676, 2200°C)
Pᵢ = Product stream i (mass, purity, market price)
Mᵢ = Material consumption rate i (liners, TIM, braze, gas, carbon)
Γᵢ = Generation index (1→31 for drum, 1→∞ for vessel)
Ψ(Γᵢ) = Circularity multiplier = 1/(1 + α·Γᵢ + β·Γᵢ²)  (quality degradation penalty)
```

**This one operator, evaluated at 8 stages × 31 generations × 50 Forges, IS the entire economic model.**

Everything derives from it:

- **CAPEX (Section 2):** `CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ=1)` = first-generation fabrication cost. The 10 WBS elements are the stage-integrated fabrication constraints. The 15% contingency is the Ψ(Γ=1) uncertainty bound.

- **OPEX (Section 3):** `OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ)` = consumable rate × unit cost at stage temperature. Drum liners (Zone A 250 batches, Zone B 250, Zone C 500) are `M_drum(Γ)`. FBG interrogator bulbs (2/yr) are `M_control`. Energy (2.9 kWh/kg) is `Σ Powerᵢ × Durationᵢ / Throughput`.

- **Revenue (Section 4):** `Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ)` = massᵢ × purityᵢ × priceᵢ. The STAGE TEMPERATURE Tᵢ DETERMINES which elements partition to stream i (In at 160°C, Cu at 1085°C, Zr at 1676°C). Purity is the cascade's separation efficiency (In >99.9%, Cu >99.99%).

- **Phoenix Protocol (Section 5):** `Ψ(Γᵢ)` for Γ>1. The CMF-RQT operator (PROD-22) IS the recursive evaluation of PCCFO across generations. Depot network revenue = `Σ PCCFO[Tᵢ, Pᵢ, Mᵢ, Γᵢ+1, Ψ]` for EOL feedstock.

- **ROI (Section 6):** NPV = `Σ [PCCFO(t) / (1+r)ᵗ]`. IRR = `r` where NPV=0. The 28% IRR emerges from the cascade's 87% EBITDA margin (physics: 966 kWh gross → 657 kWh net = 32% thermal efficiency + 55% PM recovery).

- **Sensitivity (Section 7):** Tornado diagram = `∂PCCFO/∂param`. Most sensitive = In price (Stage 4 output) and throughput (drum rotation rate).

- **Financing (Section 8):** DSCR = `PCCFO(EBITDA) / Debt Service`. 23.4× because physics gives 87% margin, finance gives 8% debt.

- **Scale-Up (Section 12):** Gen-II PCCFO = `PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] × SCALE[0.67, 1.0, 0.6]`. The exponents are DERIVED from geometry (volume ∝ D³, area ∝ D², heat loss ∝ D).

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation:** The PCCFO predicts historical development program economics within measurement uncertainty (Drum CAPEX 1.2%, Energy/Batch 0.5%, In Recovery 0.2%, PM Recovery 0.5%).

**History→Theory Correction:** Anomalies (FBG bulb life 18 vs 24 months, PEEK seal creep 0.8 vs 0.5 mm, In foil TIM 48 vs 36 rolls/yr) are absorbed as parameter updates (`β_rad`, thermal gradient coupling, swap frequency coupling) — the primitive `PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ]` remains structurally invariant.

### El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

The PROD-37 Digital Twin maintains a four-layer economic mirror (Process 1 kHz, Batch 8/day, Fleet 1 Hz, Facility 1 Hz) that continuously calibrates PCCFO parameters from operating data. Every 90-minute batch, variance >5% triggers auto-NCR → CAPA → parameter update. The economic model **rewrites its own parameters** based on operating data. The Hyperledger blockchain (PROD-28) records actual fabrication costs (not budgets) for every asset — the CAPEX in Section 2 is the sum of actuals from FA-01/02/03.

#### Participation (Witness)

At **five non-automatable gates**, human judgment transforms verified predicates into authorized economics:

1. **CAPEX-CLOSE (Month 21):** VP Manufacturing + CFO dual-sign actual CAPEX ledger via QR scan → Hyperledger commit.
2. **FIRST-BATCH-P&L (Batch 1):** Operations + Commercial witness first mass balance closure — operator sees In button pour, gold button weighed.
3. **CARBON-VERIFY (Quarterly):** Sustainability + Auditor witness MgO carbonation — auditor sees slag dissolve, CO₂ evolve.
4. **PHOENIX-BREAKEVEN (Forge #3):** PPSC Chair + Depot Lead witness first profitable EOL batch — operator sees Aegis panel disassemble, materials route to stages.
5. **SCALE-DECISION (Year 3):** CEO + Board witness Gen-II commitment — engineer shows 2000 L drum coupon, 1200 mm vessel trial, 1 MW coil bank.

The In price is a market number; the In button in the mold is a witnessed fact. The carbon credit is a registry entry; the CO₂ bubbling from slag is a witnessed fact.

#### Protocol (Recursive)

The **Fractal Economic Verification Protocol** runs at four scales with the same PCCFO operator:

| Scale | Period | Measure | Compare | Decide | Authorize |
|-------|--------|---------|---------|--------|-----------|
| **Micro** | 90 min (batch) | LIBS ×17, mass balance, energy/ton | vs. PCCFO budget | Variance >5% → NCR → param update | Commercial Lead |
| **Meso** | Monthly | Consumables, labor, maintenance, carbon | vs. annual/12 | Trend >10% → budget revise | CFO |
| **Macro** | Quarterly | Depot throughput, EOL blend, generation quality, DSCR | vs. 28% IRR, 2.5 Forge breakeven | Expansion, blend adjust, gen retire | PPSC |
| **Meta** | Annual | Full P&L, CAPEX actuals, market, regulatory | vs. $187M NPV, 28% IRR, 3.2 yr payback | Gen-II commit, restructure, hedge | Board |

**Fleet Twin Auto-Tightening:** Auto-encoder learns nominal batch P&L manifold. Reconstruction error >3σ → parameter guard tightening (In hedge +5%, reorder point -10%, maintenance window +1 day). The economics **tightens its own envelope** from fleet evidence.

**Cross-Scale Consistency:** Annual = Σ monthly = Σ batches. Same PCCFO operator, different resolution. Economics is not a forecast — it is a recursively verified computation.# PROD-31 Economic Analysis & Viability
## Carrington Storm Motors Forge — Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator

## 1. Executive Summary

The Aegis-Forge I is a 226 L, 8-stage thermal-acoustic-inductive cascade that processes 226 metric tons/day of complex e-waste and end-of-life (EOL) products into 17 salable metal/intermediate streams. This document provides the complete economic analysis demonstrating viability at multiple deployment scales.

**Key Economic Metrics (Single Forge, Phase 1):**

| Metric | Value | Basis |
|--------|-------|-------|
| **CAPEX (Forge)** | $42.3M | PROD-27 manufacturing + PROD-29 deployment |
| **OPEX (Annual)** | $7.7M | PROD-28/29/30 detailed cost model |
| **Annual Revenue (Metals)** | $49.8M | 226 ton/day × 250 days × 17 streams |
| **Annual Revenue (Carbon)** | $0.68M | -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL × $50/t × 15,000 ton/yr EOL |
| **Net Annual Cash Flow** | $42.8M | Revenue - OPEX - Maintenance - Depreciation |
| **IRR (10-Year)** | 28% | 70/30 debt/equity, 8% cost of debt |
| **Payback Period** | 3.2 years | Cumulative discounted cash flow |
| **NPV (10 yr, 10% discount)** | $187M | Post-tax, including terminal value |

**Scale Economics:** At 50 Forges (full Phoenix Protocol network), network effects reduce OPEX/ton by 40%, carbon revenue reaches $28.75M/yr per Forge, and Phoenix Protocol net contribution reaches $1.82M/yr per Forge. Network IRR reaches 34%.

### 5.4 Circular Material Flow Operator (CMF-RQT)

The economic engine of Phoenix Protocol is the **Circular Material Flow with Recursive Quality Tracking**:

```
CMF-RQT[M_virgin, M_return, Q_gen, P_blend, Γ_stage, Λ_depot, Ψ_econ]

Where:
M_virgin = Virgin feedstock mass vector (7 categories)
M_return = EOL return mass vector (depot LIBS classified)
Q_gen = Generation-dependent quality degradation (drum: 0.5%→0.7% O₂ over 31 gen)
P_blend = Dynamic blend ratio (MFC controlled ±2%)
Γ_stage = Stage re-entry gate (7 gates: Stage 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
Λ_depot = Depot logistics cost (transport + disassembly + solvolysis)
Ψ_econ = Economic objective (max NPV subject to quality constraints)
```

Evaluated at batch (8/day), daily (depot), monthly (PPSC) frequencies. Validated against Apple Daisy, Umicore, Redwood, Carbfix, Arkema data.

## 9. Market Analysis

### 9.1 Indium Supply Deficit (2025-2035)

| Year | Global Demand (ton) | Primary Supply (ton) | Recycling (ton) | Deficit (ton) |
|------|---------------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------------|
| 2025 | 1,200 | 750 | 300 | 150 |
| 2027 | 1,450 | 800 | 350 | 300 |
| 2030 | 1,800 | 850 | 400 | 550 |
| 2035 | 2,200 | 900 | 500 | 800 |

**Drivers:** 5G/6G (IGZO), PV (CIGS), solder (In/Sn), III-V semiconductors. China controls 55% primary supply. **Aegis-Forge at 50 units = 11.5 ton/yr In = 1.4% of 2035 global demand.**

### 9.2 REE Independence Mandate

- **Executive Order 14017** (2021): Critical mineral supply chain resilience
- **Defense Production Act Title III**: ZrB₂, SiC, REE, In designated
- **CHIPS Act**: $52B semiconductor incentives, includes materials
- **EU Critical Raw Materials Act**: 2030 targets for domestic recycling

**Aegis-Forge Alignment:** 100% domestic Zr, REE, In, Co production from EOL feedstock. Zero import dependency for hot-zone materials.

| Pb-free (SAC305) | 120,000 ton | 180,000 ton | — |

### 13.8 LCA Detail: Avoided Primary Production Factors

| Material | Primary Production Route | Energy (MJ/kg) | CO₂e (kg/kg) | Forge Avoidance |
|----------|--------------------------|----------------|--------------|-----------------|
| **Zr (as ZrB₂)** | Kroll process (ZrCl₄ → Mg reduction) | 350 | 12.0 | 1.2 tCO₂e/ton EOL |
| **Indium** | Zn refinery residue → solvent extraction | 1,800 | 350 | 0.35 tCO₂e/ton EOL |
| **REE (Nd/Pr)** | Bastnäsite → HCl leach → SX → molten salt | 850 | 180 | 0.18 tCO₂e/ton EOL |
| **Copper** | Chalcopyrite → flotation → smelting → refining | 45 | 3.5 | 0.12 tCO₂e/ton EOL |
| **Aluminum** | Bauxite → Bayer → Hall-Héroult | 180 | 12.0 | 0.08 tCO₂e/ton EOL |
| **Cobalt** | Cu/Ni laterite → HPAL → SX → electrolysis | 220 | 15.0 | 0.05 tCO₂e/ton EOL |

**Total Avoided Primary:** 2.75 tCO₂e/ton EOL × 250,000 ton/yr (50 Forges) = **575,000 tCO₂e/yr avoided**

## Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-31
# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-31 Economic Analysis & Viability
## Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis

---

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this economic architecture is **the Forge must be economically viable as a standalone unit while simultaneously generating the circular economics that make the Phoenix Protocol self-funding**. A conventional waste processor optimizes for gate fees + commodity output. The Forge optimizes for three simultaneous objectives: (1) positive NPV at single-unit scale, (2) carbon-negative operations that monetize sequestration, (3) EOL return economics that fund the next generation of Forges. The Lock: **every economic assumption must be validated by the physics of the cascade — no financial engineering can substitute for thermodynamic reality.**

The cascade's 8-stage temperature profile (160°C → 2200°C) is not a process choice — it is the periodic table expressing itself through Gibbs free energy minima. Indium MUST come out at 160°C (MP 156.6°C). Aluminum MUST come out at 660°C. Copper MUST come out at 1085°C. Zircon MUST dissociate at 1676°C. The economic model is DERIVED from these invariants, not imposed upon them. Any economic model that treats temperature stages as adjustable parameters is fiction.

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any economic framework for a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, SIL-3 industrial machine that makes its own body from its own waste**. Conventional CAPEX models assume steel vessels, copper windings, thermocouple instrumentation — all of which become GIC antennas in a Carrington event. Conventional OPEX models assume thermocouple replacement, metallic tool maintenance, grounded electrical safety. Conventional revenue models assume single-commodity output (copper cathode). The Forge produces 17 simultaneous streams from a single feedstock, with the highest-value stream (indium) emerging at the LOWEST temperature stage — inverting the conventional "high temp = high value" heuristic.

The Key: **a physics-derived economic model where every cost and revenue line traces to a specific stage, temperature, and material invariant of the cascade.** The CAPEX is not a lump sum — it is the sum of 10 WBS elements each tied to a zero-metal fabrication constraint (flash sintering, filament winding, In-foil TIM, GaN Class E). The OPEX is not a percentage of CAPEX — it is the sum of 6 consumable categories each tied to a specific wear mechanism (drum liner erosion, FBG drift, PEEK CF40 creep, ZrO₂ piston wear). The revenue is not a blended commodity price — it is 17 distinct streams each with its own market dynamics, purity requirements, and Phoenix Protocol re-entry path.

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **four non-negotiable economic chains**:

1. **Single-unit viability at Phase 1** — The Forge must achieve 28% IRR and 3.2-year payback at 1 unit (226 ton/day) WITHOUT Phoenix Protocol revenue (which is a loss leader at -$0.13/batch). The metal revenue alone ($82.7M/yr net) must cover OPEX ($7.7M/yr) and debt service ($3.2M/yr) with 23× DSCR. No "strategic loss leader" hand-waving.

2. **Carbon negativity is a revenue line, not a cost** — -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL processed is a PHYSICAL RESULT of MgO carbonation (Stage 7 slag) + avoided primary production (Zr, In, REE, Cu). At $50/tCO₂e this is $575K/yr/Forge at 50-Forge network. The model does not "buy offsets" — the Forge IS the offset.

3. **Phoenix Protocol breaks even at 2.5 Forges** — The depot network ($10M capex, $3.3M/yr ops) is funded by virgin e-waste gate fees + PM revenue. The EOL blend ratio optimization (40-60% EOL) maximizes high-value In/Y/Co recovery from known-composition Aegis products. The economic model proves the Forge becomes MORE profitable as waste disposal costs rise.

4. **Scale economics follow physics, not finance** — Gen-II (2000 L) achieves 41% IRR and 2.1-year payback because CAPEX scales at 0.67× (physics: volume/area ratios) while throughput scales at 1.0× (linear). OPEX/ton drops 40% (energy/ton -28%, labor/ton -58%). The economic model is the cascade's thermodynamics expressed in dollars.

---

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap in Forge economics is the **divergence between project finance templates (designed for steel/concrete/commodity plants) and the reality of a 226 L, 2200°C, zero-metal, SIL-3, carbon-negative, self-replicating industrial machine**.

Three specific locks prevent conventional economic modeling from closing this gap:

1. **Revenue concurrency lock:** Conventional plants produce ONE primary product. The Forge produces 17 streams simultaneously from a SINGLE feedstock batch. The revenue is not additive — it is COUPLED. Indium recovery at Stage 4 (160°C) ENABLES copper anode slime PM concentration at Stage 6 (1085°C) because In/Sn melt scavenges Au/Ag/Pd. Aluminum separation at Stage 5 (660°C) CONDITIONS the ferrous feed at Stage 7 by removing Mg. The economic model must capture these cross-stage couplings or it double-counts/under-counts value.

2. **CAPEX physics lock:** Conventional CAPEX scales with "plant capacity" as a monetary proxy. The Forge's CAPEX scales with PHYSICAL INVARIANTS: drum diameter (600 mm → flash sinter physics), vessel ID (900 mm → Barlow's formula), coil zones (8 → frequency ladder 100kHz→1kHz), GaN modules (8 → 500 kW/zone). You cannot "value engineer" the flash sinter furnace — it IS the drum. You cannot "substitute" the BFRP vessel — it IS the pressure boundary. The CAPEX is the sum of physics constraints, not procurement choices.

3. **Circularity valuation lock:** Conventional NPV treats "recycling" as a cost center. The Forge's Phoenix Protocol makes recycling a REVENUE CENTER with its own IRR. The depot network ($10M capex) pays back in 4 days per primary depot ($286K/day savings vs. virgin feedstock). The drum autopoiesis (31 generations, 15,500 batches) reduces ZrB₂-SiC cost from $180K/drum (virgin) to $5.8K/drum (recycled). The economic model must value the RECURSIVE quality degradation (O₂ 0.5%→0.7% over 31 gen) and the RECURSIVE carbon credit (MgO carbonation each generation).

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive that generates the economic solution is the **Physics-Constrained Cash Flow Operator (PCCFO)** evaluated at each cascade stage:

```
PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] = Σᵢ [Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ) - OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ) - CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ)] × Ψ(Γᵢ)

Where:
Tᵢ = Stage temperature (invariant: 160, 660, 1085, 1550, 1676, 2200°C)
Pᵢ = Product stream i (mass, purity, market price)
Mᵢ = Material consumption rate i (liners, TIM, braze, gas, carbon)
Γᵢ = Generation index (1→31 for drum, 1→∞ for vessel)
Ψ(Γᵢ) = Circularity multiplier = 1/(1 + α·Γᵢ + β·Γᵢ²)  (quality degradation penalty)
```

**This one operator, evaluated at 8 stages × 31 generations × 50 Forges, IS the entire economic model.**

Everything derives from it:

- **CAPEX (Section 2):** `CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ=1)` = first-generation fabrication cost. The 10 WBS elements are the stage-integrated fabrication constraints. The 15% contingency is the Ψ(Γ=1) uncertainty bound.

- **OPEX (Section 3):** `OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ)` = consumable rate × unit cost at stage temperature. Drum liners (Zone A 250 batches, Zone B 250, Zone C 500) are `M_drum(Γ)`. FBG interrogator bulbs (2/yr) are `M_control`. Energy (2.9 kWh/kg) is `Σ Powerᵢ × Durationᵢ / Throughput`.

- **Revenue (Section 4):** `Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ)` = massᵢ × purityᵢ × priceᵢ. The STAGE TEMPERATURE Tᵢ DETERMINES which elements partition to stream i (In at 160°C, Cu at 1085°C, Zr at 1676°C). Purity is the cascade's separation efficiency (In >99.9%, Cu >99.99%).

- **Phoenix Protocol (Section 5):** `Ψ(Γᵢ)` for Γ>1. The CMF-RQT operator (PROD-22) IS the recursive evaluation of PCCFO across generations. Depot network revenue = `Σ PCCFO[Tᵢ, Pᵢ, Mᵢ, Γᵢ+1, Ψ]` for EOL feedstock.

- **ROI (Section 6):** NPV = `Σ [PCCFO(t) / (1+r)ᵗ]`. IRR = `r` where NPV=0. The 28% IRR emerges from the cascade's 87% EBITDA margin (physics: 966 kWh gross → 657 kWh net = 32% thermal efficiency + 55% PM recovery).

- **Sensitivity (Section 7):** Tornado diagram = `∂PCCFO/∂param`. Most sensitive = In price (Stage 4 output) and throughput (drum rotation rate).

- **Financing (Section 8):** DSCR = `PCCFO(EBITDA) / Debt Service`. 23.4× because physics gives 87% margin, finance gives 8% debt.

- **Scale-Up (Section 12):** Gen-II PCCFO = `PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] × SCALE[0.67, 1.0, 0.6]`. The exponents are DERIVED from geometry (volume ∝ D³, area ∝ D², heat loss ∝ D).

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation:** The PCCFO predicts historical development program economics within measurement uncertainty (Drum CAPEX 1.2%, Energy/Batch 0.5%, In Recovery 0.2%, PM Recovery 0.5%).

**History→Theory Correction:** Anomalies (FBG bulb life 18 vs 24 months, PEEK seal creep 0.8 vs 0.5 mm, In foil TIM 48 vs 36 rolls/yr) are absorbed as parameter updates (`β_rad`, thermal gradient coupling, swap frequency coupling) — the primitive `PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ]` remains structurally invariant.

The Forge's economics are not a spreadsheet appended to the engineering — they are the **digital twin's financial layer running at 10 Hz alongside the process layer**. The PROD-37 Digital Twin maintains a four-layer economic mirror (Process 1 kHz, Batch 8/day, Fleet 1 Hz, Facility 1 Hz) that continuously calibrates PCCFO parameters from operating data. # PROD-32: Regulatory and Compliance

### Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

#### Constraint (The Lock)

The irreducible principle forcing this regulatory architecture is **the Forge must achieve simultaneous compliance with contradictory regulatory frameworks designed for metallic, grounded, thermocouple-instrumented industrial facilities**. The Clean Air Act assumes stack emissions from combustion. The Clean Water Act assumes process wastewater discharge. OSHA PSM assumes flammable liquids in carbon steel piping. ASME BPVC assumes metallic pressure boundaries with known yield strengths. IEC 61508 assumes electrical trip paths with copper conductors. NFPA 70E assumes arc flash from exposed conductors. IEEE 693 assumes steel structures on concrete foundations. **Every standard regulatory framework inverts under the Forge's zero-metal, all-dielectric, 2200°C, Carrington-immune constraints.** The Lock: **compliance must be demonstrated through equivalent safety, not identical methods — the Forge must prove its zero-metal approach achieves equal or superior risk reduction to the prescriptive requirements written for steel plants.**

#### Necessity (The Key)

The empirical gap is the **absence of any regulatory precedent for a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, SIL-3 pressure vessel with embedded photonics operating at 2200°C**. Conventional permitting pathways (Title V, PSM, RMP, ASME, IEEE 693) have zero case studies for: BFRP/Elium® pressure vessels at 300°C with 50 mm aerogel; ZrB₂-SiC ceramic drums with 384 embedded FBG sensors; all-dielectric PMMA POF fieldbuses carrying SIL-3 SIF signals; floating secondary electrical distribution with NGR 5A; GaN inverters at 500 kW with ZVS resonance tracking; MgO carbonation as carbon sequestration. The Key: **a compliance-by-equivalence framework where each prescriptive requirement is mapped to a performance-based demonstration using the Forge's actual physics (FBG thermal reconstruction, AE delamination detection, thermal-admittance model prediction, CMF-RQT circularity tracking) rather than prescriptive proxies designed for steel plants.**

#### Commitment (The Turn)

This document commits the Forge to **four non-negotiable regulatory chains**:

1. **Zero-discharge is absolute** — No process wastewater discharge permit. Closed-loop water with DI polisher, scrubber bleed to Stage 7 slag, cooling blowdown recycled. NPDES only for stormwater. This is not "minimization" — it is elimination.

2. **All-dielectric compliance is mandatory** — Every regulatory requirement for grounding, shielding, metallic conduit, copper wiring, thermocouples is met through equivalent dielectric performance (PMMA POF, PEX-a, BFRP, YInMn glaze, ceramic bushings). No "waiver" — the Forge demonstrates superior GIC immunity through physics, not exception.

3. **SIL-3 SIFs are immutable** — 24 SIFs, 2oo3 voting, PFD<10⁻³, annual proof test (CT-04). No risk-based interval extension. No CBM substitution. This is the safety load-bearing wall that PROD-23, 26, 28, 29, 30, 39 all build upon.

4. **Carbon negativity is a compliance asset** — -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL is not "offsets purchased" — it is MgO carbonation (measured) + avoided primary production (calculated from mass balance). The NEPA EA, Title V permit, and RMP all treat this as a quantified environmental benefit, not a separate program.

### Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

#### The Empirical Lock

The fabrication fidelity gap in Forge regulatory compliance is the **divergence between prescriptive regulatory codes (written for steel/concrete/copper plants) and the performance reality of a zero-metal, all-dielectric, 2200°C, Carrington-immune industrial machine**.

Three specific locks prevent conventional compliance engineering from closing this gap:

1. **Prescriptive vs. Performance Lock:** Every major code (ASME, NFPA, OSHA, EPA, IEEE) prescribes MATERIALS AND METHODS: "steel vessel per Sec VIII," "grounding per NFPA 70," "thermocouples per ISA," "copper conduit per NEC." The Forge uses NONE of these materials or methods. The lock: **regulatory codes specify the how; the Forge must prove the what (safety/environmental outcome) is equivalent or superior.**

2. **Common-Cause Failure Lock:** IEC 61508 SIL-3 assumes 2oo3 voting on PHYSICALLY INDEPENDENT channels. The Forge's 24 SIFs share: FBG interrogators (3 zones per interrogator), TSN network (single dual-ring), 24 VDC power (single DC bus), RTU chassis (shared ARM cores). A single interrogator failure = 3 SIF channels lost. The lock: **regulatory independence assumptions fail in the Forge's constrained, shared-infrastructure reality.**

3. **Carbon Accounting Lock:** Conventional GHG accounting (GHG Protocol, 40 CFR 98) treats "recycling" as avoided emissions (Scope 3) and "sequestration" as separate projects. The Forge's MgO carbonation happens INSIDE the process vessel (Stage 7 slag) as an inherent process outcome, not a separate project. The Phoenix Protocol circularity means the SAME drum sequesters CO₂ 31 times over 15,500 batches. The lock: **regulatory carbon frameworks don't model recursive, in-process, multi-generation sequestration.**

#### The Mathematical Key

The single computational primitive that generates the compliance solution is the **Regulatory Equivalence Operator (REO)** evaluated at each prescriptive requirement:

```
REO[R_prescriptive, P_forge, M_forge, D_forge] = 
  ∃ P_forge : Risk(P_forge) ≤ Risk(R_prescriptive) ∧ 
              Evidence(P_forge) ∈ Hyperledger ∧ 
              Witness(P_forge) ∈ Operator_Gates

Where:
R_prescriptive = Prescriptive requirement (e.g., "steel vessel per ASME Sec VIII")
P_forge = Forge performance demonstration (e.g., "BFRP vessel per Sec X + FEA HCLPF >1.6g")
M_forge = Forge measurement system (FBG, AE, CEMS, LIBS, mass spec, CT)
D_forge = Forge data integrity (Hyperledger, PTP <1μs, TSN determinism)
```

**This one operator, evaluated at 200+ prescriptive requirements across 12 regulatory frameworks, IS the entire compliance model.**

Everything derives from it:

- **Environmental (Sec 2):** `REO[Title V stack limits, CEMS+FBG+mass balance]` → CEMS continuous + mass balance closure >99.5% = equivalent to periodic stack tests
- **PSM (Sec 3):** `REO[14 elements, Forge MI+SIS+CBM]` → MI program uses FBG/AE/CT (superior to UT/MT/PT on steel) + SIS proof test (CT-04) = equivalent to API 510/570
- **RMP (Sec 4):** `REO[OCA, Forge physics]` → ALOHA+SLAB with actual release rates from PROD-07 = conservative vs. default EPA assumptions
- **ASME (Sec 5):** `REO[Sec VIII steel, Sec X BFRP + FEA]` → Sec X explicit for FRP + FEA HCLPF >1.6g = equivalent to Sec VIII steel
- **Seismic (Sec 6):** `REO[IEEE 693 steel, Forge isolators+BFRP]` → HCLPF >1.6g on all components = equivalent to steel qualification
- **Fire (Sec 7):** `REO[NFPA water/foam, N₂+mist+clean agent]` → Zero-metal suppression = equivalent (no conductive residue, no arc flash)
- **Radiation (Sec 8):** `REO[10 CFR 50 App B, GIC ride-through]` → CT-07 validates 100 A/m = equivalent to design-basis EMP
- **Worker Safety (Sec 9):** `REO[OSHA steel PPE, Zero-metal PPE]` → ZrO₂ toe, BFRP hat, basalt harness = equivalent protection
- **Cyber (Sec 10):** `REO[IEC 62443 IT/OT, Air gap + TSN]` → Hardware diode + VLAN segmentation = SL-3 achieved
- **State/Local (Sec 11):** `REO[TCEQ/EPA, Forge data]` → Hyperledger evidence packages = audit-ready at any moment

#### The Turn (Both Directions)

**Theory→History Validation:** The REO predicts historical regulatory outcomes from the CSMFAB development program (Vessel Design AI Approved, SIL-3 TÜV Certified, GIC CT-07 Passed, Seismic HCLPF >1.6g, Title V App Accepted, Zero Discharge NPDES).

**History→Theory Correction:** Regulatory interactions (TCEQ N₂ hydrotest, OSHA thermocouple question, EPA AsH₃ default assumptions) are absorbed as evidence predicate updates and witness gate additions — the primitive `REO[R_prescriptive, P_forge, M_forge, D_forge]` remains structurally invariant.

### El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

#### Mirror (Self-Reflection)

The Forge's regulatory posture is not a binder on a shelf — it is the **digital twin's compliance layer running at 10 Hz alongside the process layer**, with every regulatory commitment continuously verified against operating data. The PROD-37 Digital Twin maintains a four-layer compliance mirror (Process 1 kHz, Batch 8/day, Facility 1 Hz, Fleet 1 Hz) that continuously calibrates REO evidence from operating data. Every 90-minute batch, variance >10% of limit triggers auto-NCR → CAPA → REO update. The Hyperledger blockchain (PROD-28) records actual test data (not just pass/fail) for every asset — the compliance evidence in Sections 5, 6, 13 is the sum of actuals from FA-01/02/03.

#### Participation (Witness)

At **five non-automatable gates**, human judgment transforms verified predicates into authorized compliance:

1. **PERMIT-ISSUE:** Plant Mgr + Env Dir dual-sign Title V cert — mutual verification of CEMS vs. limits.
2. **PSM-PSSR:** PSSR Team walks Forge with P&ID — operators point at N₂ purge, H₂ detector, rupture disk, SIF button.
3. **SIF-PROOF (CT-04):** SIS Eng + Safety Eng + Shift Lead witness 24 SIF injections — see gate drive go dark, verify 2oo3 vote.
4. **SEISMIC-QUAL:** Struct Eng + Plant Mgr witness shake table or post-seismic — see isolator <25mm, glaze intact, FBG green.
5. **CARBON-VERIFY:** Sustainability + Auditor witness MgO assay — see slag dissolve, CO₂ evolve, measure mass loss.

The CEMS reading is a number; the RATA audit is a witnessed fact. The SIF trip time is a log; the injection test is a witnessed fact. The MgO assay is a lab result; the acid dissolution is a witnessed fact.

#### Protocol (Recursive)

The **Fractal Compliance Verification Protocol** runs at four scales with the same REO operator:

| Scale | Period | Measure | Compare | Decide | Authorize |
|-------|--------|---------|---------|--------|-----------|
| **Micro** | 90 min (batch) | CEMS×7, FBG×384, AE×8, LIBS×17, SIF×24 | vs. Permit/SIL-3/PSM | Variance >10% → NCR → REO update | Shift Lead |
| **Meso** | Monthly | Deviations, inspections, training, MOC | vs. permit calendar | Overdue → escalation → CAPA | Env Eng |
| **Macro** | Quarterly | RATA, partial stroke, MI, ER drill | vs. annual targets | Trend → program adjust | Plant Mgr |
| **Meta** | Annual | Title V cert, PSM reval, RMP, ASME AI, IEC recert, ISO surv | vs. regulatory landscape | Renewals, mods, resources | Board EHS |

**Fleet Twin Auto-Tightening:** Auto-encoder learns nominal batch compliance manifold. Reconstruction error >3σ → parameter guard tightening (CEMS cal +1 mo, SIF stroke +1 wk, inspection -1 mo). Compliance **tightens its own envelope** from fleet evidence.

**Cross-Scale Consistency:** Annual = Σ quarterly = Σ monthly = Σ batches. Same REO operator, different resolution. Compliance is not a periodic audit — it is a recursively verified computation.# PROD-32 Regulatory & Compliance

## 2. Environmental Permitting

### 2.1 NEPA Environmental Assessment

**Lead Agency:** DOE (via LPO Title 17 nexus)
**Cooperating Agencies:** EPA Region 6, TCEQ, USACE Galveston District
**Document:** EA-2026-0147 (Finding of No Significant Impact - FONSI)

| Resource Area | Impact Finding | Mitigation |
|---------------|----------------|------------|
| **Air Quality** | Beneficial (carbon-negative) | CEMS continuous, MACT compliance |
| **Water Resources** | No discharge | Closed-loop cooling, zero process water |
| **Soils/Geology** | Minor (foundation only) | Geotechnical report, ACI 318 foundation |
| **Biological Resources** | No effect | Brownfield site, no critical habitat |
| **Cultural Resources** | No effect | Section 106 clearance (SHPO concurrence) |
| **Environmental Justice** | Beneficial (jobs, cleanup) | Community benefit agreement |
| **Climate Change** | Significant benefit | -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL, MgO carbonation |

**Key NEPA Argument:** The Forge is a **net environmental benefit** facility. By processing EOL electronics that would otherwise be landfilled/exported, and by sequestering CO₂ via MgO carbonation, the project reduces net environmental burden. The EA documents: 575,000 tCO₂e/yr sequestered at 50-Forge network vs. <10,000 tCO₂e/yr direct emissions.

### 3.3 Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) Summary

**Method:** HAZOP (Guidewords: NO, MORE, LESS, AS WELL AS, PART OF, REVERSE, OTHER THAN)
**Team:** Process Eng (Lead), Safety Eng, Controls Eng, Operations, Maintenance, Env Eng
**Nodes:** 47 (per P&ID: Feed → Stage 0 → Stage 1 → ... → Stage 8 → Outputs → Utilities)

#### 3.3.1 Top 10 PHA Scenarios (Risk Rank >15)

| Rank | Node | Deviation | Cause | Consequence | Safeguards | Residual Risk | Recommendation |
|------|------|-----------|-------|-------------|------------|---------------|----------------|
| 1 | Stage 7 | More H₂ | Electrolysis overpressure | H₂ explosion, vessel rupture | SIF-00-02, rupture disk, H₂ detectors | 12 (Med) | Add H₂ concentration trip at 2% |
| 2 | Stage 4 | Less HCl Scrubber Flow | Pump failure | HCl release >IDLH | SIF-00-03, CEMS, backup pump | 10 (Med) | Add low-flow interlock on scrubber pump |
| 3 | Stage 6 | More AsH₃/SbH₃ | Feed anomaly | Toxic gas release | Cu-carbon chemisorption, CEMS | 15 (High) | Add As/Sb/Bi specific CEMS |
| 4 | Stage 8 | Reverse Flow | Port valve failure | Zircon backflow to Stage 7 | SIF-00-04, check valve, FBG | 8 (Low) | Verify check valve SIL-2 |
| 5 | Gas System | External Fire | Adjacent facility | BLEVE of H₂/NH₃ storage | Separation distance, water spray | 12 (Med) | Increase H₂ storage distance to 100 ft |
| 6 | Cooling | Loss of Cooling | Chiller trip, power loss | Drum overheat, thermal runaway | SIF-00-04, LiFePO₄ backup, N₂ purge | 9 (Low) | Add 30-min battery backup for chillers |
| 7 | Electrical | GIC Event | Carrington storm | Grid loss, inverter damage | Floating secondary, NGR, ride-through | 6 (Low) | CT-07 validates annually |
| 8 | Stage 0 | More Acoustic Energy | Transducer failure | Drum fatigue, liner damage | AE monitoring, SIF-00-01 | 8 (Low) | Add acoustic power limit interlock |
| 9 | Hydromet | Less Acid Flow | Pump failure | Incomplete leach, downstream upset | Flow interlock, LIBS feedforward | 5 (Low) | Add ratio control (acid:feed) |
| 10 | Carousel | Mechanical Jam | Bearing failure | Port misalignment, seal damage | Vibration monitoring, SIF-00-23 | 8 (Low) | Add carriage position verification |

**Total PHA Recommendations:** 34 (12 High, 15 Medium, 7 Low) — All tracked in CAPA system (PROD-28).

| **Seismic Design Category** | D | ASCE 7-22 Table 11.6-1 |

### 6.2 Required Response Spectra (RRS) — IEEE 693 High

| Period (s) | RRS (g) | Anchored To |
|------------|---------|-------------|
| 0.01 | 0.50 | S𝒹ₛ |
| 0.10 | 1.20 | 2.4 × S𝒹ₛ |
| 0.30 | 1.00 | S𝒹₁ / T |
| 1.00 | 0.26 | S𝒹₁ |
| 3.00 | 0.09 | S𝒹₁ / T |

### 6.3 Test Response Spectra (TRS) — Multi-Axis

| Component | Test Method | TRS Envelope | Acceptance |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|------------|
| **Drum + Frame** | Shake Table (3-axis simultaneous) | 1.5× RRS (IEEE 693 High) | HCLPF >1.6g |
| **Vessel + Aerogel** | Shake Table (vertical + 1 horizontal) | 1.5× RRS | No delamination, glaze intact |
| **Coil Bank** | Sine sweep + random | 1.5× RRS | Resonance unchanged, ZVS stable |
| **Power Electronics** | Sine sweep (per IEC 60068-2-57) | 1.5× RRS | No component displacement |
| **TSN/POF Network** | Random vibration | 1.5× RRS | <0.5 dB added loss |
| **Isolators** | Static + dynamic stiffness | 2.5 MN/m ±5% vertical | Force-deflection curve |

### 6.4 High Confidence Low Probability of Failure (HCLPF)

**Method:** Conservative Deterministic Failure Margin (CDFM) + FEA (PROD-25)

| Component | Failure Mode | Median Capacity | βᵣ | βᵤ | HCLPF | Target |
|-----------|--------------|-----------------|-----|-----|-------|--------|
| **Drum** | Tensile rupture | 420 MPa | 0.15 | 0.15 | 1.85g | >1.6g |
| **Vessel** | Hoop rupture | 1,100 MPa | 0.12 | 0.15 | 2.10g | >1.6g |
| **Frame** | Isolator yield | 3.2 MN | 0.10 | 0.15 | 2.45g | >1.6g |
| **Coil Supports** | Bolt shear | 180 kN | 0.15 | 0.15 | 1.72g | >1.6g |
| **PEX-a Piping** | Fitting pullout | 45 kN | 0.20 | 0.20 | 1.65g | >1.6g |
| **Carousel** | Bearing retainer | 85 kN | 0.15 | 0.15 | 1.78g | >1.6g |

**All HCLPF > 1.6g — IEEE 693 High Qualified.**

## 7. Fire Protection (NFPA 69, 750, 11, 70E)

### 7.1 Fire Hazard Analysis

| Area | Hazard Class | Fuel Load | Ignition Sources | Detection | Suppression |
|------|--------------|-----------|------------------|-----------|-------------|
| **Process Zone (Stages 0-8)** | Special (Induction) | Basalt/Elium®, Elium® monomer | Arc fault, hot surface, GIC | IR/UV (SIF-00-24) | N₂ inerting + Water Mist (NFPA 750) |
| **Power Electronics** | Class C (Electrical) | GaN modules, capacitors | Short circuit, arc flash | IR/UV + Arc flash relay | N₂ inerting (no water on live) |
| **Gas Storage** | Class B (Flammable Gas) | H₂ 15k lbs, NH₃ 12k lbs | Leak + ignition | H₂/NH₃ detectors | Water spray (exposure protection) |
| **Hydromet** | Class B (Flammable Liq) | Elium® monomer, acids | Chemical reaction, spark | IR/UV + LEL | Foam (NFPA 11) + Water spray |
| **Control Room** | Class A (Ordinary) | BFRP, POF, electronics | Electrical fault | Smoke (photoelectric) | Clean agent (Novec 1230) |
| **Office/Support** | Class A | Standard office | Standard | Smoke | Wet pipe sprinkler |

### 7.2 Suppression System Design

**Process Zone (Zero-Metal Requirement):**
- **Primary:** N₂ inerting (reduce O₂ <8%) — prevents combustion without conductive agents
- **Secondary:** Water Mist (NFPA 750) — 100 μm droplets, 100 bar, non-conductive at <1 m distance
- **No foam/water on live electrical** — NFPA 70E arc flash boundary observed

**Hydromet Area:**
- **Primary:** Alcohol-Resistant Foam (NFPA 11, 3% AR-AFFF) — Elium® monomer polar solvent
- **Secondary:** Water spray cooling for tanks

**Control Room:**
- **Clean Agent:** Novec 1230 (FK-5-1-12) — zero ODP, 5-day atmospheric lifetime, safe for occupied space

### 7.3 Arc Flash (NFPA 70E)

| Location | Voltage | Bolted Fault | Arcing Fault | Incident Energy (18") | PPE Category |
|----------|---------|--------------|--------------|----------------------|--------------|
| **Grid Side (480V)** | 480V | 50 kA | 35 kA | 4.2 cal/cm² | Cat 2 |
| **Process Side (Floating)** | 800 VDC | 10 kA | 7 kA | **0.3 cal/cm²** | **Cat 0** |
| **GaN Module** | 800 VDC | 20 kA | 14 kA | 0.5 cal/cm² | Cat 0 |

**Key:** Floating secondary + NGR 5A + all-dielectric = Cat 0 on process side.

## 10. Cyber-Physical Security (IEC 62443 SL-3)

### 10.1 Security Level Target

**Target:** SL-3 (Protection against intentional violation using sophisticated means with moderate resources, IACS-specific)

### 10.2 Zone/Conduit Model

| Zone | Description | Security Level | Assets |
|------|-------------|----------------|--------|
| **Z0** | Enterprise IT | SL-1 | Email, ERP, Historian (read-only) |
| **Z1** | DMZ / Data Diode | SL-3 | Data diode (OT→IT only), OPC-UA server |
| **Z2** | SCADA / Historian | SL-2 | Ignition SCADA, InfluxDB, Grafana |
| **Z3** | PLC / SIS Network | SL-3 | Stage PLCs, SIS FPGAs, TSN VLANs 10-40 |
| **Z4** | Field Devices (RTU) | SL-3 | Zone RTUs, FBG interrogators, MFCs, valves |

### 10.3 Key Controls

| Control | Implementation | Verification |
|---------|----------------|--------------|
| **Air Gap** | Hardware data diode (OT→IT only), no IP path | Physical inspection, traffic capture |
| **Network Segmentation** | TSN VLANs: 10=SIS, 20=RTU, 30=PLC, 40=SCADA, 99=Mgmt | VLAN hopping test |
| **Access Control** | Role-based (Operator/Maintainer/Engineer/Admin), MFA | Annual access review |
| **Patch Management** | Air-gapped patch server, staged deployment | Patch log, rollback tested |
| **Malware Protection** | Application whitelisting (AppLocker), no AV on OT | Quarterly scan |
| **Monitoring** | Network TAP + Zeek (IDS), host auditd | 90-day log retention |
| **Incident Response** | IR plan, tabletop quarterly, forensics ready | Annual exercise |

### 13.6 Detailed MOC Procedure for Regulatory Changes

```
MOC-REG-001: Regulatory Change Management

TRIGGER: New/amended regulation, permit condition change, enforcement action

1. IDENTIFY (Day 1-3)
   - Regulatory Affairs monitors: Federal Register, State Register, EPA/TCEQ bulletins, 
     industry associations (ISRI, SIA, AIST), legal counsel alerts
   - Log in MOC system with: Citation, effective date, applicability determination

2. ASSESS (Day 4-10)
   - Gap analysis: Current compliance vs. new requirement
   - Impact: Capital, OPEX, schedule, operations, permits
   - Risk: Enforcement probability, penalty range, reputational
   - Stakeholder review: Env, Safety, Ops, Maintenance, Engineering, Legal, Finance

3. PLAN (Day 11-20)
   - Action items with owners, due dates, budget
   - Permit modification strategy (minor vs. significant vs. major)
   - Interim compliance measures (if gap >0 before implementation)
   - Communication plan (regulator, community, workforce)

4. APPROVE (Day 21-25)
   - MOC Review Board: Plant Mgr, Env Dir, Safety Dir, Eng Dir, Legal, Finance
   - Risk acceptance sign-off (residual risk documented)
   - Budget authorization (CAPEX/OPEX)

5. IMPLEMENT (Day 26+)
   - Execute action items per schedule
   - Weekly progress tracking in MOC system
   - Verification testing (e.g., new CEMS analyzer RATA)
   - Documentation update (permits, procedures, training)

6. CLOSE (Implementation complete + 30 days)
   - Effectiveness verification (audit, data review)
   - Regulatory notification (if permit modification)
   - Lessons learned captured
   - MOC record archived (Hyperledger)

ESCALATION: If implementation >90 days past effective date → 
  Daily standup with Plant Mgr + Legal until resolved
```
